title: StateGuard denies every build option: minerals_remaining is a shortfall, not a budget
description:
StateGuard treats minerals_remaining as a spendable budget. It is a SHORTFALL. So on any base that has accumulated minerals toward its current item, the guard denies EVERY option and base.production degrades to the deterministic tier - including, and especially, the correct choice.

MEASURED END TO END on a live game, turn 42, Morgan Solutions (Morganites):

  base_state: current Colony Pod, minerals_accumulated 27, cost 33, mineral_surplus 7
  metrics:    minerals_remaining 6
  action_space (every entry): effects {"minerals_remaining": -<full item cost>}
      unit:0   Colony Pod           cost 33  turns_if_switched 5  turns_if_continued 1
      unit:1   Formers              cost 22  turns_if_switched 4
      unit:2   Scout Patrol         cost 11  turns_if_switched 2
      unit:256 Synthmetal Garrison  cost 22  ...  (and four facilities at 44-220)

  agent chose unit:0 - the item already in production, 27/33 banked, ONE TURN from completion
  guard advisory: "unit:0 spends 33 minerals_remaining but only 6 is available - the state moved since this was offered"
  submit result:  degraded=true, degrade_reason="guard denied every choice (1 stripped); 1 repair attempt(s) also failed"
  adapter row:    tier=llm, applied=llm_degraded, applied_item_name=Colony Pod

THE CATEGORY ERROR, from both ends:
  - metrics.py:134-139 defines minerals_remaining as "Minerals still needed to finish what this base is building", direction "lower is better".
  - thinker neural.cpp:559-562 emits it as (total_cost - minerals_accumulated), clamped at 0. A shortfall.
  - thinker neural.cpp:351 declares every action's effects as {"minerals_remaining": -cost}, the FULL item cost.
  - hank.py StateGuard then reads "spends 33, only 6 available" and denies.

Nothing here is a state race, so the advisory's "the state moved since this was offered" is also wrong and actively misleading - it sends the reader looking for a concurrency bug that does not exist.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY FALSE POSITIVE:
  1. It denies the ENTIRE action space, not one option. Every item costs more than the shortfall by construction, because the shortfall is at most the cheapest thing the base is already building. So the LLM tier cannot land ANY choice on a base mid-build.
  2. It is hardest on the decision the project most wants right: continuing a nearly-finished item. 27 banked minerals and turns_if_continued=1 is the textbook continuity case that na-61c.2's history work and the play skill's "prefer continuity" guidance exist to get right - and the guard vetoes exactly that.
  3. It is invisible in aggregate as a QUALITY problem. The game still gets a legal item (the deterministic fallback picked the same Colony Pod here), so nothing looks broken; the run just quietly stops being an LLM-tier run. The decision record does say degraded=true, so it IS measurable - degrade_rate on base.production should be near 1.0 on any developed game, which is the number to check.

CANDIDATE FIXES, and the choice matters:
  (a) Stop declaring item cost against minerals_remaining. An item's cost is not a withdrawal from a shortfall. For a SWITCH the meaningful effect is that the accumulated minerals are forfeited; for CONTINUING it is that the shortfall falls to zero. Both are expressible, neither is "-cost".
  (b) Teach StateGuard that a "lower is better" shortfall metric is not a resource pool and must not be treated as an affordability budget. This is the more general fix - the same trap waits for any future metric with that direction.
  (c) Declare cost against a metric that IS a pool. There is no per-base mineral pool in the vocabulary today (minerals_accumulated is not in metrics.py), which is why (a) was reached for.

(b) plus (a) is the honest pair: the guard should not infer a budget from a direction, and the adapter should not declare an effect it cannot mean.

ACCEPTANCE: on a base with accumulated minerals, an agent choosing the item already in production is APPLIED (adapter row tier=llm, applied=llm, not llm_degraded), and no advisory claims the state moved. Add a regression test with a world view shaped like the one above - banked 27, cost 33, minerals_remaining 6.

Found while running na-1wu. It is the reason base.production has no tier=llm/applied=llm row yet, while faction.se has four.
close_reason: Fix is live and verified three ways: metrics.py Metric.pool + is_pool() present, hank.py:190-198 gates on 'if not is_pool(metric): continue' with a comment naming na-co2, and 52 guard/pool/state tests pass. Close commit 668a08a already recorded a live before/after on identical state (turn 42, Colony Pod 27/33: llm_degraded -> llm, degraded=false). Engineering finished 2026-08-01; the bead has been re-dispatching because status writes to this embedded store are not sticking (aegis-t15jl) — my own defer earlier this session also did not persist.

title: Decision log records tier=llm applied for decisions the game abandoned (llm_timeout_ms=2500)
description:
The orchestrator records tier=llm, degraded=false, "applied to the game" for decisions the game ALREADY ABANDONED. Measured end to end on a live game at turn 39.

WHAT HAPPENED

Ran the agent-brain loop against a real game: NA_BRAIN=agent, orchestrator up, thinker posting to 127.0.0.1:8000. Answered two decisions through /agent/next + /agent/submit. Both returned:

  {"submitted":"unit:0","applied":["unit:0"],"status":"applied to the game","degraded":false}

and the orchestrator's decision log recorded:

  faction.se       t39 Gaians tier=llm degraded=False chosen=['se:none']
  base.production  t39 Hive   tier=llm degraded=False chosen=['unit:0']

The ADAPTER's own log for the same turn says the opposite. Zero rows with tier=llm out of 66; every base.production and faction.se row reads:

  tier=deterministic  applied=native  fallback_reason="orchestrator unreachable or slow"

So the game asked, gave up, applied Thinker's own pick, and moved on. The answer I submitted minutes later was accepted by an orchestrator that had no idea the decision was dead, and written into the record of truth as a successful LLM-tier decision that was applied. It was not applied. Nothing in the decision log distinguishes it from a real one.

ROOT CAUSE, two defects

1. THE TIMEOUT DEFAULT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION.
   thinker src/main.h:180  -> `int llm_timeout_ms = 2500;`
   thinker src/na_http.cpp:285 -> "timeout_ms <= 0 means wait indefinitely, which is the
   configured default."
   Those cannot both be true, and the code wins: the adapter waits 2.5 seconds. thinker.ini
   ships without an llm_timeout_ms line, so 2500 is what every run gets.

   .claude/skills/play-alpha-centauri/SKILL.md tells the agent "The game blocks while you
   think ... there is no clock on your reasoning." That is false against this build by three
   orders of magnitude. An attached agent cannot answer in 2.5s; a human-driven one certainly
   cannot. So on the current default the agent brain CANNOT EVER win the race, and every
   agent-tier run silently degrades to Thinker while reporting success.

2. THE ORCHESTRATOR CANNOT KNOW, AND CLAIMS ANYWAY.
   /agent/submit returns "status":"applied to the game". It has no signal from the adapter that
   the application happened - the adapter already returned native_choice to the engine and hung
   up. A pending decision is never expired, so an answer arriving after the game moved on is
   indistinguishable from one that arrived in time.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A NORMAL BUG

It corrupts the record of truth in the direction that flatters us. docs/observability.md 5.4
exists to catch "a run of pure fallbacks that completes and looks green". This is that failure
inverted and made invisible: the fallbacks ARE recorded, correctly, in the adapter log - and the
orchestrator writes a second, contradictory record marking them llm-tier successes. Every number
derived from the decision log is affected: coverage, degrade_rate, tier attribution, directive
attention and override rates (na-mmp), and any A/B outcome measurement (na-6db). A measurement
that reads 'the LLM tier decided this' when Thinker decided it cannot be corrected after the
fact, because both records look well-formed.

It also invalidates the obvious reading of na-1wu / na-ckn. Submitting successfully and seeing
tier=llm in the decision log is NOT evidence the loop closed. The only proof is a tier=llm row in
the ADAPTER's na-observations.jsonl, or applied_item matching what the agent chose.

FIX

- Short term, unblocks the P0s: set llm_timeout_ms explicitly. 0 for the documented
  wait-indefinitely behaviour, or a large finite value (300000) so an unanswered decision cannot
  freeze the game forever. Either way thinker.ini must carry the line rather than inherit 2500.
- Reconcile main.h:180 with na_http.cpp:285. One of them is lying and the comment is the one
  people read.
- The orchestrator must stop asserting what it cannot observe. Either expire a pending decision
  once the adapter's deadline has passed and record it as abandoned, or have the adapter confirm
  application and only then finalise the record. "status":"applied to the game" should be
  reported by the side that applied it.
- Correct the SKILL's "no clock on your reasoning" line to state the real bound.

Note there is already a related commit, thinker 267275a "fix(neural): record a cached decision
that the board overtook" - same family (an answer arriving after the world moved), different
path.

VERIFY BY MECHANISM, NOT BY THE REPORTING INTERFACE: two logs disagreed here and the one that
was easy to read was the wrong one.
close_reason: All four of the bead's own fix items verified done in code, not by commit message: (1) llm_timeout_ms now provisioned and brain-coupled (87e3147, mine); (2) main.h/na_http.cpp comment reconciled (692080d) — 2500 correctly retained for non-agent brains; (3) orchestrator stops asserting what it cannot observe (bf3170e) — _accepted_status no longer says 'applied to the game', AgentBrain abandons before the engine via ABANDON_MARGIN_SECONDS, late submits get 409 telling the agent not to resubmit; (4) SKILL.md:12 corrected. Full suite 477 passed 0 failed. Residual late-finish path is now REPORTED as late rather than recorded as an applied llm decision — the silent flattering misrecord this bead was about is gone. Dead-process pendings remain na-bzd.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
ADAPTER HALF LANDED — NeuralAmplifier 87e3147. Orchestrator half is NOT done (na-bzd).
(ellie, 2026-08-02)

MEASURED WHAT WAS ACTUALLY LEFT, because two of this bead's four fix items were already done:

  [DONE, 692080d] Reconcile main.h:197 with na_http.cpp:285. The comment now states the truth
                  ("that is the INTENDED default and it is NOT what ships").
  [DONE]          SKILL.md "no clock on your reasoning" — line 12 now reads "but only for
                  llm_timeout_ms, and the built-in default is ...".
  [DONE, 87e3147] thinker.ini must carry the line rather than inherit 2500.  <- this commit
  [NOT DONE]      The orchestrator must stop asserting what it cannot observe.  -> na-bzd

THE GAP WAS NARROWER AND WORSE THAN THE BEAD STATES. The bead says "thinker.ini ships without an
llm_timeout_ms line". True, but the repo's thinker.ini has no llm block AT ALL — play-thinker.sh
WRITES one (llm_factions, llm_endpoint) and omitted llm_timeout_ms. So the provisioner that
exists to configure the gate was the thing that left the timeout inherited. Grepped the whole
tree: before this commit llm_timeout_ms appeared only in docs, comments and tests, and in NO
file the engine reads.

AND 2500 IS NOT ITSELF A BUG — worth stating, because "raise the default" is the obvious wrong
fix. main.h chooses it "to cover a Haiku call on a warm connection", which is right for the LLM
tier and is what keeps a dead orchestrator from hanging a turn (invariant 9). It is wrong only
for the ONE brain invariant 9 already carves an exception for. AGENTS.md:59-66 documents that
exception and says to set "NA_AGENT_TIMEOUT (and llm_timeout_ms on the adapter)" — so this was a
documented requirement that nothing implemented.

FIX: the timeout now follows the brain, which is the coupling AGENTS.md requires.
    NA_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS set -> that value      NA_BRAIN=agent -> 300000      else -> 2500
All three verified, plus idempotence against the real play dir (an ini already carrying
llm_timeout_ms=0 is left alone and the value reported, matching the existing llm_factions rule).
Finite rather than 0 deliberately: <=0 means wait indefinitely, and an unattended run that hangs
forever is what NA_TIMEOUT exists to catch (na-ie9) — under Xvfb a hung game looks exactly like
a working one.

The script now WARNS when it takes 2500 with no NA_BRAIN set. The silence was the defect.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, so nobody reads this as closing the P0: the orchestrator still returns
"status":"applied to the game" for something it cannot observe, and a pending decision from a
dead game is still accepted. Until na-bzd lands, the decision log can still record a tier=llm
success for a decision the game abandoned — this commit only stops the agent from LOSING the
race by construction. Leaving na-t3h OPEN for that reason.

VERIFY BY MECHANISM, per this bead's own closing line: the proof an agent decision landed is a
tier=llm row in the ADAPTER's na-observations.jsonl, or applied_item matching what the agent
chose — never the orchestrator's own record.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
CLOSING — all four of this bead's own FIX items are done and verified by mechanism.
(ellie, 2026-08-02)

The bead lists four fixes. I checked each against the code rather than against its commit
message, because a commit existing is not the code being live — the lesson na-co2 just taught
me three dispatches running.

  [1] "thinker.ini must carry the line rather than inherit 2500"
      DONE — 87e3147 (mine, this session). The gap was narrower than the bead states: the repo
      thinker.ini has no llm block AT ALL; play-thinker.sh WRITES one (llm_factions,
      llm_endpoint) and omitted the timeout. Grepped the tree first: llm_timeout_ms appeared
      only in docs, comments and tests, never in a file the engine reads.
      The timeout now FOLLOWS THE BRAIN, which is the coupling AGENTS.md:65 already required:
        NA_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS -> that value | NA_BRAIN=agent -> 300000 | else -> 2500
      All three verified, plus idempotence against the real play dir (an ini already carrying
      llm_timeout_ms=0 is left alone). Finite not 0: <=0 is wait-indefinitely and a hung
      unattended run is indistinguishable from a working one under Xvfb (na-ie9).

  [2] "Reconcile main.h:197 with na_http.cpp:285"
      DONE — 692080d. Read the comment: it now states the truth outright ("that is the INTENDED
      default and it is NOT what ships"). main.h still defaults 2500 and that is CORRECT — it is
      chosen "to cover a Haiku call on a warm connection" and is what keeps invariant 9 for
      every non-agent brain. Raising it would have been the obvious wrong fix.

  [3] "The orchestrator must stop asserting what it cannot observe"
      DONE — bf3170e. Verified in code, not just message:
        service.py:_accepted_status  no longer emits "applied to the game"; returns
          "accepted — returned to the engine to apply", or for a passed deadline
          "NOT applied — the engine's {N}ms deadline passed ... the game has applied its own
          fallback and moved on"
        AgentBrain waits on min(self.timeout, engine deadline) - ABANDON_MARGIN_SECONDS,
          floored at half the deadline, so it abandons FIRST and the existing
          Unanswered -> BrainError -> degrade path records honestly
        WorldView.decision_deadline_ms typed (not a passthrough extra — na-wzw's lesson),
          with 0/negative collapsing to None so "absent stays unbounded"
        DecisionQueue.await_answer returns that reason as the 409 body, telling the agent not
          to resubmit

  [4] "Correct the SKILL's 'no clock on your reasoning' line"
      DONE — SKILL.md:12 now reads "but only for llm_timeout_ms, and the built-in default is ...".

TESTS: full orchestrator suite 477 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. Targeted
`-k "abandon or deadline or pending or agent_brain or submit"` -> 37 passed.

RESIDUAL, documented rather than hidden — and it is why _accepted_status keeps its deadline
branch. The abandon margin (250ms) does not cover work that happens AFTER the answer is handed
over: grounding, the guard, and a possible repair. So a decision can still finish late. The
difference from the state this bead was filed in is that it is now REPORTED as late instead of
recorded as an applied llm decision. That is the defect this bead was about — silent and
flattering — and it is gone.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS, and deliberately not claimed: a pending from a genuinely DEAD game process
is a different failure — no deadline logic saves you when the run itself vanished. That is
na-bzd, which contract.py:264 calls "the companion to decision_deadline_ms and the half it
cannot cover", and it is partially landed already (b675d9d names the run so the orchestrator can
see the game die). Still open, still mine.

VERIFY BY MECHANISM, per this bead's own closing line: proof an agent decision landed is a
tier=llm row in the ADAPTER's na-observations.jsonl, or applied_item matching the agent's
choice — never the orchestrator's own record.

title: Play a turn with Claude Code driving via MCP
description:
Supersedes the transport half of na-ckn. Everything is built and verified without a game; this is the run that needs one.

  1. $SMAC_DIR present, 'just game verify' clean.
  2. thinker.ini: llm_factions=2, llm_endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:8000, llm_timeout_ms=0 (wait indefinitely).
  3. 'just play' — orchestrator with NA_BRAIN=agent.
  4. claude mcp add neural-amplifier, then let the play-alpha-centauri skill drive.
  5. Confirm: the game blocks at a base.production decision, next_decision returns a world view built from LIVE engine state, submit_orders changes what the base builds.
  6. Then kill the agent mid-decision with NA_AGENT_TIMEOUT set and confirm the game degrades to the deterministic tier instead of hanging.

Watch specifically for the window going 'not responding': the DLL slices its wait and calls PeekMessage(PM_NOREMOVE) without dispatching, deliberately, to avoid re-entering the engine from inside mod_base_build. If the window is unusable rather than merely stale, that trade needs revisiting - do NOT fix it by dispatching messages.
notes:
THE LOOP CLOSES. First adapter-side proof, 2026-08-02, live game:

  {'surface_id':'faction.se','turn':41,'faction':'Gaians','tier':'llm','applied':'llm','fallback_reason':None}

An attached Claude Code agent claimed a decision from a live engine via POST /agent/next, answered it via /agent/submit, and the ENGINE applied it. Verified in na-observations.jsonl (the adapter's own log), not in the orchestrator's - see na-t3h for why the orchestrator's record cannot be trusted for this.

Setup that made it work, all from step 2 of this bead: llm_factions=2 (Gaians, faction_id 1), llm_endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:8000, llm_timeout_ms=0. The last of those is load-bearing and the bead was right to name it: the built-in default is 2500ms and NO attached agent can meet it (na-t3h).

STILL OUTSTANDING for this bead:
  - Step 5 names base.production specifically. The surface proven is faction.se. The path is shared (na_decide_* -> na_http_post -> apply) so the mechanism is surface-agnostic, but the literal check has not been made: no tier=llm base.production row exists yet. Driving turns 41->42 produced no Gaians base.production decision, and the turn stopped advancing at 42 (the scripted TURN COMPLETE / confirm clicks stop working there - a unit awaiting orders, most likely).
  - Step 6 (kill the agent mid-decision with NA_AGENT_TIMEOUT set, confirm the game degrades rather than hangs) has NOT been run.
  - Step 4 used the HTTP agent endpoints directly rather than 'claude mcp add'. mcp_server.py wraps the same /agent/next + /agent/submit, so this is a thin difference, but it IS a difference and the bead says MCP.

Two operational traps found while doing it, both of which cost real time:
  - The orchestrator survives game restarts and keeps pendings from DEAD game processes, which then look like live work. Restart the orchestrator whenever you restart the game, and confirm /agent/waiting is empty before trusting the queue.
  - 'orchestrator unreachable or slow' is one message for two different causes (connection refused vs deadline passed). A decision that fired while the port was momentarily free is indistinguishable from one that timed out.

BASE.PRODUCTION REACHED THE LLM TIER (turn 42, Morgan Solutions, Morganites):

  adapter row: tier=llm, applied=llm_degraded, applied_item_name=Colony Pod

So step 5's transport half is proven on base.production, not just faction.se: the game blocked, /agent/next returned a world view built from live engine state (base_state, metrics, an eight-item action space with costs and both turn estimates, run_id, history), and the answer went back through the apply path.

BUT the choice did NOT change what the base builds, and the reason is a new P0: na-co2. StateGuard denied the entire action space because it reads minerals_remaining (a SHORTFALL - minerals still needed, 6 here) as a spendable budget, while every action declares effects of the full item cost (33). Every option therefore looks unaffordable by construction, the decision degraded, and the deterministic tier's pick was applied. `applied=llm_degraded` is the adapter recording that honestly.

So the state of this bead is now precise:
  - faction.se: FULLY closed loop, applied=llm, four times (turns 41, 42, and 1 of the stray run).

title: -na-autoload: exit the main menu after loading (menu-to-session transition)
description:
-na-autoload (thinker fork 2b82af5) successfully loads a savegame - mod_load_daemon returns SAVE_LOAD_VALID (status 0) against a real Autosave_<year>.sav, verified on the gaming host. But the game stays on the main menu, so the loaded state is unreachable.

Clearing *GameHalted is not sufficient. The engine does more of the menu-to-session transition inside load_game (engine.cpp:1057, address 0x5AAAB0) than state loading alone - probably tearing down the menu's own modal loop and entering the main interface. load_game takes (int, int) and addresses saves by slot, which is why it cannot be called directly for an arbitrary path.

Candidate approaches, cheapest first:
1. Identify what load_game does around its call to load_daemon (the call site is hooked at patch.cpp:639, address 0x5AAD7D) and replicate the surrounding steps. Disassembly of 0x5AAAB0..0x5AAD7D would answer it directly.
2. Find the menu's modal loop exit condition and set it alongside GameHalted.
3. Drive the menu with synthetic input instead. xdotool is installed and CAN see the Wine window ('Wine Desktop'), so sending the load-game keystrokes is feasible. Brittle and resolution-dependent, but it needs no engine RE and would unblock unattended runs today.

Approach 3 is the pragmatic unblock; 1 is the correct fix.
acceptance_criteria: Launching with -na-autoload <save> results in a playable in-game session with no human input; na-observations.jsonl shows base.production lines appearing without anyone touching the keyboard
notes:
Starting the QUICK START trace: the label 'QUICK START' does not appear as a string in terranx.exe, in any *.txt in the game directory, or in the 00000409.256 localization resource. So the startup menu is NOT a popp/Script.txt dialog - which rules out the cleanest intervention (intercepting the menu's popp call and answering it programmatically) and means the buttons are drawn from a graphical resource with the dispatch table in code.

Consequence: finding the QUICK START handler needs the menu's click-dispatch code located by structure rather than by string reference. Suggested route: the startup menu is drawn as a Console/Win, and gui.cpp already declares thiscall wrappers for the main-menu class at 0x5FB100 and neighbours (CMAINMENU_ADDSUBMENU_F etc.) - that class is the place to start, since whatever owns the buttons owns their handlers.

Note this does NOT invalidate the strategy in the previous note. Starting a game normally and then swapping state via the replay path is still the right shape; only the means of triggering 'start a game normally' is still open. If QUICK START proves awkward to invoke, any path that establishes a session will do, including a scripted new-game start.
close_reason: SOLVED. -na-autoload reaches a playable session unattended: click QUICK START (opens nothing modal), press Enter to confirm PLANETFALL, then run the engine's own replay/undo load sequence. Verified end to end with no human input - turn 35 from the target save, GameHalted clear, map rendered, no dialog. Key insight: stop constructing the menu-to-session transition and let the engine perform it, then swap state.

description: Run sha1sum against the Steam Planetary Pack install; want 4b19c1fe3266b5ebc4305cd182ed6e864e3a1c4a (3,084,288 bytes). Thinker refuses any other build. If it differs, the physical ISO plus the official v2.0 patch becomes the primary fixture source. Blocks every game-dependent lane. See docs/headless-harness.md section 2.

RESOLVED on gaming host (2026-07-29), but NOT by matching the hash.

Steam Planetary Pack (app 2204130), installdir 'Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri':
  terranx.exe  sha1 7bbcc54e64760c11a24f48862f15dbaaeab61435  3,094,576 bytes
  terran.exe   sha1 ca90a0776a5685a01c346e85fd23f3116ece975e  3,201,128 bytes
  PE: i386, 8 sections, link timestamp 1999-12-20 20:30:55 (original Firaxis build, not repacked)

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Staged — thinker `70e488d` is what the next launch will load (harding)

Staged CURRENT `origin/master` at execution time as you asked, which had moved again:
`7a930f8` -> `b97d2b9` -> **`70e488d`** (na-tit, `factions_at_war`). All three of the things
that matter are in it: defer, the base.hurry routing fix, and the entry-point hook shipping OFF.

### What was done, and why in the staging checkout rather than by copying a DLL in

`/tmp/thinker-good` was a detached checkout at `2b39bdc` whose built DLL was **byte-identical**
to the one the live game had loaded (`b38669d5…` on both) — that agreement between git tree and
artifact is the property that made the directory trustworthy. Copying a DLL built elsewhere into
it would have kept the artifact current and left the git tree saying `2b39bdc`, which is the
"the checkout says X and the binary is Y" trap this project has paid for elsewhere.

So: `git checkout --detach 70e488d` in the staging dir, then rebuild in place. Tree and artifact
agree again.

    staged      /tmp/thinker-good/build/release/thinker.dll
                sha256 e0f9546dc3dd429c82f37eaf6d486b12221287a3e2f87a5e736c788b6c5a1152
                built from 70e488d, in the staging checkout, which is now at 70e488d

    rollback    build/release/thinker.dll.rollback-2b39bdc-20260823-002443
                sha256 b38669d5a1a66e9d66ee099ce792cc35dfc6af712b2c4dee6dfa5341227b60f6
                the exact bytes the live game was running; `modmenu.txt` copied beside it

Restoring is a copy back over `build/release/thinker.dll`, no rebuild and no git operation.

### Verified by the artifact, not by the copy succeeding

Symbol markers, staged against rollback — each one a positive and a negative in the same line:

| marker | staged | rollback |
|---|---|---|
| `defer` / `deferred` | **2** | **0** |
| `factions_at_war` | 1 | 0 |
| `hurry-stats` | 1 | 0 |
| `dialog-stats` | 1 | 0 |
| `base.hurry` | 3 | 3 (control — the surface existed either way) |

`modmenu.txt` is staged beside the DLL and contains `#TOPMENU` — the na-nnn draw-buffer fatal.

**Note the two DLLs are not byte-identical to my worktree's build of the same sha**
(`e0f9546…` vs `d67d874…`). That is ordinary non-reproducible-build variance — embedded paths —
and it is why the check above is on symbol markers rather than on a sha match between two trees.
The sha that matters is the staged one, recorded here.

I did **not** write into the Steam play directory. `play-thinker.sh` copies `THINKER_DIR/build/release/thinker.dll`
into it at launch and takes its own stock backup, so the next `play-thinker.sh` run picks this up
with no further action. A launch of `terranx.exe` by hand would still load the old
`$STEAM/.../thinker.dll` — say the word if you want that overwritten too.

## ⚠️ One consequence of the hurry fix that should not be discovered in a live session

The fix works, which is the problem worth naming. Measured on the live configuration:

| | measured |
|---|---|
| live `thinker.ini` | `llm_factions=126`, `llm_endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:8000`, **`llm_timeout_ms=0`** |
| live orchestrator env (pid 3671407) | `NA_BRAIN=agent`, **no `NA_AGENT_TIMEOUT`** |
| captured world views | `decision_deadline_ms: null` |

`llm_timeout_ms=0` means the adapter waits indefinitely; `NA_AGENT_TIMEOUT` unset means the
AgentBrain does too. So **every routed decision blocks until something answers it.** That was
already true and the game played fine, because base.production was the only base surface routing
and somebody was answering.

base.hurry now routes as well, and it is not a small addition:

    base.production   ~108 decisions per turn  (324 over 3 turns, 2026-08-21 log)
    base.hurry        136 decisions per turn   (measured, this session)

**Roughly 2.3x the decisions per AI round**, all of them blocking, none of them previously seen
by whoever was answering. Nothing is broken by this — it is the surface working for the first
time — but a session that starts and finds the AI round two and a bit times longer should know
why before reaching for a rollback.

Two things take the sting out, and both already exist:

- **The plan table covers base.hurry.** `PlanEntry` is keyed `(surface_id, base_id)`, so a turn
  plan can answer hurry decisions in milliseconds exactly as it does production ones — which is
  what na-7bk is for and what makes this affordable rather than merely correct.
- **Rollback is one copy**, above, and needs no rebuild.

One honest limitation, recorded on na-4zs and repeated because it bites here: a base.hurry
decision record carries `native_choice: null` and always will — the engine's version decides and
spends in one pass, so the surface cannot be both observed and decided. na-6db has no native
baseline for it.

comments.text: Launch regression: game dies at splash with the engine fatal "unable to allocate draw-buffer; terminating program" when the current master build (020d68c) is installed. Pre-update build 2b39bdc launches and loads saves cleanly — bisect range is 2b39bdc..020d68c (25 commits), prime suspect the upstream Thinker v5.5 merge b8c1fb8 (rewritten game startup code: e6e02c9, 1eda847; engine_win.h +661). Not display/wine related: same prefix+display works with the old build; wine GDI renderer made no difference; thinker.ini video settings unchanged (video_mode=2, 2560x1440). Crashed run's own na-observations show the na.autoload quickstart flow ran then gave up ("no session after quickstart"), so the fatal fires during game-session setup, not window creation. comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Bisect verdict + root cause (harding, 2026-08-21)

**Not one defect but two, stacked.** The second was invisible until the first was fixed, and the
first is not in our code at all — it is a data file the install path never ships.

### Bisect: f10683f GOOD -> b8c1fb8 (the v5.5 merge) BAD

Headless, on a staged copy, both control arms measured BEFORE bisecting:

| commit | verdict | evidence (its own na-observations.jsonl, not an exit code) |
|---|---|---|
| 2b39bdc | GOOD | `event:"loaded" ... status=0, turn:100` |
| f10683f (last pre-merge) | GOOD | same |
| b8c1fb8 (Merge upstream Thinker v5.5) | BAD | `event:"give_up" "no session after quickstart"` |
| 020d68c (master) | BAD | same |

The six upstream-side commits (b8c1fb8^1..b8c1fb8^2: 1eda847, e6e02c9, 41fc7d4, 760cfdd, cc44b38,
c0e270c) are **untestable by any predicate we own** — they carry no Neural Amplifier code, so
-na-autoload is not parsed, na_autoload_tick never runs and nothing is logged. `git bisect` cannot
narrow past the merge and says so. Synthetic merges to test them individually are not available
either: all six conflict against f10683f (`git merge-tree`), which is why the real merge was
hand-resolved.

Harness: `scripts/bisect-thinker-launch.sh` (NA repo, wt/harding). It reads the verdict from the
run's own log because thinker.exe is an injector and discards the game's exit status. It skips a
commit whose built DLL has no `-na-autoload` literal in it — that is a fact about the artifact,
available in milliseconds, and it turns each untestable commit from a 4-minute timeout into an
immediate correct `skip`.

### Root cause 1: v5.5 moved the main menu into thinker, and the menu's DATA FILE is not installed

Debug build, startup trace ends at `top_menu 0` — thinker's **new** reimplementation of top_menu,
installed by the merge (`write_call(0x52AC4A, top_menu)` is a + line in patch.cpp). It calls:

    Popup_start(&cur_popup, "modmenu", "TOPMENU", ...)     // game.cpp:720-721 @ 020d68c

**`#TOPMENU` does not exist in the installed modmenu.txt.** It was added to `docs/modmenu.txt` by
the merge (0 occurrences at 2b39bdc, 1 at 020d68c, 8 items: START GAME / QUICK START / SCENARIO /
LOAD GAME / MULTIPLAYER / CHANGE OPTIONS / VIEW CREDITS / EXIT GAME). The play directory's copy is
an older Induktio release and matches NEITHER revision by md5. Asked for a popup section that is
not there, the menu cannot be built and the engine dies with its own
`Unable to allocate draw-buffer; terminating program.`

`play-thinker.sh` installs thinker.dll, thinker.exe and thinker.ini. It has never installed
modmenu.txt. So the DLL was updated and the data file it now depends on was not — the failure is
in the install path, not in the merge.

### Root cause 2 (revealed by fixing 1): the autoload's fixed-pixel click now lands on SCENARIO

With 020d68c's `docs/modmenu.txt` in place the **fatal is gone** — no FATAL ERROR window at any
sample point, the menu renders. But the run still ends `give_up`, because:

    NA_QUICKSTART_FX = 2370/2560, NA_QUICKSTART_FY = 1034/1440    // neural.cpp:3651

The new `#TOPMENU` is BOTTOM-anchored (`#y -5`) and has 8 items where the engine's own menu had 7.
Adding an item grows the list upward, so every entry moved up one row (~75px at 1440). Measured on
the frame: QUICK START now centres at y~959; the click still goes to y=1034, which is SCENARIO.
Photographed at t=26s: a **LOAD** file browser listing the scenario folder is open on screen.

### Evidence this is not about NA at all (2x2, same harness)

| build | flags | FATAL ERROR window at 20s |
|---|---|---|
| 020d68c | `-na-autoload <save>` | YES (present at t=8s, *before* the autoload's first action at 12s) |
| 020d68c | none | **YES** |
| 2b39bdc | none | no |
| 2b39bdc | `-na-autoload <save>` | no - loads the save, turn 100 |

The fatal fires with no NA flags at all, and it fires BEFORE na_autoload_tick acts. This corrects
the bead's opening inference ("the fatal fires during game-session setup, not window creation"):
it fires earlier than either - during main-menu construction, on the splash screen. The
click_quickstart / confirm_planetfall records in the crashed run are the state machine posting
into an already-dead game; they are noise, not cause.

### Incidental: the DEBUG build lane is broken on master

`src/gui_dialog.cpp:420` passes `reserve` to `debug()`, but the value was refactored into
`na_energy_loan_terms()` and no longer exists in that scope. Release builds compile because
`debug(...)` expands to nothing; `cmake --preset debug` fails outright. It blocked this diagnosis
until patched locally. (Also: only Release/Develop get `-static`, so a debug thinker.dll silently
fails to load unless libstdc++-6/libgcc_s_dw2-1/libwinpthread-1 are next to terranx.exe - it looks
exactly like a mod that did nothing.)

### Isolation used (a live game was running on this host throughout)

Staged copy at ~/workspace/smac-bisect (rsync of the install), its own wine prefix
(~/.local/share/na-wine-bisect), and llm_endpoint repointed to a dead port so no bisect run could
reach the orchestrator on :8000. The Steam directory, :8000 and :3030 were never touched.

Fixes for both root causes next, on this bead.

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Both defects fixed and verified end-to-end (harding)

Branch `wt/harding` pushed on both repos (scbrown/thinker, scbrown/NeuralAmplifier). Not merged
to master — a thinker build gets installed over the running game, so that call is yours.

### thinker @ wt/harding

- `8706c35 fix(launch): ship modmenu.txt with the DLL, and pick QUICK START by name (na-nnn)`
  - **CMakeLists.txt**: a POST_BUILD rule stages `docs/modmenu.txt` next to thinker.dll. The
    binary and the menu definitions it cannot start without now move together, which is what
    makes it installable by everything downstream — play-thinker.sh copies from there, and so
    does `just game stage`, whose `--mod` overlay is that directory.
  - **neural.cpp / neural.h / game.cpp**: `na_autoload_menu_choice()`. top_menu is our code
    since v5.5, so the autoload NAMES the item it wants (#TOPMENU index 1, read the same way
    top_menu's own switch reads it) instead of aiming a synthetic click at a screen fraction.
    NA_QUICKSTART_FX/FY stay as the fallback for a menu we did not build. na_autoload_tick
    skips its click when the menu was answered directly — checked BEFORE the `!*GameHalted`
    guard, because a quickstart that reaches a session quickly clears GameHalted and a guard
    waiting for it to be SET would hang there instead of giving up.
- `2753522 fix(build): restore the debug lane` — the `reserve` break reported above.
- `tests/run-na-tests.sh`: **38 checks, 0 failures**. The seam checker caught the new call site
  as UNTRACKED (that is the guard doing its job); manifest regenerated, 70 call sites.

### NeuralAmplifier @ wt/harding

- `d9999eb fix(play): install modmenu.txt with the DLL; add the headless launch bisect harness`
  - play-thinker.sh installs modmenu.txt, backs up the stock one, and **refuses** to launch if
    the installed DLL carries the TOPMENU literal while the installed modmenu.txt has no such
    section. Both outcomes proven: stale file -> `EXIT=1` with the refusal naming the fatal;
    normal build -> `EXIT=0`, silent, `#TOPMENU` count 1.
  - `scripts/bisect-thinker-launch.sh` kept for the next launch regression.

### Verification — the bad commit now launches and resumes

020d68c (the commit this bead was filed against), release build, headless, staged play dir:

    hook_alive          saves/auto/Autosave_2200.sav
    menu_choice         QUICK START (#TOPMENU index 1)      <- new deterministic path
    quickstart_selected top_menu answered directly          <- no click posted
    confirm_planetfall  VK_RETURN
    loaded              saves/auto/Autosave_2200.sav status=0   halted:0  turn:100

No FATAL ERROR window at any of the eight sample points (8/14/21/26/33/40/55/70s), against a
photographed one at t=8s before the fix.

### One thing I got wrong, and how it was caught

The refusal check first used `strings -el` (copied from assert_flag_in_dll) — wrong encoding,
since `-el` finds wchar_t literals and "TOPMENU" is a plain char literal, so it matched nothing
and passed silently. Fixing that, it STILL passed. The reason is worth carrying:

**`set -o pipefail` + `grep -q` is a false negative on a large producer.** `-q` makes grep exit
at the first match, which SIGPIPEs the `strings` still writing, and the pipeline then reports
failure although the match succeeded. Measured 5/5 against this DLL. `assert_flag_in_dll` has
the identical shape and is safe only by accident — `strings -el` emits 13 lines here against
`strings`' 14246, so grep drains it before exiting. Hardened both to a counted form; its failure
mode is refusing to launch over a flag that IS present.

Both were caught only because the failing case was run. A guard verified in one direction is
half a guard.

### Not done here

- **Merge to master** — yours to call; a thinker build lands on the live game's DLL.
- **`just game stage`'s overlay** now has modmenu.txt available in the build dir, but I did not
  exercise that path (it needs a pristine SMAC_DIR, which does not exist on this host — the
  only install is the Steam one, which is the live game).
- **The live game keeps running on 2b39bdc** and I did not touch it, its prefix, :8000 or :3030.

comments.text:
## Addendum: two loose ends from the comment above, both now closed (harding)

**1. `just game stage` — I said I had not exercised it. Half of that is now measured.**
`game_fixture.py stage` copies *every file* in the `--mod` directory into the play dir
(`scripts/game_fixture.py:404-407`), and the justfile's default `--mod` is
`{{thinker}}/build/develop`. The POST_BUILD rule is attached to the `thinkerlib` TARGET rather
than to a configuration, so it fires for every preset — verified by building `develop` and
finding `build/develop/modmenu.txt` with `#TOPMENU` count 1 beside `build/develop/thinker.dll`.
So the staging path carries the file now. What remains untested is a full `stage` RUN, which
needs a pristine SMAC_DIR; this host's only install is the Steam one, which is the live game.

**2. Attended launches now skip the main menu, which is a real behaviour change.**
`play-thinker.sh` passes `-na-autoload` on every launch (NA_RESUME defaults to 1), so a human
launching normally used to see the menu for ~12s before the state machine clicked QUICK START
for them. It is now selected immediately and the menu is not drawn. Same end state, one less
flash — but if you wanted those seconds to reach the menu by hand, `NA_RESUME=0` boots there
and is the documented way. Calling it out because it is the kind of change nobody reads a
commit message to discover.

**Full verification matrix**, one harness, staged play dir, photographed each run:

| build | flags | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 020d68c (before) | `-na-autoload` | FATAL ERROR window at t=8s |
| 020d68c (before) | none | FATAL ERROR window |
| 2b39bdc (workaround) | none | menu renders |
| 2b39bdc (workaround) | `-na-autoload` | loaded, turn 100 |
| **fixed** | `-na-autoload` | **loaded, turn 100** — menu answered directly, no click posted |
| **fixed** | none | **menu renders normally**, nothing auto-selected |

The last row is the one that matters for the gating: the fix is inert for anyone who did not ask
for an autoload.

title: Move whole-function seams onto the patch table, following na_base_hurry_observed
description:
The pattern that already demonstrably works. na_base_hurry_observed is a single line in patch.cpp — write_call(0x4F7A38, (int)na_base_hurry_observed) — with the wrapper body living in neural.cpp. It needed ZERO work across v5.5. The in-body game.cpp seams, by contrast, cost the whole relocation.

The reason it survives is structural: patch.cpp is a table of addresses, and addresses are what upstream is careful not to churn. Our entry sits in a list of ~200 sibling entries and merges as one line.

Mapped the enclosing function of every invasive hunk against patch.cpp's table. Seven host functions are ALREADY patch-table entries, so their edits could become a registered na_*_observed wrapper instead:

  base.cpp        mod_capture_base
  base.cpp        mod_base_production
  gui_dialog.cpp  mod_base_swap
  gui_dialog.cpp  mod_energy_trade
  gui_dialog.cpp  mod_buy_tech
  basewin.cpp     BaseWin_gov_options
  gameturn.cpp    faction_upkeep

Check each before converting — the technique only applies where the seam needs the function's inputs and its return value. faction_upkeep is the known exception: its three seams (ODP upkeep, corner market, council) are mid-body and observe state the wrapper cannot see, so it stays as it is. Treat that as the shape of the test, not as a discouragement.

Explicitly NOT candidates, because they are internal Thinker helpers with no table entry: select_build, consider_staple, push_item (build.cpp), governor_priorities (plan.cpp). Those need a different answer or none.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the seven candidates is either converted to a patch-table-registered wrapper or has a one-line note saying why it cannot be; the invasive hunk count in the converted files drops correspondingly; build clean with zero warnings and wire tests still green.
close_reason: Analysed all eleven candidates; NONE is convertible, and the negative result is the deliverable. na_base_hurry_observed works because mod_base_hurry takes no arguments (reads *CurrentBaseID from globals) AND an existing patched call site (0x4F7A38) was available to re-point — both halves are required and no other seam has both. Notably mod_base_build, which looked like the best candidate, is not in the patch table at all: it is reached only from mod_base_reset (base.cpp:1094), so there is no entry to redirect. mod_base_reset itself is convertible in principle but has 20 table entries, so converting would change 20 lines to save one seam. Full per-candidate table recorded in docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md section 5.2 so this is not re-derived. Durable answer for the other 67 seams is verification (na-alr.1), not relocation. Spun out na-4zs: re-pointing one table entry only intercepts that call site, and mod_base_upkeep calls mod_base_hurry directly at base.cpp:4263 on the production path.

title: Seam manifest + source-level guard so a dropped seam cannot pass CI
description:
The highest-value item, and the cheapest, because the fork already has the idiom in-house: tests/check_native_choice_withheld.py asserts a structural property by READING SOURCE. It just only reads neural.cpp.

The gap, demonstrated on the merged tree rather than argued: comment out na_observe_econ_energy_sliders in gameturn.cpp and you get build exit 0 with zero warnings, 43/43 wire tests, and check_native_choice_withheld.py green. Nothing anywhere notices.

That is not a hypothetical for this fork. The v5.5 merge presented 547 lines of ours against an empty upstream side and eight seams had to be re-placed by hand; dropping one would have produced a clean, green, silently-degraded build.

Build a manifest of the 88 seam call sites (counts per host file, excluding comments: gui_dialog 18, base 15, main 9, build 8, gameturn 8, basewin 7, plan 7, game 4, gui 4, patch 4, faction 2, move 1, tech 1) recording for each: the na_ symbol, its host function, and the ordering invariant that makes it correct where one exists. The invariants are already written as comments at each site and they are load-bearing — 'FIRST, before *CurrentTurn is incremented', 'LAST, after all four SE_alloc_labs narrowings', 'reserve read BEFORE the deduction'. Those are the interesting half: a seam that survives a merge but MOVES is as wrong as one that vanishes, and only the ordering ones can catch that.

Follow check_native_choice_withheld.py's approach — source order and regex over the host file, no game required — so this runs in CI next to the wire tests.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest covering all 88 seams; a checker that fails when a seam is missing and, for seams with a stated ordering invariant, when it moves relative to its anchor; wired into tests/run-na-tests.sh or the pre-push gate; proven by deleting a seam and watching it go red.
close_reason: Manifest at thinker tests/na_seams.tsv (68 call sites + 17 helper definitions across 13 upstream-owned files); checker tests/check_seams.py verifies presence, count, and 7 pinned ordering invariants; a vanished anchor fails rather than passing. Held to its claim by tests/test_check_seams.py: 10 mutations of a copied tree (dropped, commented out, moved between functions, drifted past first/last/before anchors, duplicated, untracked, host function deleted) all refused, plus a control proving the real tree still passes. Wired into run-na-tests.sh, which also now runs check_native_choice_withheld.py — that was an orphan test nothing executed. Commit f2bec14.

title: [epic] Position the Thinker fork to survive upstream releases
description:
Follow-up to the v5.5 sync (na-15o). Measured rather than assumed, on the merged tree:

  our own files (neural.*, na_http.*, tests)   ~7,700 lines   ZERO conflict surface
  edits inside upstream-owned files            ~1,100 lines   96 hunks / 19 files

Of those 96 hunks only 28 are invasive (modify or delete an upstream line), across 6 files: base.cpp, main.cpp, gui_dialog.cpp, patch.cpp, build.cpp, plan.cpp. The other 68 are pure insertions, which git merges around. That is consistent with what v5.5 did: a release rewriting ~5,000 lines produced exactly three conflicts.

So conflict VOLUME is not the problem, and restructuring to avoid conflicts would optimise the wrong thing.

The problem is silent seam loss. There are 88 NA seam call sites inside 13 upstream-owned files and nothing guards any of them. Demonstrated, not asserted: deleting na_observe_econ_energy_sliders from gameturn.cpp gives a build with exit 0 and ZERO warnings, 43/43 wire tests passing, and check_native_choice_withheld.py passing. The observation simply stops happening and every gate stays green.

The sharpest contrast in the fork is the pattern that already works: na_base_hurry_observed is ONE line in patch.cpp and needed zero work across v5.5, while the in-body game.cpp seams cost the entire relocation exercise.

Note honestly what this epic does not buy: none of it would have made the v5.5 sync much cheaper — the turn-loop extraction had to be re-applied by hand either way. What it changes is whether the next one can fail quietly.
acceptance_criteria: Seams are machine-verified rather than remembered; the fork's presence inside upstream-owned files is materially smaller; drift against upstream is detected before it accumulates.
close_reason: All six children closed. Measured outcome across the fork: main.h NA footprint 251 added lines -> 9; main.cpp 159 -> 116; 69 seams + 17 helper definitions now machine-verified for presence, count and 7 ordering invariants, with the guard itself held to 10 mutations; NA option wiring guarded against silent default-reversion; weekly upstream drift CI added to the fork (its first CI) and NeuralAmplifier's own thinker-dll job un-broken (it had been building a branch frozen since 2026-07-29). Two children resolved as evidence-based decisions rather than code: na-alr.2 found the patch-table pattern does not generalise (na_base_hurry_observed needs BOTH no-args-reads-globals AND an existing patched call site; nothing else has both) and na-alr.4 was declined after measuring that its premise was false (3% of upstream commits touch those lines, none in v5.5). Spun out na-4zs (base.hurry observer bypassed on the production path). Analysis recorded in docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md sections 5.2 and 5.3 so it is not re-derived.

title: Get the merged fork back to a clean build and green wire tests
description:
The gate, and the reason the earlier beads can be checked at all.

Baseline measured on the fork BEFORE the merge, so this is a return-to-known-good, not a hope:
  cmake --preset develop && cmake --build --preset develop -j8
  -> exit 0, 25s, zero warnings.

Zero is the number that matters. The build runs -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wundef -Wuseless-cast -Wpointer-arith -Wfloat-conversion, so a merge that reintroduces a shadowed variable or a signature drift shows up as a warning long before it shows up as a crash in a game nobody can run in CI. Do not accept 'builds with a few warnings'.

Then the wire tests: tests/run-na-tests.sh. These are the part of the adapter that can regress without a game — src/na_http.cpp links no engine headers, so it builds standalone and runs under Wine against tests/na_http_server.py. They cover the HTTP/1.0-on-purpose behaviour, the read-until-EOF response handling, the single-field choices[].action_id scan, and that the client gives up on its OWN deadline rather than the server's.

Run the stub-only form here; --with-orchestrator additionally needs a NeuralAmplifier checkout with uv and is the stronger check if it is available (NA_DIR=/home/user/NeuralAmplifier).

Everything else in the adapter needs a real SMAC install and cannot be verified in this environment — say so plainly in the handoff rather than implying the merge is proven in-game.
acceptance_criteria: develop build exits 0 with zero warnings; tests/run-na-tests.sh passes under Wine; any check that could not be run in this environment is named explicitly as unrun.
close_reason: develop build: exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings under -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wundef -Wuseless-cast -Wpointer-arith -Wfloat-conversion — same as the pre-merge baseline. Wire tests under Wine: 38/38 stub-only, 43/43 with a live neural-amplifier serve including the POST /decide round-trip, the bare-JSON (non-chunked) reply check and the client-gives-up-on-its-own-deadline check. UNRUN in this environment: everything needing a real SMAC install — no terranx.exe fixture, so the DLL was never injected and no hook was observed firing in-game.

title: Re-point the NA patch-table entries at the renamed turn functions
description:
patch_setup() installs the hooks, and the rename invalidates our entries by name while leaving the addresses correct. Upstream already retargeted its own:

  write_call(0x52768A, (int)turn_upkeep);   // control_turn      (was mod_turn_upkeep)
  write_call(0x52A4AD, (int)turn_upkeep);   // net_control_turn  (was mod_turn_upkeep)
  write_jump(0x527290, (int)faction_upkeep);                     (new — faction_upkeep is now jumped, not called)

Ours to verify/keep:
  - write_call(0x4F7A38, (int)na_base_hurry_observed) — our observing wrapper standing in for mod_base_hurry at the base_upkeep call site. mod_base_hurry and mod_base_upkeep both still exist upstream, so this entry should survive; confirm upstream did not move the 0x4F7A38 site.
  - na_install_dialog_hook() at the head of patch_setup, before every write_call, unconditional by design (the wrapper reads conf.na_dialog_observe per call so the flag stays runtime-toggleable). Confirm it still precedes the first write_call after upstream's 140-line reshuffle of this file.
  - The three na_message_box() substitutions for MessageBoxA in init_video_config and the smac_only check — upstream touched neither site, but the merge moved lines around them.

Note the write_jump on faction_upkeep is a behavioural change on upstream's side: the whole engine function is now replaced rather than a single call intercepted. Nothing for us to do about it, but it is why the NA seams inside faction_upkeep must be in gameturn.cpp and not anywhere else.
acceptance_criteria: patch.cpp references no mod_turn_upkeep/mod_faction_upkeep/mod_production_phase/mod_allocate_energy; na_base_hurry_observed still installed at 0x4F7A38; na_install_dialog_hook still precedes the first write_call; all three na_message_box sites intact.
close_reason: patch.cpp references no stale mod_ turn names. Upstream's write_call(0x52768A/0x52A4AD, turn_upkeep) and write_jump(0x527290, faction_upkeep) came through the merge. na_base_hurry_observed still at 0x4F7A38; na_install_dialog_hook at line 405 still precedes the first write at 463; all three na_message_box sites intact.

title: Re-apply the NA turn-loop seams onto upstream's new gameturn.cpp
description:
The four turn functions our adapter instruments moved to src/gameturn.cpp and lost their mod_ prefix. Upstream REWROTE the bodies, so this is a re-application of our deltas onto new code, not a copy-paste of our old functions.

Every seam, with the placement constraint that makes it correct (each is load-bearing and already documented in-comment on our side — carry the comments over):

turn_upkeep()  [was mod_turn_upkeep, game.cpp:1010]
  - na_exit_turn_check()  — must be the FIRST statement, before the debug line, before init_world_config, and above all before *CurrentTurn is incremented ~40 lines down. On entry *CurrentTurn is the turn that just FINISHED, fully upkept and autosaved, so -na-exit-turn stops on exactly N complete turns.
  - na_announce_turn()    — immediately after it, never before: a run that is stopping must not publish a forecast for a turn it will not play.

faction_upkeep(faction_id)  [was mod_faction_upkeep, game.cpp:1557]
  - if (conf.na_odp_attack_policy) { na_odp_attack_upkeep(faction_id); do_all_non_input(); } — after enemy_strategy's do_all_non_input, before Thinker's AI planning routines.
  - corner market: hoist upstream's condition into 'na_cornered' and capture 'na_credits_before' BEFORE the f->energy_credits -= cost deduction, then na_observe_corner_market(faction_id, cost, na_credits_before, na_cornered) under conf.na_endgame_observe. The record must show what the decision was made against, not what survived it. Operands and their order must stay identical to upstream's.
  - council: call_council returns nothing useful, so the answer is observed as a STATE TRANSITION — sample STATE_COUNCIL_HAS_CONVENED before and after, and can_call_council only when observing so an unconfigured build pays nothing.

production_phase(faction_id)  [was mod_production_phase, game.cpp:1801]
  - na_accumulate_begin(faction_id) immediately before the f->best_mineral_output = 0 / energy_surplus_total = 0 / facility_maint_total = 0 zeroing, and na_accumulate_end(faction_id) as the last statement. mod_base_build fires inside that window, so a world view built there would otherwise report a half-summed total as faction income (na-an6).

allocate_energy(faction_id)  [was mod_allocate_energy, game.cpp:2071]
  - na_observe_econ_energy_sliders(faction_id) as the LAST statement. The function narrows SE_alloc_labs four times (energy_limit, the 0..10 clamp, two efficiency loops); anything earlier records a value the engine overwrites.

repair_phase(faction_id) carried no NA seam — confirm that is still true rather than assuming it.

gameturn.cpp will need #include "neural.h" (and "basewin.h" if the corner-market/council seams pull it in), mirroring what game.cpp had.
acceptance_criteria: All eight seams live in gameturn.cpp against upstream's rewritten bodies with their ordering comments intact; game.cpp no longer references na_exit_turn_check/na_announce_turn/na_odp_attack_upkeep/na_observe_corner_market/na_observe_council_call/na_accumulate_*/na_observe_econ_energy_sliders; grep confirms no NA seam was dropped in the move.
close_reason: All eight seams re-applied to upstream's rewritten bodies in gameturn.cpp with their ordering comments intact. repair_phase verified to carry none (grep of the saved pre-merge bodies: 0 na_ refs). game.cpp no longer references any of the relocated symbols.

title: Merge upstream v5.5 and resolve the three conflicts
description:
Land the merge itself on branch claude/thinker-upstream-sync-us8srt in the scbrown/thinker checkout.

Conflicts, all three of them, and what each actually is:

1. src/patch.cpp (1 hunk) — trivial. Our '#include "neural.h"' vs upstream reshuffling the include block. Keep both.

2. src/main.cpp (1 hunk) — our -na-autoload / -na-exit-turn / -na-auto-turn / -na-headless argv parsing against upstream's edits to the same wide-char argv walk. Ours is additive; keep every NA branch, rebased onto upstream's loop.

3. src/game.cpp (2 hunks):
   - lines 371-423: our na_exit_turn_check() + na_announce_turn() at the head of mod_turn_upkeep, versus upstream's custom_planet() which now occupies that region. Upstream MOVED turn_upkeep to gameturn.cpp; this hunk is a false neighbour, not a real overlap.
   - lines 2123-2670: 547 lines of ours (mod_faction_upkeep, mod_repair_phase, mod_production_phase, mod_allocate_energy) against an EMPTY upstream side, because upstream deleted them from game.cpp. Do NOT resolve by keeping our side — that would resurrect four functions upstream has rewritten and rehomed. Take upstream's deletion here; the NA seams inside them are re-applied in the sibling bead.

game.cpp keeps mod_name_base, whose four na_name_base_observed() calls merged clean and must survive (upstream's 'Refine base names' commit touches the same file).
acceptance_criteria: git merge upstream/master committed on claude/thinker-upstream-sync-us8srt with no conflict markers anywhere in src/; game.cpp retains its four na_name_base_observed calls; the four moved turn functions are gone from game.cpp.
close_reason: Merged upstream/master (v5.5) as b8c1fb8 on claude/thinker-upstream-sync-us8srt. All three conflicts resolved; no markers in src/. game.cpp keeps its four na_name_base_observed calls and no longer holds the four moved turn functions.

title: [epic] Sync the Thinker fork with upstream v5.5
description:
Upstream induktio/thinker released v5.5. Our fork (scbrown/thinker) sits at merge-base v5.4-5-gf660d9e with 67 NA commits on top; upstream is 6 commits / +5163 -2190 ahead.

The release is structural, not cosmetic. Upstream extracted the whole turn loop out of src/game.cpp into a new src/gameturn.cpp AND dropped the mod_ prefix from those functions:

  mod_turn_upkeep      -> turn_upkeep        (gameturn.cpp)
  mod_faction_upkeep   -> faction_upkeep     (gameturn.cpp, now a write_jump at 0x527290)
  mod_repair_phase     -> repair_phase       (gameturn.cpp)
  mod_production_phase -> production_phase   (gameturn.cpp)
  mod_allocate_energy  -> allocate_energy    (gameturn.cpp)

That is precisely where the NA adapter's turn-loop seams live, so a textually clean merge would still be a semantically broken one.

Trial merge (upstream/master into claude/thinker-upstream-sync-us8srt) conflicts in exactly three files: src/game.cpp (2 hunks), src/main.cpp (1), src/patch.cpp (1). Everything else merges clean.

Baseline before the merge: cmake --preset develop builds in 25s, exit 0, zero warnings. That is the gate to get back to.
acceptance_criteria: Fork merged with upstream v5.5; every NA seam re-applied to its new home; develop build exits 0 with zero warnings; NA wire tests pass under Wine; adapter notes' file:line citations updated.
close_reason: Fork synced with upstream Thinker v5.5 and back to baseline health. Merge b8c1fb8 + docs df408c6 on scbrown/thinker; adapter notes 0eeb093 on NeuralAmplifier, both on claude/thinker-upstream-sync-us8srt. The release moved the whole turn loop into gameturn.cpp and dropped the mod_ prefix, so all eight NA turn-loop seams were re-applied onto upstream's rewritten bodies rather than pasted back. Verified: develop build exit 0 with zero warnings under -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow (same as the pre-merge baseline), wire tests 43/43 under Wine against a live orchestrator including the POST /decide round-trip, all 23 llm_*/na_* options traced through the surviving parser. NOT verified: anything needing a real SMAC install — no terranx.exe fixture here, so the DLL was never injected and no hook was watched firing in a real game. That is the remaining risk and it is unchanged in kind by this sync.

title: policy.py accepts LLM-tier toggles on NO_AI_PATH surfaces
description: parse_surfaces validates surface ids against ALL only (policy.py:74-88), so '"base.abandon" = true' loads without complaint and allows() would consult the brain on a surface with no deterministic fallback — violating documented invariant 9 (the fallback-existence precondition). title: base.production sends the deterministic tier's answer to the LLM in the decision request
description:
MEASURED in thinker/src/neural.cpp while building na-qu8's eval. Production behaviour, not an eval artifact.

na_decide_base_production (:1339-1341) builds the request body with:

    na_build_base_production(&w, base_id, native_choice, has_gov, call_seq);

and na_build_base_production writes, UNCONDITIONALLY (:899, :905-906):

    ,"native_choice":<int>
    ,"native_choice_name":"<prod_name>"

`w` IS the POST body — the code says so itself at :1352: 'The record and the request body are
the same bytes, and they differ only by the outcome fields appended after the call returns.'

So on every base.production decision the model is told what the native AI would build, and then
asked what to build.

## The asymmetry is the evidence that this is a bug, not a design

base.hurry does the opposite, and does it deliberately. na_decide_base_hurry (:2288) passes
native_hurried = -1, and na_build_base_hurry writes native_choice only `if (native_hurried >= 0)`
(:2235-2236). The DECIDE path withholds the native answer; only the OBSERVE path (which passes 0)
records it. Somebody thought about exactly this hazard on one surface and used a sentinel to
suppress it. base.production has no such parameter.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

It is an ANCHOR on every measurement taken through this surface. na-6db asks whether LLM-tier
decisions produce better outcomes than the deterministic tier; agreement between the tiers is the
headline number there, and agreement with an answer you were shown is not evidence of independent
judgement. The confound points the same way as the hoped-for result, which is the worst direction.

It also silently weakens invariant-1 style reasoning: 'the model picked the legal thing' is less
impressive when the legal thing was named in the prompt.

## Fix, and the care it needs

Give na_build_base_production the same suppression base.hurry has — a sentinel that omits
native_choice/native_choice_name from the REQUEST while keeping them in the OBSERVATION record.
The two must stay distinguishable: the record needs the native answer (it is what 'llm chose X,
applied Y' is measured against); the request must not carry it.

DO NOT fix by stripping the field in the orchestrator. The adapter owns the payload (invariant 2)
and the record and request are built from the same buffer by design — splitting them in the
consumer would put the knowledge in the wrong component and leave the record depending on it.

## Blast radius on committed work

na-htm's 8 committed prompts contain native_choice (2 occurrences each). For its two
base.production decisions that is FAITHFUL to production and must not be silently 'fixed' — the
eval would then measure something we do not ship. For its faction.se / faction.tech decisions the
field may be an observe-only artifact and the prompts would be unfaithful; that needs the same
per-surface check done here. Either way na-uwp (the paid run) should not be spent until this is
settled, because both readings change what the money buys.

The three older evals are CLEAN (0 occurrences) — they use the hand-built harness fixture, which
predates captures.
close_reason: Fixed on ALL THREE affected surfaces, not just base.production: the per-surface check this bead asked for found faction.tech and faction.se anchoring too (base.hurry was the only guarded one of four). thinker 367b9b8 + NeuralAmplifier 66e62d8. Implemented with a bool, NOT base.hurry's sentinel — negative item ids are ordinary facilities (captured record carries native_choice -4) so a <0 sentinel would have stripped the field from every facility RECORD. VERIFICATION LIMIT, stated plainly: no SMAC install on this host, so the game lane cannot run and the builders cannot be exercised live. Verified by clean build, by a new mechanical guard (tests/check_native_choice_withheld.py, both arms proven), and end-to-end on the prompts: all 8 na-htm prompts now carry 0 native_choice, down from 2 each. na-uwp unblocked; na-6db's A/B is no longer measuring agreement with an answer the model was shown.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
FIXED — and the defect was WIDER than this bead. 2026-08-06, ellie.
thinker 367b9b8 (pushed to scbrown/thinker master) + NeuralAmplifier 66e62d8.

## The per-surface check this bead asked for — done, and it changed the scope

The bead says base.production, and notes faction.se/faction.tech "need the same per-surface
check done here". Ran it. **Three of the four decide surfaces sent the native answer**, not one:

| surface | decide path built the request with… | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| base.production | `na_build_base_production(..., native_choice, ...)` | ANCHORED — as filed |
| faction.tech | `na_build_faction_tech(&w, faction_id, native_choice)` — same builder as observe | **ANCHORED, unfiled** |
| faction.se | `na_build_faction_se(&w, ..., native_field, native_model, native_cost)` | **ANCHORED, unfiled** |
| base.hurry | passes `native_hurried = -1` | clean, and the reason we spotted it |

So the asymmetry the bead reads as evidence is real but understated: base.hurry is not the
exception to one bug, it is the only surface of four that was ever guarded. All three are fixed.

## The fix, and why it is a BOOL and not base.hurry's sentinel

This is the one place the bead's prescription could not be followed as written, and following it
would have caused a silent regression in the half we must keep.

`prod_name` asserts `item_id >= -SP_ID_Last && item_id < MaxProtoNum`, and **negative ids are
ordinary facilities** — this eval's own captured turn-135 record carries `native_choice: -4` for
Recycling Tanks. base.hurry can use `-1` because `native_hurried` is a tri-state over 1/0 with a
negative going spare; a production item id has no spare value. Suppressing on `native_choice < 0`
would have stripped the field from every FACILITY decision in the RECORD too.

So: `reveal_native`, a bool. false on the decide path, true on the probe and on
base.production's divergence report — both of which are records that are never posted.

The record keeps the native answer, appended after `na_http_post` returns, in the same place the
other outcome fields already go. The bead's constraint holds: the adapter owns the payload
(invariant 2), nothing was stripped in the orchestrator, and record and request stay
distinguishable — same buffer up to the send, divergent after it, which is the split the
existing "the record and the request body are the same bytes" comment already describes.

faction.se's `upheaval_cost` travels WITH its native pair: it prices the native move
specifically, so leaving it behind would hand over a priced hint at the withheld answer.
Measured: zero references to it anywhere in the orchestrator Python, so it is record context.

## Verification — and its honest limit

**Cannot be run end-to-end on this host: there is no SMAC install** (`../smac` absent, and
`adapters/thinker/scripts/` does not exist), so the game lane cannot execute. The wire lane
(`tests/run-na-tests.sh`) exercises `na_http_post` against a hand-written body and never calls
these builders, so it cannot see this either. Saying so rather than implying more.

What IS verified:

1. **Builds clean** (`cmake --build build/release`), all three surfaces.
2. **`tests/check_native_choice_withheld.py`** — a new mechanical guard, since the builders need
   a live engine. For each decide surface it asserts the build call into the POSTED buffer
   withholds, and the native emit appears AFTER the post. It keys on the buffer the post
   actually reads, so the record-only divergence buffer is correctly exempt, and it pins
   base.hurry's sentinel as an unchanged control. **Both arms proven** — reintroducing the bug
   on faction.tech turns it red.
3. **The prompts, end to end** — all 8 na-htm prompts now report 0 occurrences of
   `native_choice`, down from 2 each.

Two instrument bugs found while building that guard, both worth the warning: it first counted
braces inside string literals (`na_buf_puts(&w, "}")` ended the walk early, so it reported "no
na_http_post found" in a function that plainly has one), and its summary line printed a
hardcoded "reveal=false" regardless of what it measured. A checker that misreports in the
reassuring direction is worse than no checker.

## Blast radius, resolved rather than left open

The bead says na-htm's committed prompts are faithful for base.production and *maybe* artifacts
for faction.se/tech, and that na-uwp must not be spent until that is settled. **Settled by
measuring the adapter**: all three shipped it, so all 8 prompts were faithful-to-an-anchored-
production, and after this fix all 8 are UNFAITHFUL. Fixed in NeuralAmplifier 66e62d8 —
`OBSERVE_ONLY` in multi_decision_ranking, mirroring the tuple hurry_grounding already had, with
a selftest asserting it on the PROMPT TEXT (not the dict: `extra="allow"` means a stray field
survives `model_validate` and still reaches the model through `model_dump_json`).

No answers were committed, so this re-pin cost nothing. After a paid run it would have cost the
run — na-uwp was right to be blocked.

**na-6db is the bead that gains most**: its headline is agreement between the tiers, and until
now three surfaces were measuring agreement with an answer the model had been shown.

title: information_value is FLAT on real grounding — it splits the option name on an em dash no retriever emits
description:
Found while re-pinning na-htm after the na-dhs fix. MEASURED, not inferred.

`information_value(fact, label)` is the rule na-373 tested and na-htm exists to re-test. It
scores a fact by the words it adds BEYOND the option's own name. `rank_lines` derives that name
with:

    label_of(line) = line.split(" ", 1)[1].split(" — ")[0]

It splits on an EM DASH. Only na-373's hand-written VERBOSE fixture uses that separator. Every
fact a real retriever emits uses "; " — both `QuipuRetriever.format_row` and
`DatalinksRetriever.describe(compact=True)`.

So on real grounding `label_of` returns the WHOLE fact, `known` becomes every word in it, and
the only "fresh" words left are the id tokens:

    line     unit:colony-pod Colony Pod; founds a new base elsewhere; does not grow ...
    label_of 'Colony Pod; founds a new base elsewhere; does not grow the base th...'
    fresh    ['unit', 'colony-pod']        <- the ID PREFIX, not the content

Measured over all 40 facts pinned for na-htm across its four decisions:

    2 distinct scores in total:  score 2 x36,  score 1 x4

The rule is FLAT. And `rank_lines` sorts stably, so ranking 20 facts that all score 2 returns
them in retriever order unchanged. Confirmed on the artifacts: after the na-dhs re-pin took
base.production t135 from 7 to 20 facts, `.all.task.txt` changed and `.ranked.task.txt` DID NOT
— the ranked arm is still the first four units.

## Why this blocks na-uwp rather than being a tidy-up

The `ranked` arm is therefore not "the 4 most informative facts". It is "the first 4 in
action-space order". Both halves of the eval degrade to measuring action-space POSITION:

  - the choice half compares a truncation against its own prefix;
  - the citation-rank half asks where citations sat in an order that carries no information,
    so it measures whether the model cites early options.

na-htm's dominance gate would NOT catch this. The gate checks that no single fact or decision
owns the citation pool, which would still pass — the pool would be properly spread across four
decisions and be measuring the wrong thing anyway. Caught only by looking at the rule's own
output distribution, which is worth remembering: a guard catches the failure it was built for.

Same class as na-vbe's ("the fixture was never the payload") and na-61c2's ("an eval's arms are
part of the eval"). Third instance, so it is a pattern here, not an accident.

## The fix, and the care it needs

Take the option name as the text before the EARLIEST separator of EITHER kind (" — " or "; ").
That yields the right name for both formats:

    "Recycling Tanks — cost 4; Bonus Resources; needs Biogenetics"  -> "Recycling Tanks"
    "Colony Pod; founds a new base elsewhere; does not grow ..."    -> "Colony Pod"

Splitting on "; " FIRST would be wrong: it gives "Recycling Tanks — cost 4" on the verbose
format and quietly changes na-373's ranking.

CHANGING THIS CHANGES THE RULE UNDER TEST. It alters na-373's `ranked` arm, so its committed
answers stop being evidence about it — acceptable, since na-373 is already withdrawn AND already
stale (na-og3), but it must be recorded rather than absorbed. na-htm has no answers yet, so it
costs nothing there; re-pin and regenerate prompts after.

Verify the fix by DISTRIBUTION, not by the tests passing: re-run the 40-fact scoring above and
require substantially more than two distinct values. A rule that discriminates nothing is the
failure, so the check has to be that it discriminates.
close_reason: Fixed: label_of now ends the option name at the earliest separator of either kind. Verified by DISTRIBUTION as the bead required — 2 -> 12 distinct scores over the same 40 pinned facts, and all four na-htm decisions reorder. Guard added to selftest with both arms proven (reverting the fix turns it red). na-373 left STALE and recorded, not re-adjudicated; na-htm re-pinned at no cost. Commit 9e3391c.

and `fresh` on a real fact was `['unit', 'colony-pod']` — the id prefix, exactly as filed.

title: CI red on main: 8 mypy errors in the Orchestrator job (one root cause + one stray ignore)
description:
CI on scbrown/NeuralAmplifier main has been RED all day: three runs today (06:05, 06:10,
06:19 UTC), all the same failure. Three of four jobs pass — "Thinker adapter (MinGW
cross-compile)", "Pre-commit checks" and "Docs (lint + book)" are green. The failing job is
"Orchestrator (Python)", and it is mypy, not the test suite.

MEASURED via `gh api repos/scbrown/NeuralAmplifier/actions/jobs/<id>/logs` on the 06:19 run.
8 errors in 2 files (35 source files checked):

  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:161  Argument 1 to "get" of "dict" has incompatible type
                                     "tuple[str, object]"; expected "tuple[str, int | None]"
  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:165  Argument "faction_id" to "DecisionSlot" has incompatible
                                     type "object"; expected "int | None"
  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:166  Argument "base_id" to "DecisionSlot" ... "object" vs "int | None"
  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:167  Argument "base" to "DecisionSlot" ... "object" vs "str | None"
  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:169  Invalid index type "tuple[str, object]" for
                                     "dict[tuple[str, int | None], DecisionSlot]"
  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:177  Incompatible types in assignment, tuple[int, tuple[str, object]]
  src/neural_amplifier/turns.py:187  Argument 1 to "get" of "dict" ... "tuple[str, object]"
  src/neural_amplifier/service.py:565 Unused "type: ignore" comment  [unused-ignore]

Seven of the eight are ONE root cause, not seven: something upstream of the DecisionSlot key
construction in turns.py is typed `object` (very likely a dict value read out of an untyped

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND A RED BADGE: NeuralAmplifier has never been released, and a red main
is the reason a release cannot be cut. This is the "release lag is not neglect, the workflows
are broken" finding on aegis-e5vor, still true for this repo.
