comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
FINDING 2026-08-16 (Claude) — this looks already implemented. Not closing it: the bead is ellie's and was deliberately deferred by a human decision ("keep at P1 but verify before building"), so the status call is theirs. bd refused the close for the same reason, correctly.

The verification that note asked for, done by reading scbrown/thinker src/neural.cpp at 362052c. Both halves of the ask are live:

1. "Record what each base built over the last few turns and include it in the world view" — na_history_put / na_history_reset maintain a per-base ring buffer NA_HISTORY deep, and na_write_history emits it as the contract's `history` (WorldView.history / PriorChoice).

2. "Also record whether the current item was chosen by Claude or by the deterministic tier" — each ring entry carries a tier, emitted as llm | deterministic | null. Null is deliberate: it means this adapter cannot attribute the entry, rather than flattening an unknown into "deterministic".

Three details in that code worth not re-deriving:

- OLDEST FIRST, matching the contract and the system prompt. It was once emitted newest-first under the name `recent_builds`, which nothing mapped onto `history` — so WorldView.history was None on every real decision while the payload still arrived as an unexplained extra. A model applying the documented oldest-first reading to that undocumented block takes the OLDEST entry for the most recent choice, which is the na-eaa failure exactly.
- `item` is the action-space id ("unit:0" / "facility:4"), not the raw engine int, so a past choice matches an offered option exactly rather than by display name.
- Entries with turn >= CurrentTurn are skipped. mod_base_build fires several times per base-turn and the first call records this turn's choice before later ones serialise, so without the guard a seq>=2 record carries the answer to the question it is asking — which decision_stability.py would have re-fed to the brain and scored as stability.

WHAT REMAINS IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE BUILD. This bead's own revised note asks whether history actually reduces the flip rate given the measured 0.80 stability, and says that needs na-eaa's harness plus ten consecutive turns of real play. That is na-6db (does the LLM tier produce better outcomes) and na-mmp (needs a real game, not a fixture); both are open and both already say they need a game. So the honest read is: the implementation half of this bead is done, and the open question belongs to those two rather than here.

Suggested disposition for whoever owns it: close as implemented, or re-scope to the measurement and drop it to P2 behind na-mmp.

title: mod_base_build fires twice per base per turn - decide which call is authoritative
description:
Measured in real play on 2026-07-29 (26 observations, turns 2-5, six factions): every (turn, base_id) pair appears EXACTLY TWICE in na-observations.jsonl, and the two calls return different choices. Gaia's Landing on turn 2 produced both 'Scout Patrol' and 'Formers'.

Cause: mod_base_reset is hooked at eleven engine call sites (thinker src/patch.cpp:859-869) - bases_reset, base_production x5, and four BaseWin entry points - and each calls mod_base_build (src/base.cpp:998).

Why this blocks A1 rather than being cosmetic: orchestrator.py owns 'exactly one decision record per decision, on every path'. If the adapter POSTs on every mod_base_build call, one base-turn produces two LLM decisions - double-counted coverage, double-billed tokens, and two contradictory orders for the same slot. The engine is authoritative about what it asks; we have to decide what constitutes one decision.

Thinker fork commit bd1a6ea now records has_gov (mod_base_build's own second parameter) on each observation so the two calls are distinguishable. Next step is to collect a longer sample and determine whether has_gov alone separates them, or whether the call site must also be identified (which would mean passing a discriminator from each patch site).
design: Candidate rules, cheapest first: (1) has_gov distinguishes them cleanly - filter on it; (2) last-call-wins per (turn, base_id), since the final call is what mod_base_change actually applies; (3) identify the call site by passing a constant from each of the eleven patch sites. Prefer (1) or (2) - (3) touches eleven hook sites and couples the adapter to engine layout.
acceptance_criteria: A rule is documented for which mod_base_build invocation is the decision of record; the adapter emits one observation per decision per base-turn, or emits all of them with a field that unambiguously marks the authoritative one; validated against a sample of at least 20 turns
notes:
VERIFIED in real play 2026-07-29, and the original framing was wrong in an important way.

Sample: 50 base.production records, turns 26-34, 38 distinct (turn, base_id) groups.

  call_seq values seen:      1 x38, 2 x10, 3 x2
  calls per (turn,base):     once x28, twice x8, three times x2
  call_seq unique in group:  38 of 38, zero collisions
  records with call_seq==1:  38 - exactly one per distinct base-turn

So gating on call_seq == 1 provably yields exactly one decision per base-turn. A1's
one-paid-call guarantee holds, and the invariant 'exactly one decision record per
decision' is satisfiable.

CORRECTION to the earlier finding. The title says 'fires twice per base per turn'.
It does not - it fires ONE to THREE times, and most often only once (28 of 38 groups).
The first sample happened to catch a turn where duplication was universal, which made
a variable phenomenon look constant.

This matters concretely: any rule of the form 'take the second call' or 'take the last
call' would have MISSED 28 of 38 decisions entirely, because for those groups there is
no second call. call_seq == 1 is correct precisely because it is the only invocation
guaranteed to exist for every base-turn. Had we settled on last-call-wins - which was
the leading theory and sounded principled - A1 would have silently skipped three
quarters of its decisions.
close_reason: Resolved and verified. call_seq is unique within every base-turn group (38/38, no collisions) and exactly one record per base-turn has call_seq==1, so gating on it gives one decision per base-turn. Also corrected the premise: the engine fires 1-3 times, not always twice, and most often once - so a last-call-wins rule would have missed 28 of 38 decisions.

title: K1: Quipu datalinks read path and static briefing
description: Implement Retriever against Quipu: smac shapes, alphax.txt to episode ingester, cached-once static briefing prompt-cached at game start. Exit: a Thinker static briefing is Quipu-sourced. Seam exists in knowledge.py; this fills it. knowledge-architecture.md K1.
close_reason: Landed less the Quipu round-trip. datalinks/ parses alphax.txt deterministically (no model: it is fixed-arity CSV with inline column docs, and a hallucinated tech prerequisite tagged canonical is the worst failure available to us), emits the smac: graph with all three anti-masquerade predicates on every node, and serves a static briefing plus action-space-scoped grounding through the Retriever seam. Verified against a real 1281-line alphax.txt: 88 techs, 133 facilities (50 Disabled), 64 SP rows, 2579 triples round-tripping through rdflib. Three bugs found by checking rather than eyeballing: (1) two facilities have commas inside effect text, so SP detection had to move from row arity to 'last five fields are ints'; (2) Turtle PN_LOCAL forbids '/', so smac:tech/biogen was a parse error that looked perfectly reasonable -- fixed with per-class prefixes and rdflib is now a dev dep gating it; (3) Disable in a preq column means excluded-from-game, not a prerequisite, and treating it as a tech would have invented 50 fake edges. Also: alphax.txt's own header calls the facility column 'Free' (grants the facility free at new bases), not obsoletedBy as knowledge-architecture.md says -- the file wins, noted in rdf.py. Added NA_EXTRACTION_MODEL (default claude-haiku-4-5) as a separate cheaper dial from the brain's, for K3's postgame episode extraction which IS genuine model work. Remaining: load the graph into a running Quipu and serve retrieval from it rather than the parsed structs -- folded into na-6ce (K2). 21 tests against a synthetic excerpt; the real alphax.txt is game data and is never committed.

title: Decide the slot mode and wire manage_player_bases/units
description: Mode B+ is the recommendation: human slot with conf.manage_player_bases and manage_player_units, giving fair rules plus a deterministic tier. Two gaps the LLM must own outright because no AI path runs for a human faction: energy sliders (game.cpp:1908 returns early) and social engineering (faction.cpp:1463 hard-returns). docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md section 5.0.

Mode B+ recommended and documented at the option in thinker.ini. Verified by MinGW cross-compile to a PE32 DLL. Intercepting an actual decision is A1 (na-61c).

title: A0 spike: log one mod_base_build decision under Wine
description: First real decision point observed. mod_base_build at thinker src/base.cpp:1145 is the cleanest seam: one int in, one int out, self-contained. Depends on the fixture and the harness.
notes:
Hook implemented and shipped: thinker fork commit 78a5af3 adds src/neural.{h,cpp} and calls na_observe_base_production from mod_base_build (src/base.cpp), gated on llm_enabled. Writes one JSON line per decision to na-observations.jsonl in the game directory, with surface_id=base.production, turn, faction, base, and Thinker's native choice. Observation only - native choice still executes, so no behaviour change.

Build and boot are verified: cross-compiles clean under i686 MinGW with -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow, produces PE32 i386, and drives the Steam terranx.exe under Wine 11.9 + Xvfb with the DLL attached (audio confirmed by Steve, so the game genuinely runs).

Producing a line needs either a human to load a game and end a turn, or the -na-autoload flag from na-ie9. That is the only thing standing between here and closing this issue.

Full chain proven: fork cross-compiled on Linux, PE32 i386 DLL attached to the Steam Alien Crossfire terranx.exe under Wine, real game, real decision points logged. title: Wine plus Xvfb headless harness for unattended runs
description: Canned save plus thinker.ini plus -na-autoload / -na-endpoint / -na-exit-turn flags added to cmd_parse. Hard timeout required: Thinker reports fatal errors via MessageBoxA, which under Xvfb hangs forever with nobody to click OK. Run windowed, not fullscreen. docs/headless-harness.md section 3.
notes:
Partially delivered as of 2026-07-29 (commit e78d07a + fork 78a5af3).

DONE - the Wine + Xvfb half:
  - scripts/setup-host.sh installs the i686 cross-compiler, wine, xvfb, cmake>=3.31
  - scripts/play-thinker.sh builds the fork, installs it, and launches, via just thinker-play [headless]
  - Uses its own prefix (~/.local/share/na-wine), never Steam's Proton prefix
  - Verified: the fork boots the Steam terranx.exe under Wine 11.9 + Xvfb, no visible display
  - Correction to an assumption in scripts/setup-environment.sh: a WINEARCH=win32 prefix is NOT
    required on Wine 9+, which runs 32-bit binaries in a default 64-bit prefix via new-wow64.

REMAINING - the menus half, which was always the real blocker (section 3.1):
  - -na-autoload <save>, now best implemented against the in-tree mod_load_daemon(char*, int)
    from upstream f660d9e rather than the raw engine address 0x5A9760
  - -na-exit-turn <n> so an unattended run terminates on its own
  - Fatal-error MessageBoxA suppression only (never blanket-suppress dialogs - invariant 7)
  There is a savegame available to test against: saves/auto/Autosave_2234.sav in the play dir.
close_reason: Unattended runs advance turns and terminate on their own, verified live: turn 1->2->3 with auto_end_turn_returned (unreachable before the fix), and -na-exit-turn 3 from a turn-4 save exited the process on its own. Blocker was the engine's OPERATIONS DIRECTOR unmoved-units modal, seen by photographing the frozen display; fixed by Console_skip-ing units with movement left so the dialog never opens. thinker 2929637, NeuralAmplifier a2baab2.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
LIVE VERIFICATION DONE, and it found a bug that made the whole headless lane a no-op.
Fix pushed: NeuralAmplifier 6fccfae (scripts/play-thinker.sh).

FIRST: this host DOES have the game. na-b4v recorded "no SMAC bytes on this host
(../smac absent; fixtures/smac holds only PROVENANCE.md, overlays.tsv, manifest)". That is
true of the PRISTINE FIXTURE and false of the PLAY DIRECTORY, which is the distinction
docs/headless-harness.md 2.4 exists to draw. Measured:

  ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri/terranx.exe
  sha1 7bbcc54e64760c11a24f48862f15dbaaeab61435, 3094576 bytes
  = the documented known-good Steam v2.0 binary (harness doc 2.1), Thinker installed alongside.

So the NA lane is NOT blocked on absent game bytes. $SMAC_DIR is unset and the fixture is
absent; the play dir is present and playable. Anything that concluded "blocked, no game"
from the fixture path should be re-checked.

THE BUG. play-thinker.sh headless could not run a game at all:

  timeout 120 xvfb-run -a ... wine thinker.exe -na-autoload <save> -na-exit-turn 2
  -> LAUNCHER rc=0 elapsed=3s
     XIO: fatal IO error 2 on X server ":99" ... explicit kill or server shutdown
     na-observations.jsonl 248 lines before, 248 after

thinker.exe is an injector, not a supervisor (fork src/launch.cpp:110-118): CreateProcess
suspended, inject, ResumeThread, return 0. It never waits on terranx.exe. xvfb-run kills its
display when ITS command returns, so the game died ~3s in - below the autoload state
machine's own 12s wait for startup to FINISH, so it had not yet acted. The run then printed
"no new observations", advising a check of llm_factions/manage_player_bases: config advice
for an already-dead process.

Attended mode hid it. With no xvfb-run to kill the display the game survives as an orphan
and plays on, so only the report was premature. The mode a human watches is the mode that
worked - which is also why the 45 pre-existing na.autoload records did not expose it.

FIX: wineserver -w after the launch (blocks until every process in our own prefix exits).
Plus NA_EXIT_TURN (forwards -na-exit-turn; the flag existed in the DLL with nothing at the
launcher layer able to set it) and NA_TIMEOUT (default 1800s headless, off attended -
harness doc 3.3 calls a hard timeout mandatory and there was none).

AFTER, same command and same save - the autoload sequence completing against a real game
under Xvfb for the first time:

  ELAPSED=423s (the full timeout, not 3s)
  na.autoload hook_alive -> click_quickstart -> confirm_planetfall
  na.autoload loaded  saves/auto/Autosave_2144.sav status=0 halted:0 turn:44

REMAINING HALF OF THIS BEAD - an unattended run still cannot advance a turn.
The run above TIMED OUT rather than stopping itself, and -na-exit-turn is not at fault.
Evidence it never got the chance: no new autosave (newest still 22:40:59, pre-run),
no decision record, no na.exit_turn record, in 7 minutes of live session. The save loads
at the HUMAN's turn and nothing ends it -> mod_turn_upkeep never fires -> na_exit_turn_check
never runs. Seam: Console_end_my_turn, engine.cpp:2177 (0x5169F0), an in-process call in the
same spirit as autoload using mod_load_daemon directly. Note harness doc 3.0.2: the in-game
map UI reads DirectInput and IGNORES PostMessage, so a synthesised keystroke is not the route.

SEMANTIC TRAP worth knowing: -na-exit-turn is an ABSOLUTE turn number
(na_exit_turn_check tests *CurrentTurn >= na_exit_turn). Resuming a save at turn 44 with
limit 2 means "already past", not "two more turns".

Ingested to quipu separately.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
SECOND FINDING: the end-turn seam BLOCKS. Console_end_my_turn does not return.

Built -na-auto-turn (thinker 64cd542) + NA_AUTO_TURN (NeuralAmplifier 94f62ca): a STALL
timer that ends our own turn after N seconds of a live session in which *CurrentTurn has
not moved, via the engine's own Console_end_my_turn(MapWin) rather than a synthesised
keystroke (harness doc 3.0.2: the in-game map UI reads DirectInput and IGNORES posted
window messages). Builds clean, PE32 i386.

MEASURED, headless, save at turn 44, -na-auto-turn 25 -na-exit-turn 46, ~10 minutes:

  na.autoload  loaded         saves/auto/Autosave_2144.sav status=0 halted:0 turn:44
  na.autoload  auto_end_turn  Console_end_my_turn                            turn:44
  (nothing further)

ONE auto_end_turn record, then silence. That is the finding. A 25s stall timer still
running would have logged ~20 records in that window; none appeared, no autosave was
written, and the turn did not advance. So the call DID NOT RETURN — it is not that ending
the turn was refused or ignored, it is that control never came back to us.

This is exactly the hazard harness doc 3.0.2 predicted for anything reached from the
window procedure: a modal dialog freezes every thread we have, including workers. The
likely modal is the "units still have moves remaining" confirmation. Note the shape of
the evidence: the log write is placed immediately BEFORE the call precisely so that a call
which never returns still leaves its attempt as the last line. That is what turned a
10-minute silent hang into a one-line diagnosis, and it is why the flag is committed
rather than deleted - it is the instrument as well as the feature.

STATUS: -na-auto-turn ships OFF by default and KNOWN NOT TO WORK. I have deliberately not
claimed it works; the commit message says so in the subject line.

UNTESTED NEXT HYPOTHESIS (recorded as a hypothesis, not a conclusion):
PREF_BSC_PAUSE_END_TURN, engine_enums.h:437. The play dir has NO Alpha Centauri.ini, so
the game runs on default preferences and whether that bit is among them was NOT
established. Other candidates: Console_end_of_turn (0x513FC0) as a different seam, or
clearing the units-with-moves state before calling so no prompt is raised.

WHAT IS NOW TRUE THAT WAS NOT THIS MORNING:
  - the headless lane runs a real game at all (was a 3s no-op; fix 6fccfae)
  - -na-autoload is verified live end-to-end under Xvfb (save loads, session live, turn 44)
  - the harness has the hard timeout doc 3.3 called mandatory
  - the reason -na-exit-turn never fires is known, measured, and is NOT -na-exit-turn
STILL OPEN: an unattended run cannot advance a turn. That is the whole of what remains on
this bead, and it is now a single well-characterised blocker rather than "the menus half".

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
SOLVED. An unattended run now loads a save, advances turns, and stops itself.

THE BLOCKER, SEEN RATHER THAN INFERRED. Photographed the frozen Xvfb display. The game was
sitting on its own dialog:

    OPERATIONS DIRECTOR
    Some of our units have not yet moved this turn. Do you really want to end the turn now?
      Cancel. / Yes, end the turn. / OK

Same screenshot also gave the first direct confirmation the harness works at all: map
rendered, Colony Pod selected, Mission Year 2101, TURN COMPLETE lit. The run was never
broken - it was waiting to be asked a question.

TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT CLOSED OFF THE ALTERNATIVES:
  1. terranx sat at ~55% CPU while "frozen" - NOT blocked, running the dialog's own nested
     pump. ModWinProc is simply not called, so nothing of ours runs and the call never returns.
  2. An xdotool click on "Yes, end the turn." against a live frozen instance changed NOTHING.
     That EXTENDS harness doc 3.0.2 (measured there on the file picker) to the game's OWN
     dialogs. Neither in-process nor external input is available.

So the fix removes the reason for the dialog instead of answering it: Console_skip on every
unit of the current faction with movement left (engine's own moves_spent vs veh_speed). By
the time we ask to end the turn there are no unmoved units. That is 3.0.2's rule applied -
never open a modal - not an exception to it. Skipping units IS a gameplay decision and is
tied to -na-auto-turn deliberately: a run ending its own turns has nobody to move units.

VERIFIED LIVE, headless, real game:
    auto_end_turn           turn=1  Console_end_my_turn after skipping 3 unit(s)
    auto_end_turn_returned  turn=1          <- unreachable before the fix

title: energy_income and labs_output are pinned on a base-scope fixture the adapter cannot produce
description:
`energy_income` and `labs_output` are declared faction-scope in metrics.py, and the vocabulary
test says the faction half "goes on every surface" — but a live game emits them on NO base-scope
world view. The pinned fixture carries them anyway, so the contract test is green against a
record the adapter cannot produce.

MEASURED (harding, 2026-08-22, live game, thinker 70e488d), one run's world views:

| surface | records | energy_income / labs_output present |
|---|---|---|
| base.hurry | 136 | **0** |
| base.production | 33 | **0** |
| faction.se | 3 | 3 |

Control: every other faction-scope name (`base_count`, `pop_total`, `military_units`,
`drone_total`, `units_in_foreign_territory`, `energy_reserves`, `factions_at_war`) is present on
all 172. So this is specific to these two names, not a broken capture.

WHY, and the adapter is RIGHT: `na_write_metrics` omits both while a faction's totals are
mid-accumulation (na-an6, neural.cpp). `mod_production_phase` zeroes the running totals and
re-accumulates them base by base, and `mod_base_build` fires inside that window — so a
base-scope world view would see a PARTIAL sum. Absent is unambiguous; a half-summed income
reads as a real number, and 0 is a value the vocabulary genuinely admits since na-s4e.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG is the pin and the claim around it:

  - `tests/fixtures/thinker_base_production.json` carries `energy_income: 11, labs_output: 9` on
    a base.production record. The adapter cannot emit that.
  - `test_metrics_vocabulary.py`'s comment: "the faction half goes on every surface". Not for
    these two.
  - `test_adapter_contract.py::test_every_faction_metric_in_the_vocabulary_is_actually_reported`
    asserts every faction-scope name appears in every pinned record — true of the pins, false of
    the game.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the failure this vocabulary exists to prevent: a directive or queued
predicate written on `energy_income` is accepted at issue time and reads UNMEASURABLE on every
base decision for the rest of the game. Unmeasurable is not unsatisfied — it means nobody
checked — so a plan that steers nothing is indistinguishable from one being followed. The test
built to catch exactly this is looking at a hand-made record instead of a captured one.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, and it needs a ruling rather than a patch:

  (a) Teach the contract the exception — a `scopes_absent_when` or per-metric note saying these
      two are faction-scope AND unavailable on base surfaces, with the tests asserting that
      rather than universal presence. Honest, and makes the omission a documented property.
  (b) Give them a base-scope-safe value. Not obviously possible: the totals genuinely do not
      exist mid-accumulation.

(a) looks right. (b) would mean inventing the number na-an6 deliberately refused to invent.

WORTH NOTING SEPARATELY: the fixtures are hand-maintained, and that is what let this drift.
Every value in `thinker_base_production.json` (base_count 1, pop_total 4) is a written scenario,
not a capture. `scripts/harvest-world-views.py` exists to capture real ones — and na-0oa says it
cannot see the adapter log, which is plausibly why nobody has.

title: thinker-emit gap: at_war, enemy_near, tile and unit-damage predicates that na-7bk slices 2 and 3 must refuse
description:
Slices 2 and 3 of na-7bk restrict queued-answer predicates and unit-intent review triggers to
`metrics.py`'s measured vocabulary — names an adapter actually emits. That restriction is
deliberate and correct: an unmeasurable predicate can never fire, so a standing answer built on
one keeps answering forever, degrading into exactly the hardcoded script the mechanism exists not
to be.

The cost is that three of the four predicates the design comments give as EXAMPLES are refused
today, and the gap is in thinker, not in the orchestrator.

| named in the na-7bk design | expressible | why not |
|---|---|---|
| `surplus collapses`, `drone riot` | yes | `mineral_surplus`, `drone_total` are emitted |
| escort strength, reserves draining | yes | `military_units`, `energy_reserves` |
| `at_war` / war state change | **no** | no adapter emits it |
| `enemy unit within N tiles of path` | **no** | needs a tile model the orchestrator deliberately does not have |
| `destination tile ownership changed` | **no** | same |
| `unit damaged below X` | **no** | per-unit state is not in the base surfaces' world view |

THE CHEAP ONE IS `faction.at_war`. It is faction-scope state the engine already holds, it needs
no tile model, and it unlocks the design's most-cited predicate. Emit it as a metric on the
faction surfaces and add the name to `metrics.py`'s vocabulary — in that order, because a
vocabulary name nothing populates reintroduces the exact failure the restriction prevents.

THE OTHERS ARE A DESIGN QUESTION, NOT A TASK. Tile proximity and per-unit damage need board state
the orchestrator does not model, and na-7bk's own fog comment says it deliberately should not:
door 2's move refuses an unexplored destination via the engine's own `is_known`, and the engine
gate is meant to be the only tile gate. So "make enemy_near expressible" is really "should the
orchestrator have a tile model at all", and that should be ruled on rather than implemented by
whoever picks this up.

DO NOT close this by widening `metrics.py` alone. A name in the vocabulary that no world view
carries produces predicates that never fire, which is worse than the refusal it replaces —
slice 2 already has four fail-closed stops, and one of them exists precisely because an answer
standing on an unread instrument is an answer standing on nothing.
close_reason: factions_at_war emitted (thinker 70e488d) and in the vocabulary (NA eef1bc6), in the emit-first order metrics.py requires. Measured live: present on 172/172 world views across three surfaces, 0/862 before. A count not a flag so a second front is visible; commlink-gated for fog; better=None. Three tests including a peace/war control pair and an absent-metric fail-closed case, proven by mutation. The other three predicates (enemy_near, tile ownership, unit damage) stay refused as the bead framed them — they need a tile model the orchestrator deliberately does not have. Fixture drift found in passing: na-095.

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Closed — `factions_at_war` emitted and usable (harding)

thinker `70e488d` on origin/master; NA `eef1bc6` on `wt/harding`. Done in the order this repo's
own metrics doctrine requires: **emit it from the adapter first, add the name second.**

### The cheap one, done

`na_write_metrics` sweeps `Factions` with the engine's own `at_war()`, commlink-gated, and emits
`factions_at_war`. Measured on a live game:

| | world views carrying it |
|---|---|
| after the change | **172 of 172** — base.hurry, base.production and faction.se alike, reporting 1 |
| before, same store, same run series | **0 of 862** |

A clean before/after control, not a claim.

**A count, not a flag, and the tests carry the reason.** The comparators are numeric, so a
boolean supports "is at war" and nothing more — while the design asks to re-raise when the war
state CHANGES. An answer conditioned on a flag stops on the first war and then stands through
every escalation, and a second front is exactly the change a standing plan should not survive.
Zero is peace with no special case.

**Commlink-gated**, the same fog rule `units_in_foreign_territory` follows: a faction we have
never met must not reach a number the brain reads even as an increment, because that is the
existence of a faction leaking through a count. Vendetta implies contact in practice, so this
should change nothing — which is not a reason to omit a fog gate from a fog-relevant sweep.

`better` is None, matching `military_units`: fewer fronts is safer, more is sometimes the plan,
and the trigger fires on the number moving rather than on which way is good.

### What it unblocks, asserted rather than asserted-about

Three tests in `test_queued.py`. The middle one carries its own control: at peace the standing
answer holds and the brain is not woken; `factions_at_war: 1` re-raises it and the advisory says
`factions_at_war is 1`. The third asserts an ABSENT metric also stops the answer — fail-closed
matters more for this name than for an economic one, being the difference between a build plan
surviving an invasion because nobody checked and stopping because nobody could.

Proven by mutation: remove the vocabulary entry and two of the three fail; restored, control
green. 866 orchestrator tests pass (+3), ruff, mypy and the docs lint clean.

### The other three predicates stay refused, and this bead said they would

`enemy_near`, tile ownership and unit damage are unchanged. They need board state the
orchestrator deliberately does not model — na-7bk's fog comment is explicit that the engine's
`is_known` is meant to be the only tile gate — so "make them expressible" is a ruling about
whether the orchestrator gets a tile model at all, not a task. Left exactly as the bead framed
it.

### Found while capturing real values: na-095

`energy_income` and `labs_output` are declared faction-scope and appear on **0 of 169** live
base-scope world views, because the adapter deliberately omits them mid-accumulation (na-an6).
The pinned base.production fixture carries both, so the contract test is green against a record
the adapter cannot produce — and a directive on `energy_income` reads UNMEASURABLE on every base
decision, which is the precise failure the vocabulary exists to prevent. Filed as **na-095**
with the measurement and two candidate fixes; it needs a ruling, not a patch, and it is not this
bead's.

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Fixed in `616c75a` — and the root cause reaches further than the report (harding)

Reproduced your two commands exactly, in a clean worktree with the same log and store copied in.
Same result: 0 vs 339. It is not arg-passing vs cwd vs env — it is the `../{{log}}` prefix in
the recipe, and there are **two** ways to land on a file that is not there.

### 1. `log=<path>` is not a named argument

`log` is a recipe PARAMETER, not a justfile variable, so `name=value` is not an override — just
binds the whole string as the positional value. Probed directly:

    ARG1=../log=orchestrator/decisions.jsonl

So the command opened a file literally called `log=orchestrator/decisions.jsonl`. Nothing about
the output said so.

### 2. And the BARE invocation was broken too — including on a recipe nobody had checked

The defaults were `decisions.jsonl` / `worldviews`, resolved against `orchestrator/` by the
`../` prefix, i.e. the **repo root**. But `just play serve` runs under `uv run --directory
orchestrator`, so the producer writes `orchestrator/decisions.jsonl`. The producer and the
consumers have never agreed on where the recording lives.

    just replay      ->  decisions: 0  + "FAIL: nothing was replayed…"
    just coverage    ->  decisions: 0, degrade_rate: 0.0, fair_play: true,
                         fog_enforced: true,  EXIT 0

**The second line is the one that was not filed and it is the worse of the two.** The justfile
describes `coverage` as failing "if the brain was largely absent or an illegal action slipped
through". On a missing file it passed **green**, asserting fair play and enforced fog over a log
it never opened. Your `replay` zero at least stopped you; this one hands a clean bill of health
to any CI job or human who runs the documented default. Your bead's framing — *the failure
direction is the bad one* — is exactly right, and it applies harder one recipe over.

Third path, quietest of the three: `WorldViewStore.__init__` mkdirs its root. Correct on the
recording side, where the run owns the directory. Here it meant a typo'd `--store` made replay
**manufacture the empty store it then blamed** — "the store has none of the log's inputs" was a
true sentence about a directory replay had just created itself.

### The fix

- `missing_input()` in `cli.py`, applied by `coverage`, `learn` and `replay` **before anything
  is constructed**, so the store check runs while there is still nothing to create. Names the
  path, says which of the two things is wrong, exit 2.
- `replay` now separates an **empty log** from a **store mismatch**. They want opposite next
  moves — an empty log means the recording did not happen, and the store is a wasted search —
  and one message covered both.
- The justfile anchors paths at `justfile_directory()`; defaults point where the producer
  writes. `log=<path>` is still not a named argument (that is just's grammar, not ours), but it
  now fails with `decision log does not exist: …/log=orchestrator/decisions.jsonl`, which makes
  the mistake self-evident rather than looking like an empty recording.
- `README.md` said `just replay --store …`, which would have passed `--store` as the positional
  log. Fixed; bare `just replay` now works.

### Verified

| invocation | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `just replay` | 0 + FAIL | **339 / 325, exit 0** |
| `just coverage` | 0, **exit 0** | **339** |
| `just coverage <missing>` | green, exit 0 | FAIL naming the path, exit 2, no verdict printed |
| `just replay log=<path>` | 0 + FAIL | FAIL naming `log=<path>` literally, exit 2 |
| `just replay <log> <typo-store>` | 0 + FAIL, dir created | FAIL naming it, **dir NOT created** |
| real log, genuinely empty store | correct message | correct message — unchanged |

That last row is the positive control: every other case here asserts an error appears, which is
the exact shape that also passes when a command has been broken into refusing everything.

Three mutations, three failures, restored, control green. 863 orchestrator tests pass (+8), ruff,
mypy and the docs lint clean.

### Your section 2 baseline stands, and is now reachable by the documented recipe

`just replay` on this tree reproduces your direct-CLI numbers exactly — 339 decisions, 325
replayed, 29 matched, 296 diverged, 14 missing inputs. The 14 absent world-view hashes are still
there and still point at na-0oa as you said.

From tonight's live human-vs-LLM session (Stiwi as Peacekeepers, agent playing 6 AI factions): per-decision agent latency (~30-60s wake+reason+submit) makes the AI round painfully slow, and door 1 cannot batch (adapter blocks synchronously in mod_base_build; N+1 does not exist until N is answered - turn-scoped-play.md section 3).

Interim shipped tonight, outside the repo: /tmp/na-executor.py - a deterministic executor that claims each decision ({"wait":60}) and answers in ms from (1) a hot-reloaded plan table /tmp/na-turn-plan.json keyed "Faction:Base" -> action_id, else (2) a policy (finish tc<=3 items; Morgan hab-cap fix; Formers when surplus<=2; small-base Recycling/Creche; faction infra preference; SE no-change; conservative default on unknown surfaces, flagged). Coordinator reviews outcomes and writes plan overrides between turns - strategy set once per turn, zero blocking.

Proper build (this bead): move the plan store into the orchestrator - POST /agent/plan installing a per-turn decision table + policy, with AgentBrain answering from it and queueing only uncovered decisions to the attached agent. The GET /turn forecast (phases 1-4 built, na-8ja) is the natural companion: agent reads the forecast, submits the plan, done. Keep decisions.jsonl recording tier=plan vs tier=llm so replay can tell strategy-driven answers from agent-driven ones.

comments.author: sattler
comments.text:
## Investigation: is there a "w"/wait for door-1 decisions? (sattler, 2026-08-21)

Stiwi asked whether thinker exposes something like SMAC's "w" (wait - defer a unit, cycle returns to it later) for turn decisions.

**Engine answer: no, and it cannot at the hook.** mod_base_build's signature is one int in, one int out - na_decide_base_production's own comment: "nowhere to park a decision and resume it later" (neural.cpp:1444, verified in source). The engine consumes an item id synchronously on its own thread. "w" exists only for unit cycling in the engine's input loop, which is a different surface than the decision hook.

**But the defer SEAM exists, made of three things already built and verified in source:**
1. Every /decide failure path returns native_choice - the deterministic tier's pick - as invariant-9 control flow. So "no answer" is already a safe provisional answer.
2. base.production is a revisable queue write, last-write-wins (turn-scoped-play.md section 6), and the engine re-asks bases within a turn (21/24 base-turns fired twice, measured upstream).
3. Door 2's build verb (Phase 2, BUILT) sets any base's item directly, refreshes the adapter's per-base cache so a door-1 replay cannot undo it, and reads the item back after mod_base_change.

## Proposed mechanism: DEFERRED DECISIONS (the long-term replacement for tonight's /tmp executor hack)

- Adapter (thinker): recognize {"action_id":"defer"} in the /decide reply -> apply native_choice, record tier=deferred (not deterministic - the distinction is the whole point), do NOT treat as an error. Today an unparseable id already lands on native_choice, so the wire behavior degrades compatibly on old DLLs.
- Orchestrator (NA): a deferred decision stays OPEN in a pending-review set instead of closing. New surface: GET /agent/pending (deferred decisions with grounded world views) + the agent resolves each via the existing POST /order build verb; the orchestrator marks the deferral resolved and links the outcome record. Unresolved by the next turn's /turn forecast -> closed as deferred-expired (engine's choice stood), recorded honestly.
- Agent contract: the agent brain auto-replies "defer" after a SHORT deadline (or immediately in bulk mode), then the attached agent reasons at its own pace - grounded via NA_QUIPU_URL retrieval - and sweeps the pending set once per turn. Game never blocks; decisions stay thought-out; decisions.jsonl distinguishes tier=llm (answered live) / tier=deferred->revised (answered via door 2) / deferred-expired.
- SE/dialog surfaces: defer = no-change now; they re-fire per faction-turn anyway.

## Prerequisites and notes
- na-nnn blocks any new thinker build: current master (020d68c) dies at launch with the draw-buffer fatal; tonight's play runs on pre-v5.5 2b39bdc. Bisect the v5.5 merge first.
- Door-2 order gating refuses halted/not-routed (neural.cpp:3505-3509); AI factions are routed here (llm_factions=126), but revision timing vs the AI turn sweep needs a live test: a revision landing after a base processed applies to next turn's minerals - acceptable for multi-turn builds, must be recorded not assumed.
- Grounding is live as of tonight: local quipu store (.quipu/na.db, datalinks graph) served at 127.0.0.1:3030, orchestrator restarted with NA_QUIPU_URL - preflight all-green. The deferred-review flow should show the retrieved knowledge in the pending view, which it already does since grounding happens before the brain.

comments.text:
## Design extension: INTENT LAYER (Stiwi's direction, 2026-08-21 late session)

Stiwi: queue certain decision types - a unit destination many turns out, an overall intent for a
unit - preserve that intent via quipu, and queue decisions that can be changed later ONLY if a
tactical response is needed.

### What already exists (verified in source tonight)
- memory.py (K3): decision log -> mem: episode nodes in quipu, bitemporal - per-game group
  memory:game:<id> keyed on in-game turn, durable tactics in memory:durable as refutable claims
  (confirmedBy/refutedBy). recall() hands tactics to later prompts. WAS DISABLED in our serve env;
  NA_MEMORY_QUIPU_URL now points at the local store (127.0.0.1:3030) alongside NA_QUIPU_URL grounding.
- directives.py: standing intents accepted only if measurable (vocabulary-checked), kept across
  decisions, MEASURED against each new world view, horizon-expired. This is faction/base-level
  intent persistence, built.
- Engine side: set_move_to persists multi-turn goto orders already; door-2 move issues them.

### What to build (the two genuinely new pieces)
1. UNIT-LEVEL INTENT NODES: when the agent gives a unit a long-horizon order (door-2 move to a
   distant tile, a ferry role, a former workplan), write a mem: intent node in the per-game group:
   subject unit id, goal, rationale, horizon (turns), and REVIEW TRIGGERS (enemy unit within N
   tiles of path, destination tile ownership changed, unit damaged below X, war state change).
   Grounding recall already runs before every brain call, so an intent surfaces automatically in
   any later world view naming that unit/base - no new prompt plumbing. The engine executes the
   goto; the graph remembers WHY; the agent re-decides only when a trigger fires.
2. CONDITIONAL QUEUED ANSWERS: extend the deferred-decision mechanism (comment above) with
   standing answers carrying invalidation predicates over the world view (e.g. base build queue
   [Hab Complex, Energy Bank] holds unless: at_war flips, enemy_near, drone riot, base captured,
   surplus collapses). Orchestrator auto-applies the queued answer while predicates hold and
   records tier=queued; a fired predicate re-raises the decision to the agent as tactical, with
   the violated predicate named in the world view. This is the "changed later only if needed to
   respond tactically"半 - the predicate vocabulary should reuse directives.py's measured-metric
   vocabulary so queued answers stay refutable/checkable, never untestable ambition.

### Sequencing (updated)
na-nnn bisect -> adapter defer patch -> orchestrator pending set -> conditional queued answers
(predicates over world view) -> unit intent nodes + review triggers. Memory/grounding stores are
live from tonight, so intent recall costs no new infrastructure - only the write path and the
trigger evaluation are new code.

comments.author: sattler
comments.text:
## Design constraint: FOG OF WAR, enforced by quipu NAMED GRAPHS (Stiwi directive, 2026-08-21)

Ruling: an agent deciding for faction F must not decide with knowledge of other factions'
decisions or private state. Named graphs are the enforcement mechanism, not convention.

### Where fog already holds (built, cite before rebuilding)
- World views: adapter sends own-bases-only (na_board_state doc calls another faction's bases
  "an information cheat"); fog.py gates the foreign-diplomacy feed (deltas naming uncontacted
  factions). Grounding/recall run BEFORE the brain, so the agent's inputs are exactly the world
  view - scoping recall scopes the agent.
- Door 2: move refuses unexplored destinations via the engine's own is_known (phase 4). No
  orchestrator tile model exists; the engine gate is the only tile gate - by design.
- Executor v2's trivial/policy tier is fog-clean by construction: stateless, sees only the one
  world view it is answering.

### Named-graph partition (the new rule for every write path in this workstream)
- memory:game:<game_id>:faction:<fid> - episodic memory AND unit-intent nodes are PER-FACTION
  graphs. A unit intent is faction-private by definition. Conditional queued answers and their
  predicates live here too.
- memory:durable - cross-game tactics only. Promotion rule: a durable tactic must be a
  game-agnostic claim about SMAC mechanics (public-book knowledge), promoted from a faction's own
  confirmed outcomes, and the promotion step strips/refuses board-specific facts - otherwise a
  durable tactic becomes a laundering channel for one game's private observations.
- datalinks (alphax rules graph) - public, shared: any faction could read the manual.
- ENFORCEMENT POINT: the orchestrator constructs the retriever per decision with the deciding
  faction's graph scope (group filter in every /search + GRAPH clause in every SPARQL it issues).
  The agent never queries the store directly in the decision loop; it receives recall only through
  the grounded world view. Telemetry lanes (decisions.jsonl, world-view store) stay cross-faction
  - they are the observer's record for replay/analysis, never a decision input.
- Tests that can fail (sentinel-style positive controls): plant a fact in faction 2's graph,
  decide for faction 4, assert the grounded world view does NOT carry it; then decide for faction
  2 and assert it DOES. A scoping rule without the leak-probe pair is a diagram, not a gate.

### Honest limitation of the interim (tonight)
The coordinator's strategic tier is ONE context answering all six factions - cross-faction
knowledge exists in that context regardless of store scoping. Disclosed, casual-play acceptable.
The built mechanism fixes it structurally: strategic decisions fan out to PER-FACTION agent
contexts (one subagent per faction, each fed only its faction's grounded world views and able to
recall only its faction's graph). One brain per faction is the fog boundary at the agent layer;
named graphs are the same boundary at the store layer. Both, not either.

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Slice 1 pre-flight: the fog design's enforcement mechanism does not exist in this store (harding)

The FOG/NAMED-GRAPHS comment specifies: *"group filter in every /search + GRAPH clause in every
SPARQL it issues."* Measured against the live local store (127.0.0.1:3030, read-only probes, no
restart) before building on it — all three legs fail, and one of them fails silently.

| mechanism | measured |
|---|---|
| `GRAPH <memory:durable> { ?s ?p ?o }` | **hard error**: `unsupported graph pattern` |
| `FROM <memory:durable>` | **silently ignored** — see below |
| `/search` with `group_id` | cannot even run here: `no embedding provider configured` |

**`FROM` is the dangerous one.** `SELECT ?s FROM <memory:graph-that-does-not-exist-xyzzy> WHERE
{ ?s ?p ?o } LIMIT 3` returns **3 rows**. A graph that cannot exist filters nothing, so `FROM`
looks exactly like scoping and enforces none. Anyone implementing the design as written would
reach for it after `GRAPH` errored, get plausible results, and ship a fog boundary that is a
diagram — which is the failure the design's own "leak-probe test pair REQUIRED" line exists to
catch. Control for these probes: a bare `?s ?p ?o` returns rows, so the instrument is proven.

**And there is nothing to scope yet.** The store holds exactly 10 types, all `smac:` (Technology,
Facility, SecretProject, Chassis, Reactor, Ability, Weapon, Armor, Unit, SocialModel) — the
datalinks rulebook. **Zero `aegis:` nodes, zero `aegis:Tactic`.** Positive control: the same
typed-query shape (`?s a ?ty`) returns those 10, so the zero is trustworthy. So
`MemoryStore.recall()` currently retrieves nothing at all, and "grounding is live" holds for the
rulebook path but not for the memory path.

**Where the fog boundary actually stands today** (read of the code, file:line):

- `fog.redact()` (`fog.py:67-99`) gates the *inbound* world view's diplomacy deltas. That is the
  only scoping that exists, and it operates on what the adapter sent — not on anything retrieved.
- `QuipuRetriever.build_query()` (`datalinks/quipu.py:113-147`): **no GRAPH, no group, no faction
  term.** Scoped only by `smac:appliesToEngine` and the label VALUES set.
- `MemoryStore.recall()` (`memory.py:280-311`): **no GRAPH, no group, no game id, no faction.** It
  reads every `aegis:Tactic` in the store regardless of which game or faction wrote it. Group
  labels are applied on the WRITE side only (`game_group()` `memory.py:63`, `DURABLE_GROUP` `:67`).
- `game_group()` is per-**game**, not per-**faction**: `f"memory:game:{game_id}"`. The design's
  `memory:game:<id>:faction:<fid>` does not exist on either side yet.

So the enrichment path is a global read, and the write-side group label is not something any read
can filter on.

**Proposed change to the design, for your call — I am proceeding on it unless you say otherwise:**
enforce with a **queryable predicate**, not a named graph. Every memory node carries its scope as
a triple (e.g. `aegis:memoryScope "memory:game:<id>:faction:<fid>"`), the orchestrator builds the
retriever per decision with the deciding faction's scope value, and every read adds that as a
FILTER in the WHERE clause. This works in a flat store, is testable by the leak-probe pair exactly
as specified, and does not have to be rewritten if named-graph support lands later — the scope
string is already the graph name.

Sequencing this slice accordingly: adapter defer + orchestrator pending set first (unaffected by
any of the above), then the scoped retriever with its leak probes.

comments.author: sattler
comments.text:
## Ruling on the preflight (sattler, 2026-08-21): PROCEED with scope-as-queryable-predicate — one hardening requirement

Reviewed the preflight. Method is sound (controls proven both directions, file:line cites). Approved with one addition:

**1. The retriever's scope must be REQUIRED, not defaulted.** Predicate scoping's known weakness vs named graphs is fail-OPEN: a read that forgets the FILTER sees everything, silently. Convert that to fail-closed at the API layer: `MemoryStore.recall()` / the scoped retriever REFUSE to run without an explicit scope value (no default-global read path in the decision loop). The leak-probe pair then guards the query text; the required parameter guards the call sites nobody probed. Telemetry/analysis reads that legitimately want cross-faction can use a separate, named method (`recall_unscoped_for_analysis()` or similar) so the grep for it is trivial and its use in the decision path is a visible defect, never a default.

**2. Keep the leak-probe pair exactly as specified in the fog comment** (plant in faction 2's graph-scope, decide as faction 4 -> absent; decide as faction 2 -> present). A scoping rule without it is a diagram.

**3. Cross-store datum, for the record and for whoever revisits named graphs later:** the two quipu deployments DIFFER in FROM semantics. Measured tonight, same probe shape on both:
- local NA store 127.0.0.1:3030: `FROM <nonexistent>` silently ignored, rows still returned (harding, control proven)
- aegis quipu.svc: `FROM <nonexistent>` correctly restricts -> 0 rows; control without FROM -> 3 rows (sattler)

So FROM support exists somewhere in the quipu lineage; the local store either predates it or runs a different backend. That makes harding's forward-compat argument concrete: the scope string doubling as the graph name means a later store upgrade can adopt real named graphs without a data migration. It also means: do NOT generalize either FROM behavior across stores — probe the store you are on (this is the second FROM-semantics surprise; treat FROM as store-specific always).

Sequencing approved as proposed: defer + pending set first, then scoped retriever + leak probes.

(Also for honesty: my first check of harding's claim ran against quipu.svc — the wrong store for this question. The claim named "this store" and I probed a different one; the contradiction I measured was real but not operative. Caught before ruling because the discrepancy was treated as a question, not reconciled by invention.)

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Slice 1 delivered: adapter defer + orchestrator pending set + fog-scoped retriever (harding)

`wt/harding` pushed on both repos. Not merged.

- **thinker** `854e148` feat(neural): recognise `defer` on every decide surface
- **NA** `5c7e2d8` feat(agent): deferred decisions — answer the engine now, the agent later
- **NA** `259b244` feat(fog): scope memory recall to the deciding faction, fail-closed

786 orchestrator tests pass (+28), thinker's 38 source/wire checks pass, ruff and mypy clean but
for one pre-existing `yupana.py:556` error (confirmed pre-existing by stashing and re-running).

### 1. Adapter — `defer` recognised BEFORE the unparseable branch

All four surfaces that parse an action_id: base.production, faction.tech, faction.se, base.hurry.
The ordering is the whole change. The outcome is identical either way — the engine's own pick is
applied — so nothing about the game's *behaviour* would reveal a missing branch. What differs is
the record: falling through writes `tier=deterministic` +
`fallback_reason="unparseable action_id defer"`, which says the orchestrator malfunctioned. It
did not. `degrade_rate` derives from that field, so a deferral recorded as a degradation makes a
working agent look like a missing one.

`tests/check_defer_recognised.py` guards both halves statically, in the same idiom as
`check_native_choice_withheld.py`. It **discovers** the surfaces rather than listing them, so a
fifth one added without a defer branch fails — which is the day the check is needed. **Proven to
fail in both directions by mutation**: branch removed, and branch moved after the unparseable one
where it can never be reached. Wired into `run-na-tests.sh`.

### 2. Orchestrator — the pending set

Recognised BEFORE `validate()`; a moment later it is correctly an id the engine did not offer,
and the decision degrades. Not repaired, not guarded, not validated — a deferral names no action,
so no rule about actions has an opinion on it.

**Relayed on the wire rather than converted to empty orders**, which corrects my first pass.
Forwards: it is what lets the ADAPTER write `tier=deferred` in the game's own telemetry — empty
orders reach it as "no action_id in reply", indistinguishable from an orchestrator that failed.
Backwards: an adapter that has never heard of deferral reads `defer` as unparseable, which
already lands on native_choice — the same answer by the older path, so the change degrades
compatibly against an old DLL, exactly as the design says.

`GET /agent/pending` (`?full=true` returns the grounded world view the agent read). Resolution
goes through door 2's existing `build` verb — no second endpoint meaning the same thing — so the
link back is reconstructed from `base_id`, the term both sides hold, and the resolved ids come
back in the same `/order` response that retired them. **Only on an order the game CONFIRMED**:
`unknown` is never upgraded to "applied" on silence, and retiring the agent's work on a message
that may never have been read is the one way this could lose a decision outright.

Expiry is honest rather than tidy: by the time the engine asks about turn N+1 it has played turn
N's build, so an answer arriving then lands on the next turn's minerals — a different decision.
Closed `expired` with the standing choice named.

One trap worth recording: `standing_action_id` is `None` on base.production **by design**, since
na-glk withholds the engine's pick from that request body. The tempting field is
`fallback_action_id()` — a different concept wearing a similar name (the orchestrator's
degradation target). On the test world view it returns `unit:0` where the engine's pick is
`unit:1`, so it would have put a confident wrong answer in the one field an expired deferral uses
to say what actually got built. Caught by a test, not by reading.

### 3. Fog — scope-as-predicate, fail-closed, per your ruling

Scope is **required, no default**, because a default is the hole: every caller that forgot the
argument would read every faction and look exactly like one that meant to. Empty scope issues no
query. The unscoped read exists as `recall_across_factions()` — a different name for a different
job, so a call site that does not belong in the decision path is one word in a diff.

The deciding faction's graph UNION `memory:durable`, with durable reached by being **named**
rather than by the query having no filter. Invisible in the output, decisive in the mechanism.

**Cached per faction, and that is a fog property rather than a performance one.** A process-wide
cache is the leak in miniature: recall once for faction 2, hand those lines to faction 4 with no
query issued at all — so a perfectly scoped store never gets the chance to enforce anything. It
has its own probe.

**12 leak probes, in pairs.** Absence proves nothing alone: a retriever that is off,
misconfigured, pointed at an empty store or broken outright passes every negative probe
perfectly. Each negative carries the positive control that separates "the boundary held" from
"nothing was retrieved". Asserted on **what the brain was handed**, not on what the store
returned — a store that filters correctly while the prompt gets the facts anyway is a leak with
good intentions upstream of it.

### What is NOT done, and why

- **Extraction is not split per faction.** One decision log holds all six factions, and the CLI
  writes it unattributed — so those nodes land in the per-game group and a scoped recall will not
  return them. Safe direction (no leak) but a real asymmetry, and it would read as a broken
  query, so `neural-amplifier` now **says so on the write** rather than leaving it to prose.
  Splitting `episodes()` per faction is slice 2 work: node names embed only the game id, so the
  partition needs care rather than a loop.
- **The rulebook retriever is still unscoped**, deliberately: `datalinks` is the public manual and
  the ruling names it as shared.
- **Nothing is deployed.** The orchestrator on :8000 serves the live session and the brief says
  not to restart it, so all three commits are pushed and the running service is still old code.
- **Conditional queued answers and unit-intent nodes** are the rest of na-7bk, untouched.

comments.text:
## Slice 2 delivered: conditional queued answers (harding)

`e934515` on `wt/harding` (NA). 802 tests pass (+16), ruff/mypy clean but for the pre-existing
`yupana.py:556`. Not merged, not deployed.

`POST /agent/queue` installs a standing answer; `GET /agent/queue` lists standing and retired
ones. The orchestrator applies it before the brain is asked — not waking the agent is the point —
and records `tier="queued"`, a fourth tier for the reason `deferred` is a third: no brain was
asked, and an agent chose it deliberately with stated conditions, so it is neither `llm` nor
`deterministic`. Keeping it separate is what makes the only question worth asking answerable
afterwards: how often did a standing answer stand, and how often was it overtaken?

### The predicate vocabulary is the measured one, and that is a refusal

Per the design's "reuse directives.py's measured-metric vocabulary so queued answers stay
refutable, never untestable ambition". An unmeasurable **directive** fails to steer; an
unmeasurable **predicate** keeps answering, because its invalidation condition can never fire —
so it degrades into exactly the script this mechanism exists not to be. Refused at install with a
422 naming the vocabulary, while the agent still holds the decision.

**This costs three of the four predicates the design comment gives as examples.** `at_war`,
`enemy_near` and `base captured` are not in `metrics.py`'s vocabulary, so they are refused today.
`surplus collapses` and `drone riot` ARE expressible (`mineral_surplus`, `drone_total`). Making
the other three expressible is not an orchestrator change — the vocabulary is deliberately
limited to names an adapter actually emits, so it needs thinker to emit them first. Flagging
rather than quietly widening the vocabulary with names nothing populates, which would reintroduce
the exact failure the restriction prevents.

### Four ways it stops, all fail-closed

violated predicate; passed horizon; **a metric missing from this world view** (an answer standing
on an unread instrument — absence of evidence is not evidence it is still right); and the action
no longer being in the offered space (invariant-1 backstop for a decision nobody is asked about —
an item already built or with a lost prerequisite is simply gone).

On stopping, the answer is retired and **every** violated predicate goes in front of the brain.
Not just the first: an agent told one of three reasons answers that one and re-queues into the
next wake-up.

Fog applies — `faction_id` is part of the key, not a label. Base ids are one engine-wide
sequence, so a base id alone is a coincidence away from applying faction 2's answer to faction
4's decision. Probed as a pair.

### A bug worth recording: mypy caught what 15 passing tests could not

`create_app` rebinds a local `queue` to the AgentBrain's DecisionQueue further down the same
function scope, and I had named the standing-answer store `queue` too. The endpoints closed over
whichever the name ended up meaning, so **with a real attached agent** `/agent/queue` would have
called `install` on the decision queue. Every test in the new file uses a non-agent brain, so the
rebinding never happened and all 15 passed against a broken production path. Renamed; regression
test added; verified by restoring the shadowing and watching **only** that one test fail with the
real `'DecisionQueue' object has no attribute 'install'`.

The general shape, which is not specific to this repo: a name rebound later in a function scope
silently repoints closures created earlier, and a test double that avoids the rebinding hides it
completely. The type checker saw it because it does not care which brain the tests use.

### Remaining on na-7bk

Slice 3 — unit-level intent nodes with review triggers, written into the per-faction graph slice
1 established. Not started.

comments.text:
## Slice 3 delivered: unit intent nodes with review triggers (harding)

`c35fd99` on `wt/harding` (NA). 818 tests pass (+16), ruff clean, mypy clean but for the
pre-existing `yupana.py:556`. Not merged, not deployed.

The engine already persists the ORDER — `set_move_to` keeps a multi-turn goto. What it does not
keep is WHY, and from a later turn an unexplained order and a stale one look identical; the safe
reading of an unexplained order is to leave it alone, which is exactly how a stale one survives.

Recorded on a **confirmed** door-2 order and attached to it, not posted separately — one act, one
record. A second endpoint would let you have either half without the other: an unexplained goto,
or a remembered plan no unit is carrying out. Faction comes from the **caller**, never inferred
from the unit id: units are one engine-wide sequence, so inferring is a coincidence away from
writing one faction's private plan into another's graph. Probed as a pair.

Surfaced with no new prompt plumbing, since recall already runs before every brain call — and
deliberately **not cached**, unlike durable tactics. Tactics are written between games so a cache
is free; an intent is written *during* one, by this same agent, minutes ago, so caching would
make a plan formed on turn 40 invisible on turn 41 — precisely the case the mechanism exists for.
Horizon-filtered at recall rather than deleted at expiry: an intent is not wrong when its horizon
passes, it is finished, and the record is worth keeping — it just must not sit in a later prompt
reading as though it still applied.

**Refused: an intent nothing could bring back for review.** No horizon (never finished, never
leaves the prompt) or no trigger (nothing can make it wrong, so it is a note not a plan). An
unreviewable intent is worse than none, because it reads in every later world view as a plan
somebody is watching.

## The gap that now spans slices 2 and 3, and what closes it

Both slices restrict conditions to the measured metric vocabulary, and both therefore refuse most
of the examples in your design comments:

| named in the design | expressible today | why not |
|---|---|---|
| `surplus collapses`, `drone riot` | **yes** | `mineral_surplus`, `drone_total` are emitted |
| escort strength, reserves draining | **yes** | `military_units`, `energy_reserves` |
| `at_war` / war state change | no | not a metric anything emits |
| `enemy unit within N tiles of path` | no | needs a tile model the orchestrator does not have **by design** — door 2's move refuses an unexplored destination via the engine's own `is_known`, and the engine gate is deliberately the only tile gate |
| `destination tile ownership changed` | no | same |
| `unit damaged below X` | no | per-unit state is not in the base surfaces' world view |

**This is an ADAPTER change, not an orchestrator one.** `metrics.py` is deliberately limited to
names an adapter actually emits, because an aspirational name produces conditions that can never
fire — which is the exact failure the restriction prevents. So closing it means thinker emitting
those facts first (a `faction.at_war` metric is the cheap one; the tile and unit-state triggers
are a larger question about whether the orchestrator should have any tile model at all, which
your fog comment says it deliberately should not).

I have NOT filed this as an na bead: the dispatch flagged that this store's local Dolt is 28
records behind the pulled JSONL and said to reconcile with `bd init --from-jsonl` before creating
more na beads. That is a data operation on a store I do not own, so I left it — this comment is
the record instead. Say the word and I will file it, or reconcile first if you want that done.

## na-7bk status

Slices 1, 2 and 3 are all delivered on `wt/harding`: `5c7e2d8` + `259b244` (defer, pending set,
fog scoping), `e934515` (queued answers), `c35fd99` (intents). Nothing is merged and nothing is
deployed — the orchestrator on :8000 still serves the live session on the old code.

agent. That is the bead's thesis, measured rather than asserted.

The four degraded rows are worth reading as a positive control: they say

moved on"`. Nothing was answered by an agent that was not there, and nothing pretended otherwise —

build — *read the forecast, submit the plan, done* — is missing its first step at the only
interface the attached agent actually has, and the instruction to perform it is printed in the
tool that needs it. The agent can set strategy blind, or read the board one `next_decision` at a
time, which is the per-decision latency the plan table exists to remove.

Closing this is my next commit: `_get` on the MCP client, plus `turn_forecast`,

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Slice 6 delivered: the loop is reachable from MCP, and the read it starts with was leaking (harding)

`8ec244e`, pushed to `main`. 855 orchestrator tests pass (+12), ruff and mypy clean — including
`yupana.py:556`, which is no longer failing.

I set out to verify slice 5 and close this bead. The verification found the mechanism sound and
the loop unflyable, which is not the same thing.

### `submit_turn_plan` told the model to do something it cannot do

The nine MCP tools are `next_decision`, `submit_orders`, `issue_directive`, `decisions_waiting`,
`what_if`, `issue_order`, `issue_orders`, `submit_turn_plan`, `order_outcomes`. **Every one of
them writes or answers. Nothing reads.** And `submit_turn_plan`'s own description opened:

> Read the turn forecast first (`POST /agent/turn` — it lists every decision the turn is expected
> to raise), decide them all at your own pace, then install the table

An MCP client holds tools, not HTTP verbs. So bulk-turn mode's first step was unreachable from
the only surface an attached agent has, and the instruction to perform it was printed in the tool
that needed it. `docs/agent-play.md` and the play skill said the same thing, in the same
unreachable form, for the plan's applied/missed report and the deferral sweep as well.

An agent following the documentation exactly can therefore set strategy **blind**, or read the
board one `next_decision` at a time — which is the per-decision latency this whole bead exists to
remove, arrived at by doing everything right.

`turn_forecast`, `turn_plan_status` and `deferred_decisions` now exist over the endpoints that
already did. A POST alias beside each route was the alternative; that is a second spelling of one
thing, and this bead's own history has an entry about what those cost (`fallback_action_id`
beside `standing_action_id`, a confident wrong answer in the one field an expired deferral uses).

On the surface's invariant — **no second source of BOARD state** — these are on the right side,
and I rewrote the test to assert the rule rather than a name list. They report the orchestrator's
record of its own decisions: what it was told to expect, what it answered from a table, what it
parked. Nothing reachable through them was not already sent by the adapter for those very
decisions.

### The larger half: the forecast was cross-faction, and I nearly wired that into the agent

The turn store holds every faction's slots in **one keyspace** — base ids are a single
engine-wide sequence — and every slot carries its base's **name**. `GET /turn` served all of it.

Measured on a live orchestrator, on the real recorded world views, before the gate landed:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| read the turn for faction 1, count faction 3's base names | **49 returned** — `University Base`, `Saturn Center`, `Visionary Outpost`, … |
| control: same read, is faction 1's own slot there | yes — so the instrument reads slots, and this is a filter failure not an empty store |

That is the adapter's own "information cheat" — the thing `na_board_state` refuses to put in a
world view — arriving through a door the world-view builder never sees. The fog comment on this
bead names world views and `fog.redact()` and door 2's `is_known`; the turn view is a fourth
surface and nobody had looked at it. **Exposing it on MCP as-is would have moved it from
available-to-anyone-who-curls to built into the agent's interface.**

Gated per your slice-1 ruling, fail-closed **at the API layer**: `POST /agent/turn` refuses a
request with no faction (422) rather than defaulting. A default is the hole — every caller that
forgot the argument reads every faction and looks exactly like one that meant to. `GET /turn`
stays unscoped as the observer's lane, which your fog comment already carved out: telemetry is
the record of what happened, never an input to a decision. `/agent/pending` and
`DeferralSet.pending()` take the same scope, which also brings the read into line with the write
— `resolve_for_base` already refuses to act on an unattributed deferral, and a read laxer than
the write hands out precisely the rows the write will not let you use.

Two decisions inside that worth your eye:

- **An announcement's own `faction_id` now attributes entries that do not repeat it.** Without
  it the fail-closed filter withholds the entire forecast from the very faction that announced
  the turn: correct by the rule, useless in practice.
- **A slot nobody can attribute is withheld AND counted** (`unattributed`). Withholding is the
  safe direction; withholding in silence is not. From inside a plan, a base filtered out is
  indistinguishable from a base that is not there — so an adapter that stopped emitting
  `faction_id` would shrink every agent's forecast to nothing while every count in sight stayed
  self-consistent. Slots belonging to *other* factions are deliberately **not** counted there:
  that is the filter working, and mixing the two makes the number unreadable.

### Flown through the tools themselves, on real board states

Not a unit test and not curl: `build_server(OrchestratorClient(...))` against a live orchestrator
on `:8099`, calling the tools exactly as a model would. Inputs are the **49 real
`base.production` world views for turn 103 faction 3** from the 2026-08-21 session, with faction
1's 42 bases announced into the same turn as the leak control.

| step | measured |
|---|---|
| `turn_forecast(faction_id=3)` | 49 slots — **49/49 my own, 0 of the other faction's 42**, `unattributed=0` |
| unscoped control `GET /turn` | **91 slots, factions [1, 3]** — the store did hold both |
| `submit_turn_plan` (45 entries) | 2 ms |
| 45 covered decisions | **median 0.7 ms, whole faction turn 0.03 s** |
| 4 uncovered | 1.25 s each — blocked to the engine deadline, then degraded |
| decision log | **45 `tier=plan` with 0 degraded, 4 `tier=llm` degraded** |
| `turn_plan_status(3)` | 45 answers from 45 entries, **0 missed** |
| `deferred_decisions(3, full=True)` | answers (`count=0`; nothing was deferred this run) |

The unscoped control and the four uncovered decisions are the two halves that make the rest mean
anything. The first says the filter filtered rather than emptied; the second says nothing was
answered by an agent that was not there, and nothing pretended otherwise. Against the 30-60 s per
decision this bead opens with, that round is **25-49 minutes** decided one at a time and **0.03
seconds** from the table.

Six mutations, six failures, restored, control green: filter removed, announcement fallthrough
removed, 422 removed, pending filter removed, `faction_id` made optional, and the tool pointed
back at the raw HTTP route. The schema assertion is deliberately on the tool **signature** rather
than on behaviour — an optional `faction_id` passes every test that supplies one, and the leak is
the call that omits it.

One thing worth recording plainly: **`POST /agent/turn` had no test at all.** Making it require
an argument broke nothing, which is how I found out. The endpoint the entire bulk-turn loop
begins from was the untested one.

## Closing this bead

All five slices plus this one are on `main` and measured. Two things remain and neither belongs
here:

- **na-1zi** — the live orchestrator on `:8000` (pid 3485074, started 2026-08-21 20:45) answers
  `GET /agent/plan` with **404**. It is pre-plan-table code, so batch commands cannot work in the
  live session until it is restarted on `main`. Not mine to call.
- **na-x8f** — the thinker-emit gap: `at_war`, `enemy_near`, tile and unit-damage predicates that
  slices 2 and 3 refuse because `metrics.py` only admits names an adapter actually emits.
