title: Instrument the 27 surfaces that already have a native fallback
description:
just surfaces reports the split from the frozen registry: 4 of 77 instrumented, 73 remaining, and those 73 partition into 21 needing the deterministic tier built first, 25 unit-scope that stay deterministic on volume grounds, and 27 base and faction surfaces that already have a native AI path.

Those 27 are the ones to work through. They need no fork work and no new deterministic tier: the native path is the fallback, so invariant 9 holds from the first record. Each one is the same shape as the four that exist - a hook that emits surface_id with an engine-authoritative action space, plus a side-effect-free probe, because in-game input cannot be driven and a surface that fires every five to ten turns is otherwise unverifiable.

This is deliberately not the NO_AI_PATH work (na-2mn, which is step 0 and expensive) and not the unit-scope volume question. It is the incremental bucket, and it was undercounted as 20 until the registry partition was fixed - the docs listed 'no AI path' and 'unit scope' as separate piles when seven surfaces are both.

Pick order should follow decision-inputs.md: low frequency and high stakes first, because those are where a model's judgement can pay for its latency. base.hurry and faction.tech were chosen on exactly that basis.
notes:
PROGRESS 2026-08-16 (Claude) — 3 of 27 instrumented. Bucket is now 23.

NOT claiming this bead; it stays assigned to ellie and stays open. Recording work done
against it so the next person starts from 23 rather than 26, and so the pattern is written
down once instead of rediscovered per surface.

INSTRUMENTED, in the pick order this bead specifies (low frequency, high stakes):

  base.staple          na_staple_observe   consider_staple (build.cpp)
                       thinker 7cc17a8..f9bc789 / NA f9bc789
  econ.corner_market   na_endgame_observe  mod_faction_upkeep AI-only block (game.cpp)
  council.call         na_endgame_observe  call_council AI-only (game.cpp)
                       thinker 826526c / NA 92e6356

`just surfaces` now reports 4 applied, 5 observed only, 23 instrumentable.

THE SHAPE, so it does not have to be re-derived 23 more times:

  1. Hoist the engine's own gate into a named bool at the call site. Never copy it into the
     emitter — a second definition of "was this decision even available" drifts, which is
     what check_retool taught on na-lnv. Same operands, same order, same short-circuit.
  2. Record only when the gate opened, so a row is always a decision that was on the table.
  3. Emit the COUNTS the engine weighed, not its verdict. A derived boolean bakes today's
     threshold in and silently reinterprets every past row when the engine changes.
  4. native_choice is mandatory. These are observations of a working native path, so the
     record's whole value is the baseline; without it there is nothing for na-6db to A/B.
  5. One side-effect-free probe per surface. Every one of these fires rarely and cannot be
     provoked, so the probe is what makes the wire format checkable at all. The probe does
     NOT gate on eligibility — a probe that went silent exactly when the decision was
     unavailable could not do the job it exists for.
  6. Transcribe into test_adapter_contract and DIFF IT MECHANICALLY against the emitter. All
     three of these were checked that way; no field emitted that is not pinned, none pinned
     that is not emitted.
  7. OBSERVED only, never APPLIED. Nothing applies a brain's answer on any of them.

TWO FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING:

base.psych is NOT a decision surface and should not be treated as one when its turn comes.
mod_base_psych is a survey computation — the loop calls it 72 times to score talent/police
combinations and the final call applies the pending SE values. There is no choice and no
native answer to record. Someone working the list will reach it and should reclassify rather
than force a record.

council.call has no answer to READ. call_council decides internally and returns nothing
useful, so it is observed as a state transition: STATE_COUNCIL_HAS_CONVENED off before the
call, on after. Inferring the answer from can_call_council would be wrong in the one case
that matters — eligible and still declining — and wrong in the direction that looks like
agreement. Expect more of the 23 to need this treatment; an engine function returning void
is not the same as a surface with no native answer.

NONE OF THE THREE IS VERIFIED AGAINST A RUNNING GAME. No engine has fired any of these
hooks. That is what the probes are for, and it is why none of them moved into APPLIED.
PROGRESS 2026-08-16 (Claude), continued — 6 of 27 instrumented. Bucket is now 21.

Added since the last note: base.satellite (thinker 167f214), base.project (thinker 5bb34fa).
Still assigned to ellie; still open.

  base.satellite   na_satellite_observe   find_satellite (build.cpp)
  base.project     na_project_observe     find_project (build.cpp)

`just surfaces`: 4 applied, 7 observed only, 21 instrumentable.

WHAT THESE TWO ADDED TO THE PATTERN — both are about action spaces, and both generalise:

ENUMERATE WHEN THE ENGINE ENUMERATES. base.satellite offers all four orbitals and base.project
every buildable secret project, each with the engine's own numbers: availability, built-against-
goal, facility_score, already-building counts. Most of the bucket is binary; these two are not,
and a two-way summary would have thrown away the part a brain would actually reason about.

FORWARD THE ENGINE'S WEIGHTS, NEVER REBUILD THEM. base.project scores options with the same
facility_score(item, Wgov) the chooser used, Wgov passed down from the caller. Rebuilding it
locally was easy and would have produced a ranking that disagrees with the engine's for reasons
invisible in the record — while carrying the engine's authority. Worse than omitting the column.

AVAILABILITY IS NOT A PREDICTION. base.satellite's per-option `available` says the option is
legal, not that the chooser would take it: find_satellite also weighs an aerospace prerequisite
and a randomised defence bias. Read as a ranking it would score the adapter as disagreeing with
the engine on rows where they agree completely. The fixture is deliberately a board with two
available options where the chooser took the first.

A CHOOSER'S "PREREQUISITE" ANSWER IS NOT A DECLINE. Both surfaces have one: satellite answers
-FAC_AEROSPACE_COMPLEX, project answers Skunkworks or the Subspace Generator. Folding either
into "none" records a base actively working toward the thing as one that turned it down, and
afterwards the two are indistinguishable. find_project has a third shape too — a missile unit id
— emitted as unit:<id> rather than project:<id>.

WHICH SIDE OF THE GATE THE HOOK SITS ON DECIDES WHETHER A DECLINE IS A RECORD. base.staple
records only when its gate opened, because the gate is what says the decision existed. These two
record declines, because by the time the chooser runs the gate has already opened and "nothing
this turn" is an answer. Opposite rules, and the difference is structural rather than a taste
call.

PROBES MUST NOT CONSUME RANDOMNESS. Both choosers read random(), so both probes report a decline
instead of calling them: calling would risk an answer the game will not repeat AND consume a roll
the real decision was going to make. observe-project builds its weights from governor_priorities,
exactly as select_build does, so the engine_score column it prints is the real one.

TRANSLATE FILE-LOCAL SENTINELS AT THE CALL SITE. GOV_NONE is static in build.cpp; both emitters
take a `declined` bool rather than spelling its value again.

ADMIT A CAP. base.project's walk stops at 32 options and says so in action_space_truncated — the
rule na_audit already follows. A partial list presented as a whole one is how a brain comes to
believe it saw everything.

THE DIALOG GUARD HAS NOW CAUGHT THREE. base.staple, econ.corner_market and base.project are all
dialog-mapped AND independently instrumented, and every one is the same split: the dialog is the
OUTCOME (a project seized, a corner foiled, a staple confirmed by a human) while the hook is the
DECISION. Outcome and decision are different surfaces wearing one surface id. Expect this on
more of the 21.

STILL NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A RUNNING GAME. No hook in this bead has fired on a board.
AUDIT OF THE REMAINING 19, 2026-08-16 (Claude). Read the fork rather than trusting the count.

7 of 27 are instrumented. Auditing what is left turned up something that changes this bead's
premise: THE "27" IS AN OVERCOUNT, and not by a little.

The 27 came from the registry partition — "has a native AI path" AND "not unit-scope". That is a
statement about surfaces the GAME has, not about decision points THINKER EXPOSES. Several of the
remaining 19 are not separate decisions at all. Instrumenting them would either double-count a
decision already covered or invent a record for a computation nobody chose.

CLASSIFICATION. Read closely (R) or established by grep plus one read (G):

SUBSUMED BY base.production, which is already APPLIED:
  base.facility  (R) scored in select_build's build_order loop, same pass as satellites and
                     projects. There is one chooser and it returns one item.
  base.queue     (R) same loop; the queue is what select_build's answer goes into.
  base.hq_relocate (R) valid_relocate_base is a LEGALITY PREDICATE inside can_build
                     (base.cpp:4917), not a chooser. Building the HQ is a production choice.
  Instrumenting any of these emits a second record for one decision and inflates coverage.

NOT DECISIONS — computations or state, with no alternatives weighed:
  base.psych        (R) mod_base_psych is a survey: 72 calls scoring talent/police pairs, then
                        one that applies pending SE. Recorded in an earlier note.
  base.growth       (G) mod_base_growth computes growth; base_drones computes drone counts.
  base.support      (G) engine-side upkeep arithmetic, no Thinker override.
  base.drone_riot   (R) BSTATE_DRONE_RIOTS_ACTIVE is a flag the engine sets and clears
                        (base.cpp:1712, 1747). The DECISION about riots is base.staple, done.
  econ.commerce     (R) base.cpp:2258 computes commerce income across treaty partners.
  victory.conquest / victory.diplomatic (G) victory_done() is a predicate, not a chooser.

OPAQUE — engine code with no Thinker override, so out of reach without the binary:
  diplo.ai_to_ai    (R) enemy_diplomacy is a raw address (engine.cpp:809), called once
                        (game.cpp:1556). Nothing to hook.
  faction.agenda    (G) only net_agenda_on/off raw pointers.
  diplo.declare_war / diplo.treaty_break / diplo.atrocity (R) act_of_aggression (faction.cpp:755)
                        is Thinker's own, but it EXECUTES an aggression already decided upstream
                        in engine code — it has no alternatives and no answer. It is an event.
                        A record there would be a dialog-style fact, not a decision.
  base.capture      (R) its decidable content is the HQ escape, already instrumented separately
                        as base.hq_escape.

GENUINELY INSTRUMENTABLE AND NOT YET DONE:
  base.name         (R) mod_name_base (game.cpp:2106) is Thinker's own chooser and picks an
                        unused name from the faction list. A real decision with a native answer.
                        LOW STAKES, which is why it was not picked earlier under this bead's own
                        rule, not because it is hard.
  base.workers / base.specialists — NOT SETTLED. Both are assigned during base_compute
                        (base.cpp:141-142, 2023) and I did not read far enough to say whether a
                        chooser weighs alternatives or the values fall out of the tile pass.
                        Marked unknown deliberately rather than guessed.

SO THE HONEST REMAINING COUNT IS ROUGHLY 1 TO 3, not 19.

WHAT TO DO WITH THIS. I have NOT edited surfaces.py to reclassify anything — the registry is
frozen, `just surfaces` reports from it, and quietly moving entries would change the coverage
number on my own say-so. The classification above is evidence for whoever decides. My
recommendation, for ellie or ian:

  - keep every id in the frozen registry (renaming or removing invalidates past runs), and
  - add a `SUBSUMED` set alongside NO_AI_PATH so coverage() can stop counting a surface as
    instrumentable when the decision is already covered under another id, and
  - re-read base.workers / base.specialists before assuming either way.

That change moves a published number, so it wants a human's call rather than mine.

CAVEAT ON THIS AUDIT: eleven of these I read; the rest I established by grep plus a single read,
marked (G) above. A (G) entry is a strong prior, not a settled fact — the base.retool lesson was
exactly a surface everyone assumed needed work that already had it, and it went the other way.
RESOLVED 2026-08-16 — the bucket is empty. `just surfaces` reports 0 instrumentable.

and assigned to ellie for one reason only, stated at the end.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
FIRST SURFACE INSTRUMENTED — econ.energy_sliders (thinker 027a79d, NeuralAmplifier 4865fe7).

    4  applied           unchanged — this is observe-only
    1  observed only     was 0
   26  instrumentable    was 27

## Why this one, of the 27

This bead says pick order follows decision-inputs.md: low frequency, high stakes first, because
that is where a model's judgement can pay for its latency. By that rule econ.energy_sliders is
the strongest candidate in the bucket — it fires once per faction-turn and the ratio it sets
divides EVERY base's energy for the whole turn. Nothing else in the ready bucket reaches as far
per decision.

## The pattern, for the remaining 26

  - hook at the seam AFTER the native answer is final. mod_allocate_energy narrows SE_alloc_labs
    four separate times (energy_limit, a 0..10 clamp, two efficiency loops), so an observation
    taken earlier records a value the engine then overwrites — and the record would disagree with
    the game for reasons no reader could reconstruct.
  - the ACTION SPACE comes from the engine. Legal splits are labs+psych <= 10 with the economy
    remainder inside energy_limit(faction_id) — the same function the engine clamps itself
    against. Enumerating from our own reading of the rules drifts silently, which is what
    na_audit exists to catch elsewhere.
  - OBSERVED, not APPLIED. tier "deterministic", applied "native". The applied count is what says
    how much of the game the brain drives; moving it for an observation would overstate the one
    number that exists to stay honest.

## A reporting bug this exposed and fixed

`just surfaces` computed "instrumented but switched off" from OBSERVED, so the new surface printed
as switched off — inviting someone to hunt for the na.toml line that would enable it. There is no
such line: a surface can only be switched on if it has an apply path. That line read correctly
only while OBSERVED and APPLIED were the same set, which stopped being true the instant the first
observe-only surface landed. Now computed from APPLIED, with observe-only reported separately.

## Remaining

26 surfaces, each needing the same two halves (observe hook, then apply path + validation). The
apply half for econ.energy_sliders is not built — nothing applies a brain's answer to the sliders
yet, which is why it is observed and not applied.

Not yet verified live: the hook compiles, is deployed, and the wire suite passes, but no game has
run since. One run would confirm the record appears with a plausible action space.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
VERIFIED LIVE, and two findings about the remaining 26 that change how they should be picked.

## econ.energy_sliders confirmed from a running game

    faction: Gaians | turn 135
    native : econ 6 / labs 4 / psych 0  | energy_limit 10
    offered: 66 legal splits
    tier   : deterministic | applied: native

66 is the arithmetic checking out rather than my reading of it: all (labs, psych) with
labs+psych <= 10 is exactly 66, and energy_limit 10 excludes none of them. Three records in the
turn, one per routed faction. tier/applied confirm it observed without deciding.

## FINDING 1 — the ready bucket's volume filter is too narrow

`coverage()` computes volume_bound as `remaining - NO_AI_PATH` where `scope_for(s) == "unit"`. So
volume is treated as a property of UNIT scope.

base.specialists is base-scope and therefore counted "ready" — but `best_specialist()` is called
from a loop over `base->specialist_total` (base.cpp:2320-2325), for every specialist beyond the
16th, inside a block that itself runs several times per base-turn. On a 55-base faction that is
far higher volume than several unit-scope surfaces the partition excludes.

So "ready" currently means "has a native path and is not unit-scope", and it is being read as
"cheap to instrument". Those are different claims. A base-scope surface can be per-citizen.

Not fixing the partition here: changing what `ready` counts would move a number this project
quotes, and it deserves its own decision rather than being slipped in. Recorded so the next pick
is not made on a number that means something narrower than it looks.

## FINDING 2 — the seam IS most of the work; the 26 are not a batch

I tried to survey seams for ten of the remaining surfaces by grep and got nothing usable —
keyword hits across nine files each, because "where does the engine decide X" is not a textual
question. econ.energy_sliders took reading mod_allocate_energy end to end to learn that
SE_alloc_labs is narrowed four times and only the last value is real; that fact is what makes the
hook correct and no sweep would have surfaced it.

The two surfaces whose seams ARE now known:
    base.specialists   pick_specialist / best_specialist (base.cpp:4788) — high volume, see above
    econ.commerce      referenced in base.cpp, seam not yet read

Consequence for planning: each surface needs its decision function read before it can be ordered
by frequency and stakes at all, because frequency is a property of the CALL SITE and is not
visible from the registry. The pick order this bead asks for cannot be produced up front for all
26; it emerges one surface at a time.

## Pattern for the next one, established and verified

  1. find the engine function that settles the answer, and hook AFTER its last mutation
  2. build the action space from the engine's own constraint function, never from our reading
  3. land in OBSERVED, not APPLIED — the applied count is what says how much of the game the
     brain drives, and moving it for an observation overstates the one number kept honest
  4. run a game and confirm the record appears with a plausible action space

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## The bucket is empty, and the caveat every progress note carried is now resolved (harding)

Two things this bead was waiting on. One had already happened and nobody closed it; the other
had never been done at all and is the reason I picked this up.

### 1. `just surfaces` reports the bucket at ZERO

    4  applied — the brain's choice executes
    9  observed only — a record is written, the engine still chooses
   64  not instrumented, which divides into:
   20    no native AI path — the deterministic tier has to be built first
   25    unit-scope with a native path — mostly stay deterministic on volume grounds
   19    no separate decision to instrument (surfaces.SUBSUMED)
    0    have a native path and a safe fallback — INSTRUMENTABLE NOW

**"0 instrumentable now" is this bead's bucket**, the one that read 27, then 23, then 21 across
the progress notes above.

And I want to be exact about how it emptied, because "27 instrumented" would be a false claim.
It emptied two ways: **9 were instrumented**, and the rest were **reclassified** — into
`SUBSUMED`, which now holds 19 with reasons per entry (`base.facility`/`base.queue` answered by
base.production's single chooser; `base.psych`/`base.growth`/`base.drone_riot` computations
rather than choices; `diplo.declare_war`/`base.capture` events rather than decisions;
`base.workers`/`base.specialists`/`base.name` instrumented but with no action space).

That is the sanctioned outcome and this bead predicted it — its own note says of base.psych,
*"Someone working the list will reach it and should reclassify rather than force a record."*
Reclassification is not instrumentation, and the honest summary is that the bucket was drained
by doing both.

### 2. What had NOT been done: any of it verified against a running engine

Every progress note above carries the same line, and none of them ever cleared it:

> NONE OF THE THREE IS VERIFIED AGAINST A RUNNING GAME. No engine has fired any of these hooks.

The hooks were checked statically, against pinned records, by a mechanical diff. Real work, and
it cannot tell you whether the engine reaches the call site — which is the failure na-4zs turned
out to be, on a surface that had been "instrumented" for weeks while the engine never touched it.

**Done now.** One turn on a real save, an isolated copy of the game, every observe flag on, all
six AI factions:

| surface | records | raised by |
|---|---|---|
| `base.workers` + `base.specialists` | 209 each | the engine |
| `base.hurry` | 86 | the engine |
| `base.defend_goal` | **42** | the engine |
| `base.production` | 24 | the engine |
| `base.satellite` | **7** | the engine |
| `base.project` | **5** | the engine |
| `econ.energy_sliders` | **2** | the engine |
| `faction.se` | 1 | the engine |
| `council.call` | **1** | the engine |
| `base.retool` | 1 | its probe |
| `base.staple` | 1 | its probe |
| `econ.corner_market` | 1 | its probe |
| `faction.tech_steal` | 1 | its probe |

**All 9 observed-only surfaces now have a record written by a live game process** — 5 raised by
the engine itself, 4 by their probes. That split is the design working exactly as this bead
specifies it: *"one side-effect-free probe per surface, because a surface that fires every five
to ten turns is otherwise unverifiable."* Four of the nine did not come up in one turn, which is
why the probes exist and not a shortfall.

`base.defend_goal` at 42 and `base.satellite`/`base.project` firing at all are the ones I would
not have predicted from the static checks.

### One record-shape trap, found by walking into it

`base.workers` and `base.specialists` are emitted as ONE record carrying **`surface_ids`
(plural)** with `record: "base_yield"` and **no `surface_id` key at all**. My first tally keyed
on `surface_id`, counted 209 records as `None`, and I nearly reported a bug in the adapter.

It is not a bug — one engine computation genuinely answers two surface ids — but anything that
tallies the adapter log by `surface_id` silently drops 209 of 388 records, i.e. more than half,
and reports a clean number while doing it. Worth knowing for na-0oa's harvester and for anyone
reading `na-observations.jsonl` by hand. The tally in the table above reads both shapes.

### Closing

The bucket is empty by the registry's own report, and the observation layer is verified live for
the first time. Anything further on these nine is an APPLY path, which is a different question
per surface — `na.toml` lists all nine as "observed only, no apply path yet" — and na-6db is the
bead that says whether applying any of them would be an improvement.

Was assigned to ellie, whose card no longer exists after the roster cut; closing under the
one-owner haul rule.

title: Evals: keep the committed runs honest as the prompt drifts
description:
evals/runs/ holds the prompts and answers behind every measured number in the docs, and evals/runs/<id>/manifest.json holds a sha256 of each prompt. Nothing checks it.

The failure is quiet and certain: the system prompt changes - it already has, twice - and the committed answers silently become evidence about a prompt that no longer exists, while just eval score keeps printing the same confident table. The docs then quote a number measured against something we no longer ship.

Cheapest fix is a test that regenerates each arm's prompt and compares the hash to the manifest, failing with 'the prompt moved, re-run the eval' rather than pretending. It needs THINKER_DIR to rebuild the world view, so it belongs behind the same skip the quipu tests use rather than in the default lane.

Better but more work: make the prompt reproducible without the sibling checkout by grounding from the committed datalinks/thinker/alphax.ttl instead of the fork's alphax.txt, which would let the check run everywhere.

Not urgent - both runs match their prompts today - but it is the difference between a stale eval announcing itself and a stale eval being believed.
close_reason:
just eval check compares each committed run's prompt hash against what the code produces now, and prints a unified diff of what moved. It found both evals stale immediately, in two different ways.

Ordinary drift: na-373 was measured, then _SYSTEM gained a history section for na-61c2. Re-ran both arms (40 Haiku decisions) so the committed run is current rather than once-true. The finding survived and strengthened - the ranking rule now predicts citation at 0.31 against 0.50 for chance, where the first measurement gave 0.43. Every number moved a little and none qualitatively.

The worse one: na-61c2's ARMS changed underneath it. It built its contested world view from ground(view, retriever, 4), which at the time meant the top four by information value, because the retriever briefly ranked before na-373 refuted it. Reverting that silently turned the same call into 'first four in action-space order' - a different fact set, a different experiment, the same name, and the old answers still sitting beside it scoring cleanly.

Fixed by naming the four facts in build_history.CONTESTED. The lesson is in evals/README.md: an eval's arms are part of the eval, and deriving them from whatever a component currently does means the experiment changes whenever that component does.

check deliberately does not judge whether drift matters - it says what moved and leaves that to a person, since some prompt changes cannot affect a given arm and asserting which is a claim needing its own evidence. Also fixed: the just eval recipe prefixed ../ unconditionally and broke on an absolute THINKER_DIR.

title: Retrieval cost on wide surfaces must be cut option-neutrally
description:
Follow-on from na-373, which refuted rank-then-truncate. Grounding is one fact per option, so any top-k truncation under-explains the options it drops and biases the choice - measured: truncating to the top 4 moved base.production from Network Node 19/20 to Research Hospital 15/20 and cut stability 0.95 to 0.75.

So the cost problem is still open and the shape of an acceptable fix is now known: it has to treat every option the same. Two candidates.

Uniform compression - shorten every fact rather than drop some. Cheapest to try, option-neutral by construction, and measurable with the existing harness.

Two-pass - a cheap fact for every option, rich facts only for a shortlist the brain asks about. Option-neutral in pass one. Costs a round trip on the highest-frequency surface, which is the thing to measure.

Measure with scripts/retrieval_utilisation.py: it already reports utilisation, mean cited, and the choice distribution, and the choice distribution is the half that matters. Acceptance is unchanged from na-373 - utilisation up with NO change to the choice distribution.

title: mdBook docs site
description: The repo had 18 design docs and no way to read them as a site. Set up mdBook with book.toml at the repo root pointing src at docs/ in place, rather than a docs/book/src/ copy: every doc already links its siblings by bare filename and is linked to from README.md and AGENTS.md as docs/<name>.md, so a book-specific source tree would have broken both the ~40 internal cross-references and every GitHub deep link, to render the same output.
close_reason: book.toml at the repo root, src = docs, build-dir = book (gitignored). docs/SUMMARY.md is the TOC across five sections and docs/README.md the index — it also gives the docs/ folder a landing page on GitHub. All 19 chapters render and every local link in the output resolves. Eight links escaping docs/ (six ../VISION.md, two into source files) became absolute GitHub URLs: mdBook rewrites .md to .html relative to the source root, so those resolved outside the book and 404'd. just docs gains build and serve; check is now lint plus build, because a chapter renamed without updating SUMMARY.md passes every markdown rule. CI's lint-markdown lane became docs and builds the book too — it also pinned markdownlint at 0.17.2, a third copy of the version that had drifted from the other two, now 0.23.2 everywhere. mdbook added to setup-environment.sh (release tarball, not cargo install — the lane budget is ~5 minutes) and the CONTRIBUTING tooling table.

title: Hank role (c)/(d): replace StateGuard with the real board graph
description:
StateGuard (orchestrator/hank.py) does the part of Hank role (c) that needs no board graph: it checks a chosen order's DECLARED effects against the metrics the world view reports. Denies what current state cannot pay for; warns on a violated directive.

That is a floor, not the design. What it cannot do without role (d):
  - reason about anything the adapter did not declare in Action.effects
  - check board-shaped preconditions (is the tile still ours, is the unit still alive, did the target base change hands)
  - what-if / speculative apply (role e)

TRACKED UPSTREAM (filed 2026-07-31):
  scbrown/hank#78  FR-35 generic non-code fact ingestion  <- the gate, everything depends on it
  scbrown/hank#79  FR-36 game-state policy selector model
  scbrown/hank#80  FR-37 hank_guard                       <- THIS issue blocks on #80
  scbrown/hank#81  FR-38 hank_whatif
  scbrown/hank#82  FR-39 per-game tenancy (a fog security boundary when >1 faction is LLM-driven)

Design doc: hank/docs/neuralamplifier-harness.md. Honest gating from that doc: all of FR-35..39 is net-new engineering, gated twice - by Hank Phase 4 (Phase 3 multi-tenancy has not started) AND by the non-code ingestion of FR-35, which does not exist. Every Hank node today anchors to a file:line span.

Also from that doc, and worth carrying into our expectations: hank_guard sees an APPROXIMATED post-order board, because applying orders to a COW overlay re-implements engine order semantics outside the engine. So deny stays conservative and the engine remains sole authority - which is the same precedence StateGuard already honours.

The seam is ready: StateGuard sits behind the Guard protocol, composed by GuardChain, so swapping in POST /guard should not change the verdict shape or the decision record.

Done, against yupana rather than a net-new service. orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/yupana.py implements the Guard protocol over yupana's yupana_ingest / yupana_guard MCP tools: this turn's board is written to a private per-faction overlay, the proposed orders are applied speculatively, and graph-pattern policies are evaluated at the order boundary. title: Directive entity ids are cited as grounding facts and flagged as fabricated
description:
Hank's citation guard fires on 3-4 runs in 5 with 'cited facts that were never offered: fac:the-weather-paradigm'. The model is not hallucinating - it was genuinely shown that id, in a directive's entities list - but the guard reads the offered set only from the grounding block, so a directive entity looks fabricated.

Two id spaces that are deliberately the same (a directive's entities ARE grounding fact ids, which is what makes the multi-hop walk work) but only one of which counts as offered. The guard should treat ids shown in world_view.directives[].directive.entities as offered.

Left as a bug rather than fixed inline because it also inflates a real signal: utilisation counts cited-against-offered, and a citation the guard drops is currently invisible in both directions.
acceptance_criteria: A run where the only 'unoffered' citations are directive entities produces no advisory, and utilisation is unchanged by directives being present.
close_reason:
Already implemented on main; bead was left open. Verified rather than assumed.

Guard half: hank.py:81-82 builds the offered set as grounded_ids | entities_shown(world_view), and the code names na-zgz in its own comment. directives.py:304 entities_shown is the shared reader, deliberately NOT folded into grounding so the utilisation denominator does not move when a directive is present.

Utilisation half: knowledge.py summarise() splits citations into quipu_cited (retrieval, drives utilisation) and plan_cited (directive entities), so a legitimate citation is bucketed rather than dropped — which is what used to make it vanish from the record in both directions.

Acceptance covered by named tests, 12 passed: test_an_entity_a_directive_showed_is_offered_not_fabricated (no advisory) and test_a_genuinely_invented_id_is_still_caught_when_directives_are_present (a real hallucination is still flagged).

title: Metric vocabulary is six faction fields deep; most directives cannot be expressed
description:
metrics.py holds 11 names and the adapter reports 6 faction-level ones. That covers economy and expansion, which is enough for the saving/expansion plans measured so far, but a directive about military posture, terraforming progress, tech position relative to rivals, or diplomatic standing cannot currently be written at all - the name does not exist, so it is refused at issue time.

The honest order of work is adapter first, vocabulary second: a name in the vocabulary that nothing reports produces directives that are permanently unmeasurable, which is the exact failure the closed vocabulary exists to prevent. drone_total is already in the vocabulary and NOT reported - it needs a sweep over bases - so it is the first thing to either emit or remove.

close_reason:
RESTORED by ellie 2026-08-02 (aegis-uae2s). This bead was closed on 2026-08-01T04:31:10Z and
commit 36d67d0 reverted it to `open`.

Evidence it was a lost write and NOT a deliberate reopen: the durable JSONL carried
status=closed with the full reason below at b99b3ba; the embedded Dolt store's record for this
bead still read `updated_at: 2026-07-30T06:44:18Z` — OLDER than the close itself. 36d67d0
exported that stale store over the good JSONL, so the store's omission became the durable copy.
A record that predates its own close cannot be a reopen of it.

The original close reason follows, unaltered.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Found a dead seam underneath it: the adapter wrote its measurements under a faction_state key and the orchestrator reads WorldView.metrics, so on a real world view EVERY directive evaluated unmeasurable regardless of what the adapter reported. Both sides were internally consistent and separately tested. Fixed adapter-side per invariant 2 (measurements are adapter-supplied): na_write_faction_state becomes na_write_metrics, emitting the contract key. drone_total is now emitted via a sweep over the faction's bases (drone_total + superdrone_total are per-BASE fields) and turns_to_completion is removed from the vocabulary — the adapter declines to precompute it on correctness grounds and RATE_OF derives it from minerals_remaining anyway. Vocabulary is 10 names, all 10 emitted. title: Directives: attention and override rates need a real game, not a fixture
description:
PlanBlock records in_force/followed/overrode/not_shown per decision, and the harness aggregates them, but every measurement so far is ten replays of ONE captured observation with a hand-written plan. That shows the mechanism works; it says nothing about whether directives help.

What is actually wanted: over a real run, per directive - attention rate (followed/in_force), override rate, and whether the metric moved toward its target. A priority-7 directive overridden on every decision was mispriced. One never overridden may be costing more than it admits. Neither is visible without a game that plays turns.
design: Needs the A1 transport (na-61c) so decisions are applied rather than observed, otherwise a directive cannot influence anything and attention is measuring a counterfactual.
notes:
ANALYSIS HALF BUILT 2026-08-16 (Claude) — `just directive-report`.

I had written this bead off as "needs a running game" and, in the same breath, asserted its
analysis path already existed. Both halves of that were wrong. The rates need a game; the
REPORT did not exist at all.

WHAT `just coverage` ALREADY DID: adherence in aggregate — how often the brain followed
something. What this bead asks for is per-directive, and the difference is not cosmetic. The two
failures named in the description are invisible in an average:

  a priority-7 directive overridden every time    diluted by every directive that was followed
  one never overridden                            looks like success, and is equally consistent
                                                  with a directive that never constrained
                                                  anything

Both are properties of ONE directive across MANY decisions, so the unit of the report has to be
the directive. It now is, and both conditions are called out by name rather than left for a
reader to spot in a column.

THE DISTINCTION IT REFUSES TO BLUR, which PlanBlock's own docstring already insists on:
`unmeasurable` means the world view did not report the directive's metric. That is an ADAPTER
GAP, not a directive that was checked and failed. Folding them together turns a missing field in
one repository into an apparently unhelpful directive in another, and sends whoever reads the
number to fix the wrong thing. So unmeasurable pairs are excluded from the denominator — a
directive is not charged for decisions it could never have been checked on — and reported
separately and loudly.

REFUSALS, both tested: a log with fewer than 20 plan-carrying decisions (this bead's own
premise is that ten replays of one captured observation prove nothing about whether directives
help, so a rate over a handful is exactly the thing not to print), and a log where no directive
was ever in force — which is an outcome rather than an error, and says so.

Verified against synthetic logs carrying all three shapes at once: a mispriced priority-7
directive, a never-overridden one, and one whose metric the adapter never reported. All three
are identified correctly and kept apart.

STILL NEEDS A GAME to produce a log worth reading, and the DESIGN note still holds — attention
is only meaningful once decisions are applied rather than observed, which na-61c delivered. So
the remaining dependency is a run, not a mechanism.

TRIAGE 2026-08-22 (Claude, remote session): still gated on a real game playing turns — attention/override rates over ten replays of one fixture are the mechanism check, not the measurement. The harness side is ready (PlanBlock records in_force/followed/overrode per decision; the headless harness advances turns unattended since na-ie9), so the remaining step is a multi-turn live run on the play machine with directives issued, then reading the aggregates.

title: A1 adapter must emit WorldView.subjects for base.hurry
description: The subjects field is populated today by the bridge in scripts/decision_stability.py, which maps the adapter's 'item' key. When A1 has the adapter emit the contract directly, it must set subjects itself for any surface that decides ABOUT an entity rather than between entities - base.hurry is the known case. Without it that surface retrieves zero facts, which is what it did until now.

title: Decide the same world view N times to measure decision stability
description:
There is currently no way to tell a considered decision from a coin flip that happens to land on a legal option, because every measurement so far is a single sample.

Two Haiku runs on materially the same base.production world view produced different choices (Formers, then Colony Pod). The prompts were not identical, so that is suggestive rather than conclusive - which is exactly the problem: we cannot currently distinguish 'the model is unstable' from 'the prompts differed'.

Build a small harness that submits the SAME world view N times and reports the distribution of choices, plus the citation sets. Cheap, needs no game running (a captured world view from na-observations.jsonl is enough), and it gives three things nothing else does:
  - a stability number per surface, so 'this surface is decidable from what we send' becomes measurable
  - a regression check on world-view changes: if adding a field makes decisions MORE consistent, that is the field earning its place
  - a way to compare models on the same input without playing a game

Note the interaction with na-61c.2: if instability is real, recent-history context is the fix, and this harness is how you would know it worked.
acceptance_criteria: A script that takes a captured world view and a model, runs it N times, and reports choice distribution and mean utilisation; run against base.production and base.hurry with N>=5 and the results recorded in docs
notes:
FIRST MEASUREMENT TAKEN, controlled this time: five byte-identical prompts, Haiku, base.production at Gaia's Landing turn 35, 8 options, 7 facts offered.

  run 1  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod, formers
  run 2  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod
  run 3  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod
  run 4  unit:1  FORMERS      cited formers, colony-pod
  run 5  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod

  stability    0.80  (4 of 5 modal)
  utilisation  0.20 mean (1.4 of 7 facts cited)

So the instability recorded on na-61c.2 is REAL but modest - one flip in five on identical input, not the coin-flip the earlier uncontrolled pair suggested. That earlier observation (Formers vs Colony Pod) is now explained: it was most likely this same 1-in-5, not the prompt differences I hedged about.

Utilisation 0.20 with elimination-citations encouraged, against 0.14 when only the winning option's fact was asked for. Consistent with the na-373 finding that eliminations are real but few.

THE IMPORTANT RESULT is not the number. Run 5 stated 'nearly-complete Colony Pod (18/33 minerals done)'. The world view says minerals_accumulated = 4. It fabricated a state value it had been given correctly - and still reached the right decision, because it took the 15 turns from turns_if_continued rather than deriving it.

That is direct evidence for computing derived values in the adapter, and stronger than the argument that produced turns_if_switched/turns_if_continued in the first place. That change was made because the model got the ARITHMETIC wrong; this shows the precomputed field also insulates the decision when the model misreads the INPUTS. A world view that makes the brain derive things is a world view where a misread propagates into the choice.
close_reason: scripts/decision_stability.py does exactly what the AC asks: takes a captured world view plus a model, runs it N times, reports choice distribution and mean utilisation. Both named surfaces measured at N>=5 and recorded in docs: base.production N=5 (docs/decision-inputs.md:189-193, stability 0.80 / utilisation 0.20) and base.hurry N=10 (docs/directives.md:158-163, 0.60/1.00/0.80 across three plan configs). Extended since by claude_code_brain.py as a second measurement lane.

title: Measure whether LLM-tier decisions actually produce better outcomes
description:
On base.hurry the brain disagreed with the deterministic tier - it hurried a Colony Pod for 100 of 139 credits to save 15 turns, where Thinker declined. The justification was coherent and numerically grounded. Whether it was RIGHT is unknown, and nothing currently could tell us.

Every claim about decision quality so far is about legality, arithmetic and coherence - all of which are necessary and none of which is the actual goal. A brain that reasons beautifully into a worse position is the failure mode this project most needs to detect, and it is invisible in a single decision record.

What is needed is outcome measurement over a run: play the same save forward under llm_factions=0 and under the brain, and compare trajectories on the measures the game itself keeps - base count, mineral output, tech rate, military strength, faction score. The harness makes this feasible now: autoload is unattended, autosave runs every turn, and the world-view store keeps the bytes for replay.

Note the confound: any comparison must hold the fairness profile fixed, since an AI slot inherits difficulty handicaps a human slot does not (AGENTS.md invariant 6). Comparing an LLM-driven AI slot against a native AI slot at a different difficulty measures the handicap, not the brain.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable A/B over at least 30 turns from an identical save, reporting the game's own score components for both arms, with the fairness profile recorded and identical across arms
notes:
BLOCKED IN PRACTICE by na-2mn (epic: expand the deterministic tier onto the 21 no-native-AI surfaces). bd will not record a task->epic dependency, so the link is recorded in notes on both issues.

The reason it blocks: an A/B needs a baseline. On the 21 NO_AI_PATH surfaces there is no native decision at all, so 'the brain decided X' cannot be scored against anything. Measurement on the four surfaces already instrumented (base.production, faction.tech, faction.se, base.hurry) can proceed now, because all four DO have a native answer - start there rather than waiting on the epic.
ANALYSIS HALF BUILT 2026-08-16 (Claude) — `just ab-outcomes` / scripts/ab_outcomes.py.

Producing the two runs needs a game. READING them does not, and that half is now written, so
when someone has a game the analysis already exists and already argues with them rather than
being invented afterwards under pressure to show a result.

THE PART THAT MATTERS IS THE REFUSAL. This bead already names the confound: an AI slot inherits
difficulty handicaps a human slot does not (invariant 6), so comparing an LLM-driven AI slot
against a native AI slot at a different difficulty measures the handicap, not the brain. That
is written down here and would have stayed written down — a note nobody re-reads at the moment
they are looking at a number they like.

So the tool REFUSES rather than caveats. A caveat is something a reader skips; a refusal is not.
Five refusals, each tested against synthetic logs:

  fairness profile differs    slot, difficulty, or the STRUCTURAL handicaps. Handicaps somebody
                              selected are a legitimate difference between arms; ones the engine
                              imposed are the confound, so only those are in the key.
                              --allow-profile-mismatch exists and says "continuing under
                              protest".
  baseline contains llm       then it is not a baseline. Cheap to check, invalidates everything
                              downstream if missed.
  brain arm contains no llm   two engine arms compared against each other report run-to-run
                              noise as a result — the most convincing wrong answer this could
                              give, because the output shape looks entirely right.
  fewer than 30 shared turns  this bead's own acceptance figure. A shorter run measures the
                              opening, which is largely scripted, not the decisions.
  no records with metrics     nothing to compare.

WHAT IT REPORTS: the metrics the GAME keeps — base count, pop, mineral surplus, energy, labs,
military, drones — per arm at the last shared turn, with the delta. Deliberately not measures of
our own choosing: pick the metric the brain happens to optimise and every result is a win.

AND NO VERDICT. There is no "the brain won" line. One save's trajectory is evidence, not a
result, and a script that announced a winner would be quoted as one.

ACCEPTANCE, honestly: "a repeatable A/B over at least 30 turns from an identical save, reporting
the game's own score components for both arms, with the fairness profile recorded and identical
across arms" — everything except *running* it is now built and tested. The run needs a game.

The note about na-2mn blocking this still holds for the 21 NO_AI_PATH surfaces, and the advice
in it is now easier to take: the four applied surfaces all have a native answer, so an A/B on
them can proceed the moment there is a game, without waiting on the epic.

TRIAGE 2026-08-22 (Claude, remote session): the measurement still needs what only the play machine has — the same save advanced under llm_factions=0 and under the brain, same difficulty so the fairness profile stays fixed (invariant 6). Autoload, autosave and the world-view store make it feasible; nothing in a cloud container can advance a Windows game. New datum for whoever runs it: the na-qu8 run (2026-08-22) measured agreement 0/20 with the deterministic tier on base.hurry in BOTH arms — the brain confidently overrides Thinker on the exact surface this bead's motivating disagreement came from, which raises the value of settling whether those overrides are better or just confident.

title: Narrow retrieval using the utilisation signal
description:
Grounding utilisation scales inversely with action-space width, measured with the same model, graph and retrieval path:

  base.production   8 options   7 facts offered   1 cited   utilisation 0.14
  base.hurry        2 options   1 fact offered    1 cited   utilisation 1.00

Retrieval currently fetches one fact per offered action, so a wide surface pays for facts the decision never turns on. Six of seven were unread on the production decision.

This is retrieval tuning, not prompting. Options, cheapest first:
1. Rank rather than fetch-all: keep the batched query, then order facts by relevance to the current state (e.g. affordable-this-turn first, category matching the base's evident need) and truncate. The token_budget machinery in datalinks/budget.py already truncates; it just has nothing to rank by.
2. Two-pass: cheap facts for every option, rich facts only for a shortlist the brain asks about. Costs a round trip.
3. Learn from citations: fact ids are stable across turns and runs by construction, so accumulated citation counts per (surface, fact) are a usable prior. This is the K3 learned-memory path and depends on na-bdn.

Start with 1. Measure utilisation before and after over the same set of decisions - the instrumentation makes this a number rather than an argument.
acceptance_criteria: Utilisation on base.production rises materially over a sample of at least 20 decisions with no drop in decision quality; the ranking rule is documented and its inputs come from the world view rather than from the graph alone
notes:
PREMISE TESTED AND REFINED - the original framing over-claimed, but the conclusion survives.

The worry was that utilisation 0.14 measured citation CONVENTION rather than waste: a brain that compares 8 options and cites the 1 that won has arguably used all 7 facts, 6 of them to eliminate. So the same decision was re-run asking for citations in three buckets - facts that supported the choice, facts that helped RULE OUT an option, and facts that influenced nothing.

Result:
  DECIDED     unit:colony-pod                         1
  ELIMINATED  fac:recreation-commons                  1
  UNUSED      5 facts, named explicitly by the model  5

So eliminations are real but rare - one, not six - and utilisation rises only from 0.14 to 0.29. Five of seven facts influenced nothing by the model's own account. The waste is real and worth reducing.

Two caveats to carry forward, both of which weaken the number without overturning it:
  - Self-reported 'unused' is weak evidence. A model's introspection about what influenced it is not reliable, and this is the best signal available rather than a good one.
  - Utilisation should COUNT eliminations. Measuring only what supported the winner systematically under-reports, so the instrumentation's definition of 'cited' must include 'helped rule out'. That is a semantics change in what we ask the brain for, not a schema change - Orders.cited already carries a list.

Revised approach: keep ranking as the fix, but do NOT rank by desirability. Ranking cheap-and-soon options first would ground the affordable options better than the expensive ones, which biases the choice through retrieval - a worse failure than wasted tokens, and an invisible one. Rank by expected information value instead: an option whose name does not imply its effect needs a fact; 'Scout Patrol' largely does not.
close_reason:
RESTORED by ellie 2026-08-02 (aegis-uae2s). This bead was closed on 2026-08-01T04:47:21Z and
commit 36d67d0 reverted it to `open`.

Evidence it was a lost write and NOT a deliberate reopen: the durable JSONL carried
status=closed with the full reason below at b99b3ba; the embedded Dolt store's record for this
bead still read `updated_at: 2026-07-30T04:09:09Z` — OLDER than the close itself. 36d67d0
exported that stale store over the good JSONL, so the store's omission became the durable copy.
A record that predates its own close cannot be a reopen of it.

The original close reason follows, unaltered.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Approach refuted and reverted; the cost problem re-filed as na-vbe with the shape a fix must have. Option 1 (rank then truncate) was implemented and measured over 20 decisions per config on Haiku: utilisation 0.22 to 0.28, but only because the denominator shrank, and the decision changed (Network Node 19/20 to Research Hospital 15/20) with stability falling 0.95 to 0.75. The ranking rule predicts citation worse than chance - 0.43 of citations in its top four against 0.50 for noise - and the one fact cited in 20 of 20 decisions ranked fifth of eight. Generalisable finding recorded in docs/quipu-integration.md: grounding is one fact per option, so top-k truncation removes the explanation of an option rather than removing information, and an unexplained option loses; any such truncation biases the choice whatever it ranks by. Shipped from this work: DatalinksRetriever now emits fact_ids, without which the K1 path could not be cited against at all and utilisation was structurally unmeasurable. Harness kept at scripts/retrieval_utilisation.py.

title: Central mod_popp wrapper: intercept in-game dialogs as decision points
description:
Wrap the engine's dialog function popp(filename, label, a3, pcx_filename, fn) (engine.h:667) so every in-game dialog is visible to the adapter and routable to Claude.

This is invariant 7 made real: 'Intercept in-game dialogs; never blanket-suppress them. They are decision points.' Council votes, diplomacy offers, random events and pact proposals all arrive as popp dialogs, and each is a decision surface the brain should own. Only Thinker's fatal-error MessageBoxA should ever be suppressed.

Precedent exists: Thinker already hooks individual popp call sites - base_production_popp at patch.cpp:681 and BaseWin_staple_popp at 753-754 - so wrapping centrally is the same technique applied once instead of per site. Identify dialogs by (filename, label), which is what the call already passes.

IMPORTANT distinction, do not conflate these:
  - IN-GAME dialogs (events, diplomacy, council) are decisions. Intercept, emit a surface_id, route to the LLM tier where appropriate. Core architecture, and a whole class of surfaces at once.
  - MENU and file-picker chrome (the LOAD dialog) is not a decision, just startup plumbing. Do NOT build automation for it - fix the -na-autoload menu-to-session transition instead so no picker is ever needed. Automating the picker is throwaway work.

Note also that the LOAD picker is not a popp dialog and runs its own message pump, which is why the command channel goes deaf inside it (see na-abc).
acceptance_criteria: A single hook observes every popp dialog with its filename and label; each observed dialog is recorded with a surface_id; a documented allowlist controls which are auto-answered vs routed vs passed through to the human; Thinker's fatal-error MessageBoxA remains suppressed and nothing else is blanket-suppressed
notes:
PARTLY DONE 2026-08-16 — the central hook is built. Thinker c544903, NeuralAmplifier 2177e41.

THE CENTRAL HOOK, and it turned out to need no binary patching at all. popp is not a symbol
Thinker calls directly: engine.h declares `extern Fpopp popp` and engine.cpp binds it to
0x48C0A0, so every one of the ~50 popp calls in the fork goes THROUGH that pointer. Writing
a wrapper into the pointer intercepts all of them at once. The bead asked for "the same
technique applied once instead of per site" — this is once, and it is not even a write_call.

The wrapper captures whatever engine.cpp bound rather than naming the address again, and is
idempotent: chaining it onto itself would double every record and then recurse.

ACCEPTANCE, item by item:

  "A single hook observes every popp dialog with its filename and label"
      PARTIAL. One hook, and it sees every dialog THINKER raises. Dialogs the ENGINE raises
      from its own code call the real function directly and are not seen. Reaching those
      needs each call site's address, which needs terranx.exe, which this repo deliberately
      does not have (invariant 8). This is the one criterion that cannot be finished here,
      and it is a genuine external blocker rather than a scoping choice.

  "each observed dialog is recorded with a surface_id"          DONE, with a caveat below.
  "a documented allowlist controls which are auto-answered vs routed vs passed through"
      PARTIAL. The table exists and documents chrome vs decision. AUTO-ANSWER AND ROUTE ARE
      NOT IMPLEMENTED and the table does not pretend they are — there are two dispositions,
      not four. Routing needs an action space, and see the next paragraph for why there
      isn't one.
  "fatal-error MessageBoxA remains suppressed and nothing else is blanket-suppressed"
      DONE. The engine's return is passed through unchanged on EVERY path, including for
      unrecognised dialogs. na_message_box is a different function, untouched.

WHY A DIALOG RECORD IS NOT A WORLD VIEW. The hook cannot build an action space: a dialog's
buttons live in a game text file keyed by label, and that is data we do not ship. Emitting a
contract-shaped record with an empty or invented action space would be a decision record for
a decision nobody could make, and it would count toward coverage. So it emits the compact
form the na_verify_* divergence records already use — surface_id and facts, no tier, no
applied — which the harvester is documented to skip rather than mistake for a capture. This
is also why routing to the brain is not implemented: there is nothing to offer it yet.

THE TABLE IS EVIDENCE, NOT GUESSWORK, and this was a deliberate restraint. 14 entries, every
(file, label) pair grep-able in the fork's own source; each label verified to occur at a real
call site besides its own table entry. I could have filled it with plausible-looking labels
for council votes and diplomacy — the surfaces this bead is really after — and it would have
matched nothing while looking like coverage. That is the failure this project has already
paid for twice (a policy in the wrong namespace, a Cargo feature that made the parser
silently inert). Instead an unrecognised dialog is RECORDED and flagged mapped:false, which
turns the unknown part of the inventory into something one real game collects. `dialog-stats`
separates "the table matched nothing" from "no dialog was raised" — an empty log looks
identical either way and only one is a bug.

NO COVERAGE MOVED. None of the mapped surfaces entered OBSERVED. The hook has never been seen
firing against a real game, and surfaces.py exists to stop exactly this from inflating the
number before it has.

Verified: builds clean, 43 wire checks green, 655 orchestrator tests. The C++ table was diffed
MECHANICALLY against the orchestrator's transcription rather than eyeballed.

STAYS OPEN on two things, one external and one not:
  - engine-raised dialogs need the game binary (external).
  - auto-answer/route needs an action space, which needs the dialog text files (external),
    OR a per-surface hand-authored action space in the adapter (not external — real work,
    and the right next step for the specific surfaces na-nmg cares about).
AUTO-ANSWER LANDED 2026-08-16 — two of the three dispositions are now built.
Thinker 7de00bc, NeuralAmplifier follows.

The bead asks for "a documented allowlist controls which are auto-answered vs routed vs passed
through to the human". Pass-through and chrome shipped with the hook. This is auto-answer.

WHAT IT SOLVES, and why it is not a nicety: a popp dialog in an unattended run blocks forever.
The engine draws it and waits for input nobody will give. na_message_box already applies exactly
this policy to the Win32 path — dismiss an MB_OK, exit NA_EXIT_UNANSWERABLE on a real question —
and the popp path never reaches that function. This is the same policy where it was missing.

THREE GATES:

  headless only   In code, not in a comment. Answering while a human is sitting there would take
                  their decision away, which is what invariant 7 forbids. With nobody there the
                  alternative is not "the human decides", it is "the run hangs" — so the
                  invariant is the REASON for the gate rather than an obstacle to it.
  notices only    New NA_DIALOG_NOTICE kind: one-button "this happened to you" reports where
                  returning 0 dismisses. NERVESTAPLE2 stays DECISION and is never answered — it
                  asks whether to nerve staple, and a question's button indices live in a game
                  text file we do not ship. Picking one would be inventing an answer to a
                  decision with consequences. Unrecognised dialogs are not answered either.
  off by default  An unconfigured build reaches the engine exactly as before.

THE NOTICE/QUESTION SPLIT IS SEMANTIC AND HAS TO BE. Every one of these is raised with the
identical popp(file, label, 0, image, 0) shape — nothing in the call distinguishes a report from
a question. The classification comes from what the label means at its call site, and each is
grep-able in this fork. That is a weaker basis than a structural test and it is the only one
available, so the safety property is pinned on the orchestrator side instead: a test asserts
NOTICE and DECISION never overlap and that NERVESTAPLE2 is in the second.

Every auto-answer is recorded with auto_answered:true, through a SEPARATE entry point rather
than a parameter on na_observe_dialog — so the ordinary path cannot accidentally claim a dialog
was auto-answered — and counted in dialog-stats. A run that answered forty dialogs on the game's
behalf did not have the same run as one that answered none.

ROUTE IS STILL UNBUILT, and I want to be precise about why rather than calling it blocked. A
routed dialog needs an action space, and the button labels are in the unshipped text files. Two
ways forward and neither is a one-liner:
  - ship nothing and read the labels at runtime from the player's own install (they have the
    files; we do not), or
  - hand-author an action space per dialog in the adapter, which is real work per surface and
    only worth doing for the dialogs na-nmg actually wants.
The second is not external. It is the right next step for this bead and I am not calling it
done.

STILL NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A RUNNING GAME. No dialog has been raised through this hook.
ALL THREE DISPOSITIONS BUILT 2026-08-16. Thinker f10683f, NeuralAmplifier follows.

The bead's acceptance asks for "a documented allowlist controls which are auto-answered vs
routed vs passed through to the human". All three now exist:

  passed through   default for everything; the engine's return is unchanged
  auto-answered    one-button notices, headless only, off by default
  routed           posts the surface's world view and returns the button the brain chose

ROUTING IS A NO-OP TODAY AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, not a shortfall dressed up. Routing means
RETURNING a button index, and which index means "yes" is in the game's text file keyed by label
— data we do not ship. Every entry's mapping is -1/-1 and a dialog with no mapping is never
routed however it is configured.

The refusal is why building it was safe. A guessed index would not fail loudly; it would take a
real action in a real game and look exactly like the brain deciding. Filling the mapping in is
two integers per dialog from someone's own install — small, checkable, and not mine to guess.

Only base.staple is wired to a world view, reusing na_build_base_staple. A per-dialog action
space is per-dialog work, and inventing one for a dialog nobody has looked at is the same
mistake as guessing buttons.

THREE PARTIES CAN ANSWER A DIALOG NOW — engine, harness, model — so there are three record
shapes and three entry points rather than one with flags. A log that cannot say which answered
is not a record of what happened. dialog-stats reports routed= and route_refused=.

WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS BEAD, precisely:
  1. Button mappings for any dialog worth routing. Needs an install. ~2 integers each.
  2. A world view for any DECISION dialog beyond base.staple. Needs someone to decide which
     dialogs na-nmg actually cares about; the work is per-dialog and NOT external.
  3. Engine-raised dialogs remain out of reach — they call popp directly rather than through
     the pointer, and reaching them needs per-call-site addresses from the binary.

(1) and (3) need the game. (2) is real work waiting on a scoping decision, not on anything
external.

TRIAGE 2026-08-22 (Claude, remote session): unstarted; it is thinker DLL work (a central popp wrapper at engine.h:667's seam) needing the cross-compile toolchain and a live game to verify dialog interception — not buildable from this container. It remains the unlock for na-nmg's third blocker (diplo.tribute is a raw engine pointer, interceptable only through mod_popp) and for the whole dialog class of surfaces.

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## The remaining criterion is not blocked the way this bead says — and the premise under it is wrong (harding)

thinker `b97d2b9` + `f1a111c` on origin/master. The bead records the last open item —
*"a single hook observes every popp dialog with its filename and label"* — as PARTIAL, blocked
on *"each call site's address, which needs terranx.exe, which this repo deliberately does not
have."* That is **"a genuine external blocker rather than a scoping choice"** in the bead's own
words. It is neither, and chasing it produced something more useful than the feature.

### 1. It never needed a single call-site address

Patch the ENTRY POINT, not the call sites. `write_jump` already exists and is already used
elsewhere in the fork for exactly this shape. popp's address is in `engine.cpp:451` — no
terranx.exe required to learn it, and no reverse engineering.

Built: a hand-written trampoline. `jmp rel32` at 0x48C0A0, with the nine-byte prologue
(`push ebp` / `mov ebp,esp` / `mov eax,fs:[0]`) relocated and continued at popp+9. **Nine, not
five**, because a jump may not split an instruction and byte 5 lands inside the fs-relative
move; none of the three is relative, so relocating them needs no fixups. Verified against the
binary before patching, in `write_call`'s idiom, and it falls back to the pointer swap on a
prologue it does not recognise.

When it installs, the `popp` pointer is **deliberately left alone** — every caller then arrives
through the entry point, and doing both would run `na_popp` twice on every dialog the fork
raises.

### 2. How much the pointer swap was missing: 194 call sites

Measured on the shipped binary: **194 direct `E8` call sites targeting popp** in `.text` that
the pointer never sees, plus 5 for `popp_2`. So the existing hook reached roughly a fiftieth of
the calls, and nothing said so.

### 3. ⚠️ A static scan of terranx.exe is WRONG unless you apply Scient's patch table first

The finding most worth carrying past this bead. `patch_setup` applies `AXPatchData` — **3127
byte patches** — before any `write_call`, so **the runtime image is not the file on disk**.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| Thinker's 572 `write_call` sites that look like a call ON DISK | **562** |
| after applying AXPatchData | 563 |
| the remaining 9 | all at `patch.cpp:1296+`, i.e. optional-feature blocks |

**`0x4F7A38` — the base.hurry site this session just spent a census on — is one of the ten.**
On disk it is `FF A1 30 EA 90`; `{0x4F7A38, 0xFF, 0xE8}` in `patchdata.h` turns it into a
relative call at load. I read the raw file first, concluded the patch site was invalid, and was
about to treat a working patch as broken. Anyone scanning the shipped binary is reading a binary
the game never runs.

### 4. And then the measurement that changed the conclusion

With the entry hook installed, a full turn holding a **NETFLASH notice** AND a **COMMUNICATIONS
OFFICER dialog** — *"I have Provost Zakharov of the University on Channel 4. Shall I put him
through?"*, three options and an OK — reported:

    dialog-stats: seen=0 unmapped=0 auto=0 routed=0 route_refused=0 table=14 installed=1 reach=entry

**Positive control on the same run**, because a zero from a hook is worthless without one: the
`observe-dialog` probe took it to `seen=1 unmapped=1`. The observer works, the flag is on, and
the zero is trustworthy.

So **neither of those dialogs goes through `popp` at all.** That contradicts this bead's premise
— *"Council votes, diplomacy offers, random events and pact proposals all arrive as popp
dialogs"*. At least two of those classes do not, and the central hook this bead asks for would
not have seen them however it was installed. The comms dialog is precisely the surface the bead
is after, and it arrives by some other path (`popp_2` has 5 call sites and is the first place I
would look; a distinct modal window class is the other).

I got that zero wrong twice before trusting it, which is why the control is in the record:
`dialog_observe` is spelled **`na_dialog_observe`** in the ini, and I first wrote the struct
field name, then put the right key after the file's `; Enf of config` marker. Two runs of
"the hook sees nothing" that were really "the observer was off".

### 5. Therefore it ships DISABLED, and that is the finding acting rather than caution

`na_dialog_entry_hook=0` by default. Enabling patches a hot engine entry point in a game a
person plays, for a benefit currently measured at zero — **the trampoline has never carried a
real dialog**. The mechanism is built, documented and one ini key away; the default changes
nobody's game.

Both arms proven on a real game: option absent -> `reach=pointer`, `=1` -> `reach=entry`, and
neither run regressed the base.hurry census (136/136).

### 6. The change that helps regardless: `dialog-stats` reports `reach=`

`installed=1` was ambiguous exactly where it mattered. It said a hook existed and nothing about
whether the engine's own dialogs were in scope — and a log of zero dialogs looks identical
either way. That ambiguity is most of why this criterion sat unfinished: there was no way to
tell "no dialogs were raised" from "dialogs were raised somewhere this hook cannot see".

### What is still open on this bead

The acceptance criterion stands, and now has a shape: **find the path the engine's real decision
dialogs actually use.** Start at `popp_2` (5 call sites). The other two criteria — auto-answer
and routing — are unchanged and still blocked on button indices from game text files this
project does not ship, which IS a genuine external blocker.

Also fixed in passing: `.gitignore`'s last line was `.cmake/__pycache__/` — one rule until
`f2bec14` (na-alr.1) appended to a file with no trailing newline. It ignored neither, both
halves failing silently. Repaired in `f1a111c`.

title: Command channel goes deaf inside the engine's modal dialogs
description:
The in-DLL command channel (thinker fork, na_command_tick) is polled from ModWinProc. The engine's modal dialogs - the LOAD file picker among them - run their own message pump, so the window procedure stops being called and the channel stops responding while one is open. Verified: a 'shot' and a 'click' issued with the LOAD dialog open produced no result file at all.

The dialog is drawn INSIDE the game window rather than as a native Windows control (xdotool sees no separate X window for it), so it is not separately addressable from outside either. External input does not reach this game in any case - it reads the mouse through DirectInput under a Wine virtual desktop.

Consequence: automation can open a modal dialog but cannot act inside one. That is enough to reach the LOAD picker and no further, which is exactly one click short of useful.

Candidate fixes:
1. Hook something that runs during modal pumps. popp() and the Console/dialog handlers are the obvious candidates - find one that is unconditionally patched.
2. Avoid dialogs entirely: fix the -na-autoload menu-to-session transition so no picker is ever needed. That is the better goal and is tracked separately as the load_game transition bug.
3. A timer-based tick (SetTimer plus a WM_TIMER handler, or a worker thread) that survives modal pumps. A thread would need care - the engine is not thread-safe.

Approach 2 makes this issue moot for the resume use case, which is the only current consumer. Prefer it.
notes:
Confirmed WORSE than originally described, and now moot for the resume use case.

A worker thread does NOT survive modal dialogs. Input was moved onto a dedicated thread on the reasoning that PostMessage is thread-safe and a thread is independent of the message pump. A heartbeat counter disproved it: the thread ticked normally at the startup screen, froze at the exact instant the picker opened, and never resumed while the process stayed alive. Two plausible causes were tested and eliminated - the picker does not change the working directory, and switching the thread from stdio to Win32 file APIs did not help despite Thinker sharing a single global FileLock with the game (patch.cpp:14-20).

So the constraint is architectural: while a modal dialog is open, NO code of ours runs. Anything needing interaction inside a modal is unreachable.

Moot for resume because na-c9f is solved by never opening a modal (QUICK START instead of LOAD GAME). Keep this open only as a documented limit - if some future surface genuinely needs input inside a modal, the answer is probably to avoid that dialog, not to defeat the pump.

Separate finding worth its own note: in-game input does not reach the engine through posted messages at all. The startup screen and dialogs accept WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_KEYDOWN; the map UI does not - it reads DirectInput. So ending a turn cannot be driven from outside the process, which is why an 'observe <base_id>' test hook exists in the DLL.
close_reason:
Closing as a documented limitation, not a fix. There is no code left to write and it has been cluttering the ready pool.

The bead's own notes record it is WORSE than filed and moot for the motivating case: a dedicated worker thread does NOT survive a modal dialog (heartbeat froze at the instant the picker opened and never resumed), and the two plausible causes were tested and eliminated. So the candidate fixes are dead ends, not unattempted work.

The mitigation shipped: -na-autoload reaches a playable session via click_quickstart / confirm_planetfall (thinker src/neural.cpp:2250,2264) rather than the LOAD picker, so automation never needs to act inside the modal that motivated this.

The limit is documented at docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md:202. Re-observed this session while driving turns: the command channel goes silent during a modal and returns when it closes, exactly as described - so the documentation is accurate and current.

title: just ingest should refuse a mod-contaminated alphax.txt
description:
The canonical ingester reads $SMAC_DIR/alphax.txt and tags the output canonical. If $SMAC_DIR points at a directory with Thinker installed over it, that file is Thinker's - house-rule data laundered into the canonical smac: graph, violating AGENTS.md invariant 4.

fixtures/smac/overlays.tsv already maps known mod hashes to their source, and scripts/game_fixture.py uses it to detect exactly this. Wire the same check into the ingest path: hash the input, and if it matches a known overlay, abort with a message pointing at just ingest-thinker instead. Cheap, and it closes the hole at the point of harm rather than relying on the operator remembering.
