title: Restore vanilla data files and resolve the 17 unresolved manifest paths
description:
fixtures/smac/steam-2204130.manifest is marked INCOMPLETE: 17 paths held Thinker v5.4 bytes when scanned and carry no vanilla hash - alphax.txt, german/alphax.txt, and 15 basenames/*.txt. Thinker was installed directly into the Steam directory and overwrote them (verified byte-identical to Thinker_v5.4.zip).

Needs a human action in the Steam client: Properties > Installed Files > Verify integrity of game files. That re-downloads tracked files and leaves untracked additions (thinker.dll, thinker.exe, smac_mod/) alone. Then run 'just game scan' to regenerate a complete manifest - it will now succeed without --allow-contaminated.

alphax.txt is the one that matters: 'just ingest' labels it canonical, so ingesting Thinker's copy would mislabel house-rule data as game-canonical (AGENTS.md invariant 4). Do NOT run 'just ingest' against the play directory until this is resolved. basenames/ and german/ are cosmetic and block nothing.
acceptance_criteria: just game scan succeeds with no --allow-contaminated flag; manifest header has no INCOMPLETE block; just game verify passes; just ingest produces a canonical smac: graph from vanilla alphax.txt
notes:
Longer-term: $SMAC_DIR should be a pristine tree and the play directory a separate copy with the mod overlaid. See docs/headless-harness.md 2.4 and fixtures/smac/PROVENANCE.md.
RECURRENCE FIX LANDED 2026-08-16 (Claude) — `just game stage`.

The repair itself still needs a human at the Steam client, and nothing here changes that. What
DID exist as implementable work is the second half of this bead's own Longer-term note:
"$SMAC_DIR should be a pristine tree and the play directory a separate copy with the mod
overlaid".

WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING BEFORE THE REPAIR. The contamination was not carelessness — it is what
happens when Thinker's install instructions and the fixture's requirements name the same
directory. Verifying integrity in Steam fixes today's 17 files and leaves that collision exactly
where it was, so the next mod install re-breaks it.

`just game stage` copies the pristine tree to a play directory and overlays the mod THERE.
Three refusals, each tested:

  contaminated source   Refuses if the source already holds mod bytes for any manifest path,
                        naming the file and which mod it came from. Copying a contaminated tree
                        would produce a play directory that looks staged and carries the same
                        overwritten alphax.txt — this bug wearing a fresh directory name. The
                        message points at the Steam repair.
  overlapping target    Refuses a target equal to, containing, or contained by the source. All
                        three write to the tree whose whole job is to stay untouched.
  existing target       Refuses without --force rather than silently replacing a directory
                        someone may be mid-run against.

And it VERIFIES alphax.txt is byte-identical after staging rather than assuming it. "I only read
from it" is precisely what the original install also believed, which is why that check is an
assertion and not a comment.

alphax.txt is the file that matters and the bead already says why: `just ingest` labels it
canonical, so ingesting Thinker's copy mislabels house-rule data as game-canonical (invariant
4). That contamination is invisible downstream — the graph looks the same either way.

Tested against a synthetic tree, including the contaminated case built to reproduce this bead:
it refuses, names alphax.txt and "Thinker v5.4", and creates nothing. Two tests in
test_play_preflight.py pin the source-is-never-written property and the overlap refusals.

ACCEPTANCE IS UNCHANGED AND UNMET: `just game scan` still needs a repaired tree, which needs
Steam, which needs the machine with the install. This does not close the bead. It means that
once you do repair it, the tree stays repaired.

TRIAGE 2026-08-22 (Claude, remote session): remains a HUMAN action on the game machine — Steam client > Properties > Installed Files > Verify integrity, then 'just game scan'. Nothing in a cloud container can touch that Steam install, and the guard this bead exists for still matters: do not 'just ingest' against the play directory until the 17 Thinker-overwritten paths carry vanilla hashes, or house-rule alphax.txt data gets labelled canonical (invariant 4).

title: Supply an embedding model so quipu_context works
description: Filed upstream as scbrown/quipu#53. quipu knot does not embed (only /episode does), --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', and --features onnx supplies the runtime not a model. Needs .bobbin/config.toml with model_path/tokenizer_path plus the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 files. huggingface.co is NOT on the Claude Code cloud Trusted allowlist, so either add it to a Custom allowlist or vendor the model. Exact-match SPARQL grounding is unaffected and works today.
notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16 (Claude) — three alternatives ruled out, and half the artefact is
obtainable after all.

I had been reporting this as "blocked on the CDN" without testing whether a different file, a
different format or a different model would route differently. It does not, and now that is
measured rather than assumed:

  huggingface.co                                            200
  us.aws.cdn.hf.co                                          CONNECT 403
  sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 tokenizer.json     200, 466247 bytes
  sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 config.json        200, 612 bytes
  sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 onnx/model.onnx    403 via the CDN
  Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 onnx/model_quantized.onnx         403 via the CDN
  minishlab/potion-base-8M model.safetensors                403 via the CDN

THE SPLIT IS LFS, NOT SIZE OR REPO. Anything in LFS/xet redirects to the CDN and is refused;
anything huggingface.co serves directly arrives. So a smaller file does not help, a quantised
variant does not help, and a different model does not help — all three were worth one command
each to rule out, and all three are the obvious next thing someone would try.

PyPI is reachable (files.pythonhosted.org 200), so a package that BUNDLED weights in its wheel
would work. The usual candidates do not: they download from HF at runtime, which lands back
here.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE SCRIPT:
  - it now fetches config.json as well, and KEEPS a partial fetch. The tokenizer is a real
    466 KB artefact that does not change, so a later run needs only the one blocked file
    rather than starting over.
  - `--check` diagnoses reachability in seconds instead of a 90 MB timeout.
  - the ruled-out alternatives are in the header, so the next person does not repeat them.
  - models/ is gitignored, since the bead is explicit the weights are never committed.

The bead's original remedy — "add huggingface.co to a custom allowlist" — remains wrong, and now
demonstrably so from three angles rather than one. The host to allow is us.aws.cdn.hf.co.

STILL BLOCKED, and the blocking part is one allowlist entry that is not mine to grant. What is
no longer blocked: the tokenizer and config are on disk, and the diagnosis takes one command.

TRIAGE 2026-08-22 (Claude, Stiwi's remote session, complete-all-beads pass): the blocker re-measured and still holds. From this cloud container: huggingface.co resolves and serves small files, but the ONNX weights 302 to us.aws.cdn.hf.co and the proxy answers 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' — byte-identical to the 2026-08-16 measurement. Cannot be completed from a remote container regardless: the deliverable is model files + .bobbin/config.toml on the HOST that serves the quipu store (127.0.0.1:3030 on the play machine), so the remaining step is Stiwi downloading all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (tokenizer.json fetches fine; model.onnx needs an unproxied network) onto that host and pointing config at it. Exact-match /query grounding remains unaffected and in production use.
close_reason: Embeddings work on this host: 345 entities backfilled, semantic search scoring Recycling Tanks 0.587 for 'a facility that reduces waste' with no lexical overlap. The CDN block was a Claude Code cloud property, not the artefacts — us.aws.cdn.hf.co is 200 from the homelab. A SECOND blocker underneath it: quipu-server PANICS on a missing libonnxruntime.so rather than reporting a missing provider; the script now fetches it from PyPI and just quipu-serve puts it on LD_LIBRARY_PATH (no version pin — 1.24.1 and 1.29.0 both work). Two traps recorded: the section is [quipu.embedding] not [embedding], and an empty /context is reproducible with a fully working provider.

CORRECTION 2026-08-16 (Claude) — this bead's stated remedy is wrong, and following it would waste an afternoon.

The description says "huggingface.co is NOT on the Claude Code cloud Trusted allowlist, so either add it to a Custom allowlist or vendor the model." Measured from a cloud container just now:

comments.author: harding
comments.text:
## Closed — embeddings work here, and the blocker was never the artefacts (harding)

`13309f1` on `wt/harding`. Two blockers, and only the first one was known.

### 1. The CDN block is a property of the CLOUD environment, not of the files

This bead has been open since 2026-07-29 on "one allowlist entry that is not mine to grant". The
2026-08-16 re-measurement was careful and correct — three alternatives ruled out, the LFS/xet
split identified precisely — and every one of those measurements was taken inside a Claude Code
cloud session. Measured on **this host**:

| host | cloud session (bead) | homelab (now) |
|---|---|---|
| `huggingface.co` | 200 | **200** |
| `us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (weights) | **CONNECT 403** | **200** |
| `files.pythonhosted.org` | 200 | 200 |

The 90 MB model downloads in seconds. Nothing about the artefacts changed; the environment did.
`scripts/fetch-embedding-model.sh --check` now reports all three, so "is this still blocked?"
stays a one-command question wherever it is asked.

### 2. A second blocker underneath it, which nobody had reached

With the weights on disk, `quipu-server --embed-backfill` does not report a missing provider:

    Failed to load ONNX Runtime dylib: failed to load from `libonnxruntime.so`: dlopen failed
    thread 'main' panicked

The model is data; **`libonnxruntime.so` is the engine that reads it**, and Quipu's `ort` crate
dlopens it at startup. A panic reads as a broken build rather than a missing dependency, so this
would have cost the next person a diagnosis even with the CDN open — and it was invisible until
the first blocker was cleared.

Fetched from PyPI now, by the same script, into `models/onnxruntime`. **No version pin**:
`ort 2.0.0-rc.11` loaded 1.24.1 and 1.29.0 alike, both measured. `just quipu-serve` puts the
directory on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so it is a mechanism rather than a step to remember, and it is an
empty prefix when the library is absent — a host without it starts exactly as before.

### Working, end to end, through the recipe rather than by hand

    $ just quipu-serve .quipu/na.db 127.0.0.1:3031 true
    ONNX embedding provider loaded (dim=384, auto_embed=true)
    Backfill complete: 345 entities embedded

    $ curl .../search -d '{"query":"a facility that reduces waste"}'
      0.587  Recycling Tanks. type: Facility ...
      0.431  Headquarters ...
      0.388  Clean Reactor ...

**"a facility that reduces waste" scores Recycling Tanks top with no lexical overlap at all.**
That is the property exact-match SPARQL structurally cannot have, and the reason this bead
exists. Run against an isolated copy of the store on :3031 — the live one on :3030 serving
`NA_QUIPU_URL` was never touched, and I checked it afterwards.

### Two traps, recorded because each one costs an hour

**The config section is `[quipu.embedding]`, not `[embedding]`.** This script printed the latter
and `docs/quipu-integration.md` had the former; the script was wrong. A wrong section name is not
rejected — it is never read, and the server reports `No embedding provider configured`, which is
character-for-character what it says with no config at all. So the failure of a typo and the
failure of a missing file are the same message.

**⚠️ An empty `/context` is NOT evidence the embeddings are missing, and this bead's own symptom
is reproducible with a fully working provider.** Measured just now:

| query | `/context` |
|---|---|
| `"how does a Recycling Tanks facility affect a base"` | **0 entities** |
| `"Recycling Tanks"` | the facility, with facts |
| `"Formers"` / `"Terraforming Unit"` | likewise |

`/context` matches entity text tightly; `/search` handles the looser query. The bead says
"`/context` returns zero entities against a knotted graph — it does not error, which is exactly
the kind of quiet emptiness worth knowing about in advance". That is right, and it is quieter
than it looks: the same emptiness survives fixing the thing it was blamed on. Ask `/search`
before concluding anything.

### Scope, unchanged

Nothing in the decision path depended on this and nothing does now: `QuipuRetriever` posts to
`/query`, never `/search`. What this buys is `quipu_context` and semantic search — the K3 memory
path and anything that wants to find a concept it cannot spell. Weights stay out of git
(`models/` and `.quipu/` gitignored), as the bead requires.

DONE: orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/hank.py CitationGuard. Verifies that facts a brain cited were actually offered and actually resolve, with three distinct advisories because they have three different causes and fixes: fabricated citation (model), offered-but-unresolvable (datalinks integrity), offered-but-uncited (retrieval nobody reads). Verdict is warn, never deny - a suspect justification does not make an order illegal, and role (c) is explicit that legality is the engine's. A throwing resolver returns 'cannot say' rather than a violation. 8 tests.

Wired in service.py _build_guard: on whenever retrieval is, since citation integrity is meaningless without grounding. NA_HANK_GUARD=0 disables. Before this no guard was wired at all, so hank_absent was true on every decision.

This is a LOCAL STAND-IN for Hank's POST /guard, not Hank. The verdict shape and warn/deny semantics are already what that surface returns, so swapping implementations should not change the record.

STILL TO DO: roles (a) engine-mechanics grounding via hank_promote, (b) dev-time guardrail, (d) the hot in-memory game-state graph, (e) what-if over the live board. Also the real policies from the doc - garrison-border-bases, hold-expansion-under-threat, don't-break-a-pact-without-casus-belli - all of which need role (d) first because they reason over board state, not over citations.

UPDATE 2026-08-16 (1) - roles (c) and (d) are now WIRED, against yupana rather than a net-new Hank service.

orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/yupana.py speaks yupana's MCP surface (yupana_ingest / yupana_guard) and implements the same Guard protocol, so it composes into GuardChain beside StateGuard and CitationGuard with no change anywhere else. Role (d) - the hot board graph - is yupana's, already built: per-tenant, copy-on-write, with the order-boundary evaluation role (c) needs on top of it. Opt-in on NA_YUPANA_URL, policies from NA_YUPANA_POLICIES.

The local StateGuard is deliberately KEPT and stays first: it needs no service and answers affordability for free, so an unreachable yupana costs a degraded advisory rather than the arithmetic check.

Verified live against yupana 0.6.0 (--features mcp,game-state). See na-qzy for the detail.

UPDATE 2026-08-16 (2) - role (e), what-if over the live board, is WIRED.

what_if on the MCP surface, backed by yupana_whatif: speculative (yupana applies to an overlay, commits nothing), structural only, and it neither claims nor answers the decision so an agent can try three options and submit a fourth. Verified live: hurry:now on 200 reserves reports 'smac:energy_reserves: 200 -> 119', committed=false.

Getting it onto that surface required fixing something first, and the fix matters more than the tool. test_mcp_server.py holds an explicit rule - NO TOOL MAY OFFER A SECOND SOURCE OF BOARD STATE. what_if only qualifies if the board it speculates over is composed entirely from the decision's own world view. That was FALSE as first written: yupana's ingest merges, so entities from earlier decisions survived into this one.

Fixed at the source rather than worked around: yupana 0.6.1 gained a replace flag on ingest (scbrown/yupana a0bbd1e, 3 tests) and NA sends it from both the guard and what_if. Scoping a fresh game_id per decision was the obvious alternative and does not work - yupana's tenant cap REFUSES rather than evicting, deliberately, so it would exhaust 64 tenants and then refuse everything.

That also fixed a real bug in the guard shipped earlier the same day: without replace, a base razed twenty turns ago survived every later ingest that did not list it and went on matching policy selectors, so the brain was warned forever about a base it no longer owned. Verified end to end: warns on turn 42, silent on turn 60 once the world view stops listing the base.

Version floor: NA now requires yupana >= 0.6.1. An older one ignores the unknown field and merges, so the regression is SILENT - filed as na-fni to check the mechanism in the preflight rather than trusting a version string.

REMAINING on this epic: roles (a) engine-mechanics grounding via hank_promote, and (b) the dev-time guardrail. Neither is started.


---

UPDATE 2026-08-16 (3) - roles (a) and (b) are now WIRED. All five roles of this epic have an implementation.

ROLE (a), engine-mechanics grounding (K4). `just code-graph` runs `yupana export` over the fork's src (13,379 facts as bobbin:CodeModule / bobbin:CodeSymbol) and knots datalinks/computed-by.ttl, which links each surface and engine metric to the symbol that decides it via smac:computedBy. Verified: base.production -> select_build -> build.cpp, base.hurry -> mod_base_hurry, base.retool -> mod_base_making, faction.tech -> mod_tech_val, garrison_count -> garrison_count, units_in_foreign_territory -> whose_territory. Six hops, all resolving.

Every link was READ, not inferred. A computedBy pointing at a plausible-sounding function is worse than no link: it looks like provenance and is a guess, and the whole value of the plane is that "the engine does X" stops being something someone remembers. Line numbers are in the file so a re-check is cheap. IRIs are file.cpp::function, so an engine rename breaks the hop loudly rather than pointing at the wrong code.

ROLE (b), dev-time guardrail (K5). .bobbin/config.toml holds three structural rules over this repository's own invariants - a swallowed degradation in the knowledge/board-guard/memory seams, an engine name leaking into orchestrator.py (invariant 2), and code equating degraded with deterministic. Run by `yupana hook pre-edit` from a PreToolUse hook on Edit|Write. Advise mode, and it fails open twice: the shell guard makes a missing yupana silent and exit 0, and yupana itself passes the edit on a bad config or blown deadline.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING, and it applies to both roles: yupana parses Python and C++ only with the `langs-extra` Cargo feature. Without it, the pre-edit guard finds no applicable rule for a .py file and says NOTHING - correctly, since "this build cannot parse the language" is not a gap worth reporting in a Rust repo - and `yupana export` over C++ produces an empty file and exits 0. Both failures look exactly like success. I hit the first one and only noticed because I tested a violation and expected a warning. Each rule is now verified to fire on a violating edit and stay silent on a clean one, `just code-graph` refuses an empty export, and the build flag is documented in .bobbin/README.md where someone debugging silence will look.

Not the whole of role (b): the architecture wants the rules projected from Quipu's aegis:Policy rows rather than authored in a file. The field names mirror those atoms 1:1 (query is aegis:Selector.evidenceSource, pattern is aegis:Predicate.evidenceSource, match_type is aegis:matchType) so that move is a projection, not a rewrite - the same shape policies/board.ttl took for the board plane. Signing for role (a) promotion is still unkeyed.

UPDATE 2026-08-16 (4) — role (b) is now WHOLE. The gap this bead named is closed.

The remaining half of role (b) was: "the architecture wants these rules projected from
Quipu's aegis:Policy rows rather than authored in a file". policies/preedit.ttl is that
canonical form, and NeuralAmplifier d94a373 lands it.

WHAT THE MOVE REQUIRED, and why none of it was obvious. The pre-edit plane is not the
board plane with different content — it is read by a different consumer, and three things
differ. Each one fails as SILENCE rather than as an error, which is the whole reason they
are asserted in tests instead of trusted:

  - aegis:boundary must be "action", NOT "order". "order" is yupana's own extension for
    the game pre-apply seam and is what policies/board.ttl correctly uses. Copying that
    value across is the natural mistake and projects zero rows.
  - the Selector needs aegis:tier "tree-sitter" and aegis:language. A committed-tier
    policy has no structural evidence and is deliberately left to quipu's write gate.
  - the namespace is http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/, not the https://aegis.local/
    one board.ttl uses. Each is fixed by its consumer: we own the board query in
    yupana.py, yupana owns the pre-edit one in src/project_queries.rs. Wrong namespace
    parses fine and matches nothing.

A guard with no rules is indistinguishable from a guard with nothing to complain about.
That is the failure mode all three share.

A REAL BUG FOUND FROM THE OTHER SIDE, fixed in scbrown/yupana 35ebc90. Writing these rows
surfaced that yupana's projection hardcoded `applies_to: Vec::new()` and its POLICY_QUERY
never asked for aegis:appliesTo — so EVERY projected structural policy applied to every
file of its language. A policy quipu had scoped to one module was enforced repo-wide.
Nothing had caught it because a rule firing in more places looks like a rule that works.
It only showed up here because no-engine-specifics-in-the-orchestrator is scoped to a
single file and unscoped would fire on every string comparison in the package.

The fix also had to handle the multi-valued case: SPARQL returns one row per glob, so the
decoder now accumulates them instead of collapsing to whichever arrived first, and
differing scopes are explicitly NOT treated as the conflicting-definitions error a
differing pattern or effect is — that would have refused every policy scoped to more than
one glob. 5 tests.

TWO REPRESENTATIONS, HELD TOGETHER. .bobbin/config.toml is still what runs: projection
needs a quipu holding the rows and a [yupana.quipu] endpoint. So the TTL is the governed
plane and the TOML the operational one, and they drift silently in the direction that
matters most — the TOML executes, so a stale TTL describes governance nobody is subject
to. orchestrator/tests/test_preedit_policies.py compares every field both ways and fails
on a rule present in one and absent from the other. It reads the TTL through rdflib, not
a regex, because the claim being made is that the file is valid projectable governance.

Each of the five failure modes was verified to actually fail by breaking the file. Worth
recording: one of those negative checks was WRONG at first — it mutated the header comment
rather than a triple and passed, which would have left the boundary assertion looking
verified when it was untested.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN ON THIS EPIC: signing for role (a) promotion is unkeyed. That is the
only item from the original five roles without an implementation.
UPDATE 2026-08-16 (5) — role (a) signing: the mechanism is complete, the last step is a
human's, and that is now one command instead of undocumented.

This was the only item from the original five roles without an implementation. Reading it
through, "signing is unkeyed" is not a missing feature — it is a missing HUMAN ACTION, and the
distinction matters because building past it would be actively harmful.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, on yupana's side: ed25519 key generation with 0600 custody
(verdict.rs load_or_generate), verdict signing, local spooling, a `yupana verifier` command that
prints the public key, and a promote path. All of it mirrors quipu's signing.rs deliberately, so
a yupana-signed verdict verifies under quipu's root of trust. The ring dependency has been in
Cargo.toml the whole time.

WHAT IS MISSING: a registration. A signature means nothing until its public key is recorded in
quipu as an `aegis:VerifierRegistration`. yupana's own docs call this the "human-owned
VerifierRegistration root of trust", and verdict.rs describes the pubkey as what "a human pastes
into" that registration.

WHY I DID NOT JUST DO IT. Generating a key and registering it would produce something that looks
cryptographically trusted and is not: the tool would be asserting its own trustworthiness, which
is the one claim a signature cannot make about itself. Nothing downstream can tell a key a human
vouched for from a key that vouched for itself — which is exactly the property the registration
exists to provide. Minting a root of trust is also precisely the kind of thing Human Input
Sovereignty reserves to a human action.

WHAT I BUILT INSTEAD: `just signing-identity`. It creates the key if absent (0600), prints the
public key, and prints the exact TTL to knot — then stops. The recipe's own comment says why the
last step is not automated. docs/knowledge-architecture.md K4 no longer says only "signing is
still unkeyed"; it says what is built, what is missing, and that the gap is a decision rather
than an absence.

So role (a) is now: wired, signed on the way out, and awaiting one human `quipu knot` to mean
anything. That is a better state than either "unkeyed" or a self-signed key pretending
otherwise.
close_reason: All three roles are wired and verified; closed 2026-08-22 on the evidence in docs/knowledge-architecture.md. Role (c) policy guard: CitationGuard (hank.py) plus StateGuard, deny/warn/allow rulings with bounded repair — reserves-stay-solvent verified end to end (deny -> re-ask with the claim -> legal alternative, one decision, repairs:1). Role (d) hot per-faction COW state graph: served by yupana rather than a net-new Hank service — per-tenant copy-on-write board, yupana_ingest with replace so the world view IS the board, graph-pattern policies at the order boundary via yupana.py, joining the guard chain behind the local guards under NA_YUPANA_URL, dead-guard-allows recorded. Role (e) what-if: what_if on the MCP surface speculates over an overlay composed entirely from the decision's own world view and commits nothing. The one known gap this bead could have held open — base policies warning but unable to deny because order effects were not expressible on the board — was extracted to na-n72 (order-scoped board_effects), which is itself closed and in the contract (contract.py board_effects).

title: K2: per-turn Quipu retrieval and budgeting
description: quipu_context plus action-space grounding via one batched SPARQL VALUES query over this turn's action_space, plus hybrid-search tactics k=3 confidence-gated. Token budget: drop tactics before rules. Degradation already handled by the seam. K2.
close_reason: Split: the budgeting half landed, the semantic half is blocked and now has its own bead. Landed: datalinks/budget.py enforces an approximate token ceiling and sheds tactics before rules -- rules are correctness, tactics are optimization, and that ordering is the same precedence the prompt enforces, so the budget cannot invert the trust ordering to save tokens. A single greedy pass in list order would have let a long tactic at the front crowd out a rule behind it, so it fills by precedence class instead, and it keeps scanning past an oversized fact since a later shorter one may still fit. Nothing is dropped silently: the surviving grounding carries an explicit '[N tactics omitted for token budget]' line, because a truncated prompt that reads as complete is the same failure shape as the all-fallback run. Wired as QuipuRetriever(token_budget=N), default 0 = unbounded since the action-space cap already bounds the common case. BLOCKED (na-9tk): quipu_context and quipu_hybrid_search need vectors; quipu knot does not embed, --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', --features onnx gives the runtime not a model, and huggingface.co is not on the cloud Trusted allowlist so the model cannot be fetched from a session. Documented in quipu-integration.md. 12 new tests; 189 pass with a live quipu 0.3.11.

title: K3: learned memory write and recall
description: Postgame extraction to mem: episodes, bitemporal per-game and durable, tactics into the prompt. Exit: a tactic learned in game N surfaces in game N+1. K3.
close_reason:
Done — and the exit criterion this bead sets is met, not approximated: a tactic learned in game N surfaces in game N+1, verified against a real quipu-server rather than a mock.

orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/memory.py, three separable parts:
- episodes(log) turns a finished game's decision log into mem: nodes and edges. Pure, no store, no network.
- MemoryStore.write() posts them through quipu_episode, which is what buys prov:wasGeneratedBy for free — the architecture is explicit that memory is written through episodes and never as free Turtle, and provenance is the reason.
- MemoryStore.recall() reads durable tactics back as prompt lines; RememberingRetriever appends them behind whatever rulebook grounding exists, and works with none at all.

Plus `neural-amplifier learn <log>` with --dry-run, and NA_MEMORY_QUIPU_URL wiring in _build_retriever.

BITEMPORAL SPLIT AS SPECIFIED: per-game nodes to memory:game:<id>, durable tactics to memory:durable, as two separate episodes. One episode would need the reader to re-split by node type at write time.

TWO EXCLUSIONS CARRY MOST OF THE VALUE. A deterministic-tier record says what the engine would have done anyway, so learning from it teaches the brain the fallback's habits and then reads the agreement as evidence the brain was right. A degraded record is worse: it exists BECAUSE the brain could not answer, so the chosen action is the fallback's — a tactic built from those is a habit learned from the brain's absence. Both are tested.

A TACTIC IS A CLAIM, NOT AN INSTRUCTION. It carries its observation count and a confidence capped at 0.6, because a habit repeated many times inside one game is not a law of the game. mem:Outcome (confirmedBy/refutedBy) is how it earns or loses ground once outcomes are wired — na-6db.

Tactics deliberately get NO citable fact_id. Those resolve against datalinks nodes and a tactic has none; minting one would make CitationGuard resolve it to nothing and report a fabricated citation on a fact we invented ourselves.

Two things learned from quipu by probing rather than assuming, both now recorded in the module: quipu REFUSES a prefixed node type (mem:Tactic) rather than silently rewriting it to mem_Tactic — a good refusal — so types are bare and only names carry the prefix; and it mints IRIs into http://aegis.gastown.local/ontology/ with description landing as rdfs:comment and properties as aegis:<key>, which is what the recall query had to name.

17 tests, 16 offline plus the live exit-criterion round trip.

title: A1: POST the world view and apply Claude's build choice
description: First end-to-end LLM decision in a real game. Wraps mod_base_build to serialize state to the contract, call POST /decide, and apply the returned action. Keep the DLL thin.
notes:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-07-29. Input requirements are specified per-category in the new docs/decision-inputs.md section 2 - build the world view to that checklist, not ad hoc.

Orchestrator side ALREADY EXISTS: service.py serves POST /decide taking a WorldView and returning
Orders (contract.py). So A1 is DLL-side work only.

Item encoding (thinker src/base.cpp): item_id >= 0 is a unit proto id, item_id < 0 is a facility
with id -item_id, range 1..SP_ID_Last=133. So action ids should be 'unit:<proto>' and
'facility:<id>' - reversible, and it keeps engine ids out of the contract as bare integers.

Action space must be engine-authoritative via can_build(base_id, item) and
can_build_unit(base_id, unit) (base.h:68-69). Never synthesise an option. Enrich each Action with
mineral cost, turns at current surplus, category and a one-line effect - contract.Action is
extra=allow so this needs no schema change. A bare name list is not a decidable comparison and
will bias the brain toward expensive items.

Gate: ask on call_seq == 1 only and reuse the answer for the rest of the base-turn (see
thinker 73fbdbc). One decision, one record, one paid call.

Fallback is the feature, not the error handler: on timeout, transport failure, malformed response,
or an action_id outside the offered space, return native_choice and mark the record degraded.
Wire it from the first commit - invariant 9.

Faction scope: narrow llm_factions from 254 to a single slot. Per the faction-gate commit
rationale, prefer a human slot with manage_player_bases=1 over an AI slot, because an AI slot
silently inherits difficulty handicaps and makes any outcome uninterpretable.

Still to build in the DLL: an HTTP client (none exists - net.cpp is a stub and only user32/gdi32/
winmm/psapi are linked; plan is raw ws2_32 for 127.0.0.1 rather than wininet, which is slow and
quirky under Wine), world-view serialisation, minimal JSON response parsing, and the apply path.
close_reason:
A1 landed in the thinker fork (commit 8317f96, subject is this bead's title). Every element the DESIGN note listed as 'still to build in the DLL' is present: raw ws2_32 HTTP client (src/na_http.cpp:322-401), world-view serialisation, JSON response parse, and the apply path. Hook at src/base.cpp:1218. call_seq gate at neural.cpp:956-959 gives one decision, one record, one paid call. Fallback-is-the-feature wired from the first commit (neural.cpp:1000,1036-1044): applied=native_choice with tier deterministic and a fallback_reason on unreachable/slow/malformed/illegal. Action ids validated against the offered space via na_parse_item_id + na_item_is_legal. Both children already closed.

Live-run verification is NOT part of this close - that is na-1wu (and na-ckn, which now looks like a duplicate of it).

title: Replay mode and determinism diffing
description: Observability step 7. Feed stored world views back through a changed orchestrator with no game running and diff the decisions. Determinism diffing only holds for scripted-brain runs; real-model runs need the weaker assertion of same surfaces fired and same legality.
close_reason: Machinery landed and tested; recording a real game is na-oh5. Dropped the na-04z dependency: the replay path needs stored world views, not an adapter that stamps surface_id -- that was a mis-specified blocker. replay.WorldViewStore is content-addressed by the record's own world_view_hash (the blocker found on starting was that the record carries only the hash and nothing kept the bytes, so a log alone could never be replayed). Two verdicts kept separate: deterministic (exact, scripted only) and consistent (no new degradation, same surfaces fired) -- the trap is a replay where the fallback happens to pick what the brain picked. Wired as NA_WORLD_VIEW_STORE, 'neural-amplifier replay' and 'just replay', plus stored() for fixture harvesting.

title: OpenTelemetry exporter fed from the same emit call
description: Observability step 6. Layer 2. Earns its keep because Quipu and Hank are separate services and without shared trace context a slow turn cannot be attributed. Must be fed from the single DecisionLog.write call, never assembled twice.
close_reason: Layer 2 landed in orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/telemetry.py. Emitter takes the already-built DecisionRecord and hands the same instance to every sink, so 'assembled once' is structural -- the test asserts object identity, not field equality. DecisionLog is just the first sink and is written first, so an exporter failure still leaves the record of truth on disk; sinks never raise into the decision loop and failures are counted on Emitter.failures and surfaced at GET /health. OtelSink continues the adapter's W3C traceparent rather than starting a new trace (dependency-free strict parser, 10 malformed cases rejected), reconstructs span timing from latency_ms since the decision is already over, sets ERROR status on degradation, and emits the section 6 metrics with a bounded-cardinality attribute subset. Enabled with NA_OTEL=1 and the otel extra. 27 new tests against an in-memory tracer -- no collector, no game. Also fixed a real crash path: _record read world_view.trace.traceparent, which AttributeErrors on a model_copy-constructed view and would stall the game after the decision; now WorldView.traceparent() tolerates both shapes.

    Running embedding backfill for all entities...
    Backfill complete: 345 entities embedded
    quipu-server listening on 127.0.0.1:3030 (db: .quipu/na.db)

### Verified by /search, and by the path that was already working

You said to verify by `/search`, not `/context`, and to treat an empty `/context` as
uninformative. Both directions measured, before and after, on the same query:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/search "a facility that reduces waste"` | `no embedding provider configured` | **count 10** — Recycling Tanks **0.587**, Headquarters 0.431, Clean Reactor 0.388 |
| `/query` (SPARQL — the decision path) | 200 | **200** |
| orchestrator `/health` | ok | **ok**, `game_id game-df4afe47` unchanged |

The before-row on `/search` is the control that makes the after-row mean something: the provider
was genuinely absent, not merely unqueried. And `/query` is checked on both sides because that is
the path `QuipuRetriever` actually uses — the one thing this restart could have broken and the
one thing that had no reason to change.

### Two things done carefully rather than quickly

**The live store was backed up before the backfill wrote to it.** `--embed-backfill` is a write
over the database serving grounding, and 345 embeddings landing in a file is not something to
attempt with no way back. Copy at
`…/scratchpad/na6td/na.db.live-backup-20260823-004546` (1134592 bytes, pre-backfill).

**The shared checkout was 8 commits behind and had local `.beads` churn**, so the pull would have
refused. Rather than discarding it I checked what it was: exactly one record differed, `na-yd4`,
local `open` and origin `closed` — bd's auto-export taken moments before my own close, i.e.
strictly stale. Stashed with a message, ff-pulled, confirmed the checkout now reads `closed`, and
dropped my own stash. `git stash` is shared across worktrees here (aegis-pxzi4), so leaving an
unexplained one is a hazard for the next agent.

### Note on the section name you flagged

Confirmed the right way round: `[quipu.embedding]` is what the server reads, and the config
arrived with the pull rather than being hand-added. Worth repeating your warning because the
failure is silent — a wrong section reports `No embedding provider configured`, which is
character-for-character what it says with no config at all, so a typo and a missing file are
indistinguishable from the outside.

title: Sync upstream on a cadence rather than on discovery
description:
Policy, not code, and the smallest item here — but it is what makes the rest compound.

The v5.5 sync was triggered by someone noticing a release, not by a schedule, and by then the gap was 6 commits and a structural refactor. Upstream tags releases (v4.1 through v5.5 are all present as tags on induktio/thinker), so 'sync on tag' is a well-defined trigger that does not require watching master.

Once na-alr.5 exists the cadence gets cheap: CI already knows whether upstream merges clean, so a sync becomes a scheduled read of an answer that is already computed rather than an investigation.

Record the decision somewhere durable — docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md already carries the fork's operating knowledge and now has a v5.5 banner at the top that names the current sync branch.
acceptance_criteria: A stated sync trigger (upstream tag, or CI reporting a dirty trial-merge) written down where the next person syncing will find it.
close_reason: Recorded as section 5.3 of docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md, where the next person syncing will find it. Two triggers in authority order: the weekly drift job going red (it trial-merges and re-runs the seam checks, so it fires while the gap is still small), and upstream tagging a release (they have tagged steadily v4.1..v5.5, so it needs nobody watching master). Also records the lesson the conflict count hides — v5.5 produced three textual conflicts but required eight seams re-placed by hand, because git takes a deletion of code you have edited without complaint — and says to run check_seams.py after resolving, before believing the build.

title: Replace the six MessageBoxA substitutions with a compat header
description:
Every one of main.cpp's six invasive lines is the same edit: MessageBoxA -> na_message_box. patch.cpp carries three more of the same.

Each is a modified upstream line, which is the kind git actually conflicts on, and they sit in error paths upstream touches whenever it adjusts a message.

A na_compat.h carrying '#define MessageBoxA na_message_box', included once per host file, turns nine invasive edits into one additive include each. Macro-shadowing a Win32 entry point is not elegant and should be called out in a comment at the definition, but it is contained, it is exactly what na_message_box already is, and the alternative is re-resolving nine modified lines on every release.

Check first that na_message_box's signature matches MessageBoxA exactly, including return value, so the substitution stays a substitution and not a subtle behaviour change — the -na-headless routing already depends on the return value at the video-player prompt, which is the one dialog that asks a real question.
acceptance_criteria: No call site spells na_message_box directly; nine invasive edits become per-file includes; the -na-headless behaviour of all three patch.cpp dialogs is unchanged (still refusing to answer the video-player question); build clean with zero warnings.
close_reason:
WON'T DO — premise measured and did not hold. The bead assumed these lines sit in error paths 'upstream touches whenever it adjusts a message'. Measured across all 435 upstream commits: only 13 (~3%) touch MessageBoxA in main.cpp/patch.cpp, the most recent 2025-08-11, and v5.5 — the release that motivated this epic — touched NONE of the nine. So the demonstrated cost is zero conflicts in the one release we have data for, against nine obvious one-line resolutions when it does happen.

Against that, the mitigation is worse than the disease: na_message_box calls MessageBoxA on its non-headless path (neural.cpp), so '#define MessageBoxA na_message_box' would infinitely recurse in any file that both defines and uses it — survivable only with an #error trap in neural.cpp. And the macro makes main.cpp read MessageBoxA while calling ours, which cuts against a codebase where every seam carries a paragraph saying what it does and why.

Signature compatibility was checked and is exact (HWND, const char*, const char*, UINT -> int), so this is reversible cheaply if the trigger changes. REVISIT IF: a future upstream release actually conflicts on these lines, or the count grows well past nine.

title: Document llm_timeout_ms in docs/thinker.ini
description:
Found while verifying the v5.5 sync (na-15o.4), pre-existing rather than caused by it — it is absent from docs/thinker.ini on master too.

llm_timeout_ms parses fine (main.cpp option_handler) and the adapter notes §6 list it as one of the three settings that drive the bridge. It is also the most consequential of the three to leave undocumented: it is not merely a local timeout, it is SENT to the orchestrator as decision_deadline_ms so the orchestrator can abandon a decision before the engine does. Without it an attached agent's late answer gets recorded as an applied tier=llm decision the game never used — the exact failure na-t3h measured at 66 adapter rows, zero of them tier=llm.

The fork's convention is to document options at their point of use, and its two siblings llm_factions and llm_endpoint already are. Note the two edge behaviours worth stating: the default is 2500, and a value <= 0 means wait-indefinitely, in which case decision_deadline_ms is OMITTED rather than sent as 0.
acceptance_criteria: docs/thinker.ini documents llm_timeout_ms alongside llm_factions and llm_endpoint, including the default, the decision_deadline_ms relationship, and the <= 0 omission behaviour.
close_reason: docs/thinker.ini now documents llm_timeout_ms at the point of use, explicit at its real default of 2500, covering the decision_deadline_ms relationship and the <=0 omission rule. Each claim verified against code before writing it (main.h:196, na_http.cpp:234, neural.cpp:302, na_wait's single absolute deadline). Also fixed the na_http.cpp comment that argued from 'thinker.ini carries no override', which this change made false. Committed df408c6.

title: test_orders_are_serialised is timing-flaky under load
description:
Observed 2026-08-16: tests/test_orders.py::test_orders_are_serialised failed once with 'every order reached the adapter' (len(seen) == 4 got fewer), then passed on an immediate re-run with no code change. The failing run took 15.11s against a usual 6.2s, on a machine also running two cargo release builds and two servers.

Mechanism, from reading the test: four threads each call channel.issue(..., timeout_s=3.0) while a fake adapter thread polls with time.sleep(0.005) between reads. Under enough load one caller exceeds its 3s deadline before the adapter drains its order, so `seen` is short and the assertion fires.

So it is a real timing dependency, not a real serialisation bug — the property under test (orders are serialised, each caller gets its own result) is not what failed.

NOT fixed here, because the tempting fix is wrong. Raising timeout_s to hide it makes a slow-serialisation regression invisible for longer, and the test exists to catch exactly that. Options worth weighing:
(a) drive the fake adapter off an event rather than a 5ms poll, so the test is bounded by scheduling rather than by wall-clock sleep;
(b) keep the wall-clock but assert on serialisation ORDER over however many completed, and let a separate, generously-timed test assert that all four complete;
(c) mark it as needing a quiet machine and keep it out of the pre-push gate.

(a) looks right — it removes the clock from a test whose subject is not the clock. Filed rather than done because a flaky test in a pre-push gate erodes the gate, and this one is currently green often enough that a wrong fix would be worse than the flake.
close_reason:
Fixed with option (a) from the bead — take the clock out of a test whose subject is not the clock.

Root cause, now that it is written down precisely: the fake adapter looped `for _ in range(600)` with a 5ms sleep, so it served for about 3 seconds. The four issuers each allowed `timeout_s=3.0`. Those are the SAME budget, so on a loaded machine the adapter stopped polling while a caller was still waiting — and the test then failed claiming an order never reached the adapter, when what actually happened is that nobody was listening any more.

Fix: the adapter runs until the test sets an Event, with a 30s safety net far above any real run so a genuine hang still fails rather than hanging the suite. Poll interval dropped 5ms -> 1ms. The issuers' 3s timeout is UNCHANGED, deliberately — that is the assertion about serialisation speed and raising it would hide the regression this test exists to catch, which is why the bead ruled that fix out.

Verified rather than assumed: ran the test three times concurrently under six busy-loop CPU hogs — all passed. Runtime went from 15.11s on the failing run to 0.65-0.86s, which is the mechanism confirming itself: the old test was spending its time waiting out a fixed adapter lifetime. Full suite green three consecutive runs (608 passed).

title: Bump the yupana floor to 0.6.1 in the preflight
description:
yupana.py now sends replace:true on every ingest, which needs yupana >= 0.6.1 (the version where StateRegistry::ingest grew the flag). An OLDER yupana ignores the unknown field and merges — so the failure is silent and is exactly the staleness bug replace was added to fix: a base razed twenty turns ago keeps matching policy selectors, and what_if can surface an entity the current world view never carried, which breaches the MCP surface's no-second-source-of-board-state rule.

'just play check' currently only tests that yupana ANSWERS. It should also establish the version, or at least prove replace is honoured — e.g. ingest two nodes, re-ingest one with replace, and check the other is gone. That is a mechanism check rather than a version string, which is the better shape anyway: it tests the property NA depends on rather than a number that could be reported by a build without the feature.
close_reason:
Done — as a MECHANISM check rather than a version string, which is what the bead asked for.

scripts/play-preflight.py check_replace: ingest two nodes into a scratch tenant, re-ingest one with replace:true, and read the board size back. One node means the flag is honoured; two means this yupana predates 0.6.1 and is silently merging.

A version check would have been the obvious thing and the wrong one: an older yupana does not REJECT the unknown field, it ignores it, so nothing on the wire distinguishes 'honoured' from 'discarded' except the effect. The check tests the property NA actually depends on.

Its own scratch tenant (game_id na-preflight), so a game in progress is untouched — and replace on a tenant this function invented cannot clear anything a real one holds.

Reported optional, never blocking: a degraded guard is not a reason to refuse to play, and the row says exactly what breaks — the guard warns about bases you no longer own, and what_if may report entities the world view did not carry.

Two tests cover both directions with a fake client, and the live path was run against yupana 0.6.1: 'yupana replace  optional  honoured — the board is stated, not patched'.

title: Project board policies from Quipu instead of a JSON file
description:
NA_YUPANA_POLICIES points at a JSON file (policies/board.example.json). That is deliberately a starter: policies are governance, authored in Quipu and projected, and a file in this repo is a second copy that drifts.

The guard already passes policies per call rather than letting yupana hold them resident, precisely so the source can change without touching the guard — a resident copy would enforce yesterday's governance while looking current.

Acceptance: policies are read from the Quipu store (projected aegis: policy nodes) with the file remaining as a fallback for a run with no store. A run should be able to say which policy set it played under.
close_reason:
Done. Board policies now project from a Quipu store, with the JSON file demoted to a fallback.

policies/board.ttl is the authored source, as aegis:Policy nodes with aegis:Selector / aegis:Predicate. NA_POLICY_QUIPU_URL points at a store; load_policies (service.py) projects via POLICY_QUERY and policies_from_quipu (yupana.py). NA_YUPANA_POLICIES is consulted only when the store cannot be read, and the fallback is LOGGED — guarding with a stale file while saying nothing is how a run ends up enforcing rules nobody can point at. A fallback, never a merge: two live sources of governance is the drift this bead exists to remove.

The mapping is a RENAME, not a translation, and that was worth establishing before writing any of it. The field names are quipu's own governance vocabulary (shapes/aegis-properties.ttl: aegis:boundary, aegis:effect, aegis:targets, aegis:claim, aegis:selector, aegis:predicate) and yupana's StatePolicy deserialises exactly that shape in snake_case — its Boundary::as_str is documented as 'the wire spelling of aegis:boundary'. So there is no second ontology here to drift. boundary 'order' is yupana's own extension of the aegis action/transition split, for the FR-36 pre-apply seam.

Only order-boundary policies are handed to the board guard. Quipu's graph holds the whole agent's constraints including pre-edit code rules; one written for a different seam would come back 'unevaluated' on every decision, and filtering says the same thing more usefully.

VERIFIED END TO END, not just unit-tested: knotted board.ttl into a real quipu store (45 facts), served it with quipu-server on 3031, projected all three policies, and ran them through the live yupana guard — reserves 40 against a hurry costing 81 denied with the policy's own claim, the garrison policy firing pre_existing on an exposed empty base, and the third correctly vacuous. Fallback path verified too: an unreachable store logs twice and loads the file.

5 unit tests cover the projection shape, the boundary filter, the optional targets field, and the empty-store case. One lint finding fixed on the way: the row accessor was a lambda closing over the loop variable (ruff B023), now a module-level helper — and its docstring records why unquoting matters, since a literal that keeps its quotes yields a selector that silently matches nothing.

title: bd export with no -o writes to stdout, silently leaving the tracked JSONL stale (docs/UX)
description:
`bd export` with NO output path can write a STALE JSONL — silently, and in the one direction
that loses work. Measured 2026-08-03 while closing na-1p2.

## Reproduction, exact

    bd -C <na> close na-1p2 ...
    bd -C <na> show na-1p2 --json   -> status: closed, closed_at: 2026-08-03T07:43:43Z   (live store, correct)
    bd dolt commit                  -> "Nothing to commit."                              (working set clean)

    cd <na> && bd export                       # default path .beads/issues.jsonl
      issues.jsonl says: in_progress | closed_at: None      <-- STALE

    bd export -o /tmp/na-fresh.jsonl           # explicit path, same store, seconds later
      fresh export says: closed | closed_at: 2026-08-03T07:43:43Z   <-- CORRECT

Same binary, same store, same second. The ONLY difference is whether an output path was given.

## Why this is the mechanism behind two prior incidents

`.beads/export-state.json` carries `{"last_dolt_commit": ..., "timestamp": ..., "issues": 69}`.
The default-path export is watermark-gated on it; the explicit-path export is a full live dump.
When the watermark says nothing changed, the default export rewrites the file from the stale
snapshot rather than declining to write — so it produces a COMPLETE-LOOKING file with the right
id count and the wrong field values.

That is exactly the signature recorded on this repo before:
  - 36d67d0 "export the embedded store to JSONL — 14 beads existed only in local Dolt"
  - 3a0158a "restore nine closes that the last export reverted"
Both were repaired by hand. Neither identified why, and the id-set check that came out of them
CANNOT catch this: the id set is identical (69 before, 69 after, none added, none removed). Only
a per-record FIELD diff catches it, which is why that rule exists — and this is the first time
the rule has actually fired rather than being a precaution.

## Workaround (use this until fixed)

    bd export -o /tmp/fresh.jsonl && cp /tmp/fresh.jsonl .beads/issues.jsonl

then diff BOTH the id set AND the field values against a pre-write snapshot before committing.
Script used here: it fails the run if any id disappeared, if any record went closed -> not-closed,
if a record this write did not touch moved at all, or if the intended change is ABSENT (which is
the case that fired today).

## Severity

A stale export is not a cosmetic issue on this repo: the JSONL is the git-tracked tracker, so a
stale write silently REVERTS closed beads for everyone who pulls, and the revert looks like a
normal export commit. It has already cost two manual repairs.

NOT YET INVESTIGATED: whether the watermark is stale because `bd close` does not advance it, or
because the embedded engine commits without updating export-state. Both are cheap to check.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-16 (Claude) — the open question in ellie's retraction is now answered, and
it is a real gated-export path. na-2a9's retraction was right about everything it retracted.

ellie flagged one thing as UNTESTED and explicitly declined to assert it: "if an interval-gated
auto-export does capture pre-write state, that WOULD be a genuine stale-write path — but someone
has to prove it first." Proving it was cheap, and it reproduces.

THE MECHANISM, measured on this store:

  bd comment na-2a9 "..."      -> .beads/issues.jsonl updated, export-state.json advances
  bd comment na-2a9 "..."      (immediately after)
                               -> issues.jsonl UNCHANGED, exit 0, no warning, no stderr
  bd export -o /tmp/fresh      -> store has BOTH comments; tracked file has one

So `bd` DOES auto-export on write, and that auto-export is GATED. A write shortly after a
previous export does not export and says nothing. Both writes succeed and both land in the
store; only the tracked file falls behind.

This is NOT the thing ellie retracted. Her retraction is correct: `bd export` with no -o writes
to stdout and touches no file. The gate is on the AUTO-export, which is a different path, and
her measurement (issues.jsonl and export-state.json written 6ms apart at the moment of a close,
carrying pre-close state) is exactly this.

IT BIT TWICE IN ONE SESSION, which is how I noticed. Both times the shape was identical: a
`bd update --append-notes` exported, the `bd close` seconds later was gated out, and the commit
carried the new notes with the OLD status. Caught both times only because I diff the export
before committing. na-lnv and na-5vv, both self-corrected on the next export.

WHY REVIEW CANNOT SEE IT: a stale export is a well-formed file with the right id count and the
wrong field values. The id-set check that came out of the two prior hand repairs cannot catch it
— the id set is identical. Only a per-record field diff does.

GUARDED ON OUR SIDE (NeuralAmplifier). The bd behaviour is upstream and this bead is the right
place for it, but the footgun is ours to survive:

  scripts/beads-export.py    always `bd export -o` (never the auto path, never bare `bd export`
                             which writes to stdout), diffs the result against HEAD, and REFUSES
                             to install a regression: an id that vanished, a closed bead going
                             not-closed, notes or comments shrinking. Verified against all four
                             cases including that a clean export passes.
  just beads-export          the command to use instead of `bd export`
  just beads-check           exits 1 if the tracked file lags the store
  pre-commit hook            runs --check on any commit touching .beads/issues.jsonl, so a
                             gated write cannot reach a commit unnoticed

Verified end to end: two rapid consecutive `bd comment` writes leave the tracked file stale,
`just beads-check` exits 1 naming the record, and the pre-commit hook fails the commit. The
notes-shrink arm also catches the OTHER bd footgun I hit this session — `bd update --notes`
REPLACES rather than appends, and it silently destroyed an audit on na-lnv before I noticed.

UPSTREAM ASK, unchanged from ellie's: a warning when an auto-export is skipped while a tracked
.beads/issues.jsonl exists. Exit 0 with no output is the whole problem; the gate itself is
reasonable.

(The probe comments above this one are from that experiment and can be deleted.)
TWO BD WARNINGS, ONE MASKING THE OTHER — 2026-08-17 (Claude). Same UX family as this bead.

This bead is about a bd behaviour that succeeds, says nothing useful, and leaves someone with a
wrong belief. Two more of the same shape turned up, and the second only because the first was
fixed.

1. `.beads has permissions 0755 (recommended: 0700)`

   Real: the directory holds the Dolt issue database, readable by anyone on a shared machine.
   It fired on roughly FORTY commands in one session and I ignored every one — which is the
   actual finding. A warning that fires on every invocation stops being a warning and becomes
   part of the prompt.

   Fixed in scripts/setup-environment.sh rather than by a local chmod, because git does not
   track directory permissions: a chmod in one checkout helps nobody else, and the setup script
   is the only place the fix propagates to a fresh clone.

2. `beads.role not configured (GH#2950)`

   Invisible until (1) stopped. That is the part worth recording: a noisy warning had been
   masking a quieter one for the entire session, and no amount of reading the output more
   carefully would have surfaced it — the fix did.

   DELIBERATELY LEFT UNSET. bd offers `maintainer` or `contributor`, neither is documented in
   `bd help` or anywhere local, and the name suggests it governs who may write. Guessing is a
   claim about authority rather than a configuration tidy-up, and it is exactly the kind of
   guess this repository keeps paying for. Recorded in .beads/README.md so the next person meets
   it as a decision rather than as noise.

RELEVANT TO THIS BEAD because it is the same defect class: bd's output does not distinguish
"this is actionable" from "this is ambient". The export gate was one, these are two more, and
the pattern is that a warning with no severity and no once-per-session throttle gets read as
decoration.
TESTED 2026-08-17 (Claude) — orchestrator/tests/test_beads_export.py, 10 tests over regressions(). The guard had no tests until now; its whole value is in refusing and nobody had watched it refuse. Covers: un-close, disappearing issue, shrinking notes, vanishing comments, all-regressions-reported. Plus the must-not-block cases (forward progress, identical export, empty baseline, missing keys) because a guard that refuses everything gets switched off. Pinned as deliberate: the guard blocks a legitimate human reopen — correct trade, documented so it is not 'fixed' later. Still not covered by a test: that a forced 'bd export -o' returns fresher data than the auto path; that is the bead's own measurement.
close_reason: Complete. The measured mechanism (bd export with no -o goes to stdout; the auto-export is interval-gated, so a write landing inside the gate leaves .beads/issues.jsonl silently stale) is guarded where it bites: commit 839d30f added the beads-export-current pre-commit hook (scripts/beads-export.py --check, wired into just check) which fails a commit whose tracked JSONL lags the store, with just beads-export as the loss-refusing fix, and AGENTS.md states the re-export-before-commit convention. Verified 2026-08-22: the hook is in .pre-commit-config.yaml and runs in just check. Nothing further is actionable in this repo — the underlying UX belongs upstream in bd.

comments.author: ellie
comments.text:
## RETRACTION — my headline claim was FALSE, and sattler was right to push on it

I filed this as "`bd export` with no -o writes a STALE JSONL — the mechanism behind the two
close-reverting incidents". **Both halves of that are wrong.** Correcting it in full rather than
quietly editing, because a confident wrong bug report sends the next person to the wrong layer.

### What is actually true (measured twice, on two different stores)

`bd export` with no `-o` writes to **STDOUT**. It does not touch `.beads/issues.jsonl` at all.

    bd export --help:  "-o, --output string   Output file path (default: stdout)"

    NA store, same file, side by side:
      mtime BEFORE  2026-08-03 03:52:34.593697731   md5 714332b78156
      $ bd export >/dev/null            # no -o
      mtime AFTER   2026-08-03 03:52:34.593697731   md5 714332b78156   <- IDENTICAL

    Clean throwaway store (bd init --prefix zz): default export printed one JSON line to stdout
    and `.beads/issues.jsonl` was never created at all.

So there is no "stale export code path". What happened to me was simpler and entirely my own
error: I ran `bd export`, discarded stdout, then read the pre-existing `.beads/issues.jsonl` and
reported its OLD contents as "the export". `bd export -o <path>` looked like a different, correct
code path only because it is the one that wrote a file at all.

My verify script was right — "the intended change is NOT in the export" — and I misread WHY. It
was not a bad export; it was no export.

### The two prior incidents are NOT this, and their own commit messages say so

sattler's point stands and the evidence is in the history:

  36d67d0 — 14 beads "absent from the live store entirely ... no delete or tombstone event".
            Records missing from the STORE. A correct export faithfully wrote out a store that
            was already wrong. Its repair used the EXPLICIT `-o` form, i.e. my "correct" arm.
  3a0158a — "the export took the store as authoritative and wrote it over a JSONL that was more
            correct than the store", and every affected record "had a store record whose
            updated_at PREDATED its own close_at". Lost writes IN THE STORE.

Both are store-side (the aegis-t15jl family: embedded-store writes not sticking). Mine was a
reading error. **They are not the same defect and I should not have joined them.** I reached for
one mechanism to explain two prior incidents plus my own observation, which is how a tidy story
beats a true one.

### What IS still a real footgun, downgraded to what it is

`bd export` with no `-o` succeeds, prints to stdout, exits 0, and leaves the git-tracked JSONL
untouched. A workflow that runs `bd export` expecting the tracked file to update gets a stale
tracked file and no signal — which is exactly what bit me. That is a UX/docs sharp edge worth a
line in the bd docs or a warning when stdout is not a TTY and a tracked `.beads/issues.jsonl`
exists. It is NOT data corruption and NOT P1.

Re-prioritising this bead to P3 and rewriting the title accordingly.

### One thing I observed and have NOT explained — flagged as UNTESTED, not asserted

At the moment of my close, `.beads/issues.jsonl` (03:43:42.538) and `.beads/export-state.json`
(03:43:42.544) were written 6 ms apart, which looks like one export operation. A later probe
(`bd comment`) did NOT move either file, and config.yaml mentions an auto-backup `interval: 15m`,
so an interval-gated auto-export is a plausible explanation for both the write and for it
carrying pre-close state.

**Plausible is not measured.** I am recording it as an open question rather than a second
mechanism, having just been burned for exactly that move. If an interval-gated auto-export does
capture pre-write state, that WOULD be a genuine stale-write path and belongs upstream — but
someone has to prove it first.

### Upstream

sattler is right that if this reproduces against any store it belongs upstream with this bead as
evidence. The reproducible part does: default-export-to-stdout is bd behaviour, not na behaviour,
and it reproduced on a clean `bd init` store. The na-specific parts (the two prior incidents) do
not — they are store-side and already tracked as aegis-t15jl.

title: just docs check is red repo-wide on MD060 table-column-style
description:
Nineteen files — every doc with a table, plus AGENTS.md, README.md and VISION.md — fail 'just docs check' with MD060 'Table pipe is missing space' for the compact style. The pre-push gate 'just check' passes, because its markdownlint hook and the docs recipe do not run the same rule set; only the docs recipe enforces MD060.

That split is the actual problem. AGENTS.md tells you to run 'just check' before pushing and 'just docs build' if docs changed, so a doc change lands green while 'just docs check' has been red for long enough that nobody can tell which failures are new. A gate that is always red is not a gate.

Two ways out and they need a decision, not a sweep: reformat every table to the compact style and keep MD060, or disable MD060 in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml and stop claiming to enforce it. Whichever, the two configs should agree afterwards.
close_reason: Two fixes, because the red gate and the drift were separate problems. (1) markdownlint-cli2 is now pinned to 0.23.2 in both places — a `markdownlint` variable in the justfile and the matching rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml, each pointing at the other. The cause was an unpinned `npx` in the docs recipe floating to 0.23.2 while pre-commit stayed on 0.17.2, so the two gates linted the same files with the same config and different rule sets. (2) All 388 MD060 violations fixed with --fix across 19 files: table separator rows go |---|---| to | --- | --- |, plus one double-space in an empty header cell. Rendering is unchanged. Both `just check` and `just docs check` are green.

title: Ask upstream Quipu for VALUES support
description: Filed upstream as scbrown/quipu#51 (VALUES) and #52 (FILTER IN). quipu 0.3.11 rejects both -- 'unsupported graph pattern' and 'unsupported FILTER expression'. We build a || disjunction instead, which works but is O(n) in query text and gets unwieldy past a few dozen action-space items. Close this when either lands upstream and we can simplify datalinks/quipu.py build_query().
notes:
Second unsupported feature found, same class as VALUES: Quipu rejects FILTER NOT EXISTS.

  query error: unsupported FILTER expression: Exists(Bgp { ... })

Hit while writing a provenance-completeness check ('which typed nodes lack smac:sourcedFrom'). Worked around client-side, which is fine for a lint run at ingest time but means any negation-shaped question has to leave the store. Worth bundling with the VALUES request upstream - both are about expressing 'not in this set'.
close_reason:
Both landed upstream — quipu #51 (VALUES) and #52 (FILTER IN) shipped in quipu 0.3.13. This bead's own closing condition was 'close this when either lands upstream and we can simplify datalinks/quipu.py build_query()', and that simplification is done (na-01o): the || disjunction is gone, replaced by two VALUES blocks, verified against a real 0.3.23 store by diffing the rows against the old query — identical.

FILTER NOT EXISTS, recorded in this bead's notes as a third instance of the same class, is still unimplemented upstream and is now tracked where it is felt rather than here: docs/knowledge-architecture.md notes that negation-shaped questions have to be computed client-side. Worth a fresh bead if that starts costing something.

title: Parse the remaining alphax.txt sections
description: K1 covers TECHNOLOGY, FACILITIES (incl. secret projects), WEAPONS and DEFENSES. CHASSIS (four name+gender pairs before the numeric fields), UNITS, REACTORS, ABILITIES, TERRAIN, RESOURCEINFO and the SOCIO tables share the file but not the shape, and were skipped rather than half-parsed. Each needs its own row reader plus the smac: classes from knowledge-architecture.md.
notes:
#SOCIO now parsed: 16 social models with effect deltas, emitted as smac:SocialModel with effectText plus structured per-effect predicates. Graph 345 nodes / 3742 facts, provenance 100%. faction.se now has grounding through the same retrieval path as builds - verified live, Free Market resolves to 'economy +2, planet -3, police -5'.

Positional parsing note for whoever touches it: SOCIO is the ONLY section that cannot be read a row at a time. Three header lines, then four groups of four, and a model's category is its group index - nothing in the row names it. Effects are repeated signs, not digits, so -----POLICE is -5.

STILL UNPARSED: #TERRAIN, #RESOURCEINFO, #WORLDBUILDER, #MORALE, #DEFENSEMODES/#OFFENSEMODES, #ORDERS, #CITIZENS, the #SOC* effect-scaling tables, #ENERGY, #TIMECONTROLS.
close_reason:
RESTORED by ellie 2026-08-02 (aegis-uae2s). This bead was closed on 2026-08-02T01:27:57Z and
commit 36d67d0 reverted it to `open`.

Evidence it was a lost write and NOT a deliberate reopen: the durable JSONL carried
status=closed with the full reason below at b99b3ba; the embedded Dolt store's record for this
bead still read `updated_at: 2026-07-30T03:54:25Z` — OLDER than the close itself. 36d67d0
exported that stale store over the good JSONL, so the store's omission became the durable copy.
A record that predates its own close cannot be a reopen of it.

The original close reason follows, unaltered.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Landed as 23cab33. All sections from the bead's NOTES are parsed except #TIMECONTROLS, which was skipped with reasoning rather than silently: it is multiplayer wall-clock budgets - seconds of HUMAN thinking time per turn - so there is no question a brain can ask that it answers.

The payoff is the #SOC* ladders. #SOCIO already emitted 'economy +2', which on its own is a token the model fills in from recollection of a 1999 game. The ladder is the designers' own gloss of that same +2, in the file, at canonical tier. Verified against the real (Thinker-modded) alphax.txt:
  economy +2 -> '+1 energy each square!'
  planet -3  -> 'Wanton ecological disruption; -3 Fungus production'
  economy 99 -> None   (absent rungs return None rather than clamping to the nearest - the ladders are genuinely ragged, 3 to 11 rungs)
Emitted as shared smac:SocialLadderRung nodes, because 11 ladders serve 16 models and inlining would copy each gloss per model and let the copies drift.

One real bug found and fixed on the way, independently confirmed here: slug() drops a leading minus, so slug('economy -3') == slug('economy 3') - two distinct rungs would have silently merged into one IRI. Signs are now encoded (neg3).

Deliberately partial, each documented on the class and asserted by a test rather than left as a surprise:
  - #ORDERS parses 9 movement/sentry rows; every terraform order lives in #TERRAIN, which already has its own reader. Evidence rather than assumption: #TERRAIN rows carry their own key-binding columns, which they would not need if #ORDERS held them.
  - Combat-mode matchups are NOT encoded. 'Projectile weapons receive a bonus against Energy Armor' is prose in a comment; the rows carry display strings and no magnitude. Encoding it would mint a canonical-tier combat rule out of English we read. A test asserts no bonus field exists.

Scope note: #RULES was implemented although it is not in the NOTES list. It shares #WORLDBUILDER's row shape (bare numbers, meaning in an inline comment) so it cost two dispatch lines, and it is more decision-relevant (population limits, prototype costs, combat percentages). Flagged rather than slipped in. Its rows are identified by POSITION, not label - rows 17/18/19 all read 'Psi combat offense-to-defense ratio' on the real file and differ only in a parenthetical.

Row counts parsed from the real file: #RULES 72, #WORLDBUILDER 27, #MORALE 7, #DEFENSEMODES 3, #OFFENSEMODES 3, #ORDERS 9, #CITIZENS 10, #ENERGY 3, #SOC* 90 rungs across 11 ladders. Whole-file graph round-trips through rdflib: 4706 triples, 90 rung nodes, provenance on every subject.

15 tests added. Suite 421 -> 436 passed, 4 skipped. ruff clean; mypy unchanged from main.

title: Bounded deny-repair loop for guard denials
description: knowledge-architecture.md specifies deny-violations returned to the model for bounded repair (max 2 retries, then end_turn). Current behaviour is strip-then-degrade, which is correct but gives up a turn the model could have salvaged.
close_reason:
RESTORED by ellie 2026-08-02 (aegis-uae2s). This bead was closed on 2026-07-31T23:13:29Z and
commit 36d67d0 reverted it to `open`.

Evidence it was a lost write and NOT a deliberate reopen: the durable JSONL carried
status=closed with the full reason below at b99b3ba; the embedded Dolt store's record for this
bead still read `updated_at: 2026-07-29T04:50:47Z` — OLDER than the close itself. 36d67d0
exported that stale store over the good JSONL, so the store's omission became the durable copy.
A record that predates its own close cannot be a reopen of it.

The original close reason follows, unaltered.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Bounded deny-repair loop landed. A decision whose every choice was stripped is re-asked once with the reason in world_view.advisories - a contract field that existed for this and had never been set by anything.

Closed over the na-kdw dependency because that dependency is now stale, not ignored. It assumed the denying guard would be Hank's (K6). StateGuard supplies one locally, so repairs are meaningful today and nothing about the loop changes when Hank's POST /guard replaces it - it consumes Ruling.advisories either way.

Details: NA_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS clamped 0-2, default 1 - below the spec ceiling of 2 because with an agent brain the game BLOCKS for each attempt, so a repair is another round trip while a turn sits still. One record per decision regardless of attempts. adherence_violations accumulates across attempts so a repair cannot hide an invariant break. A BrainError is never repaired: a brain that failed will fail again and asking twice only doubles the delay before the fallback. Verified end to end through the agent surface - a turn that used to degrade is now played by the brain.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

gates on it. That is not me overriding a live blocker — the original close reason above states
the na-kdw dependency was judged stale rather than ignored, so the override reproduces the
author's recorded decision rather than making a new one. The dependency edge itself is left
in place, unchanged.

title: Fog-gate the AI-to-AI diplomacy feed
description: mod_NetMsg_pop sees all foreign treaty changes; a faction should not know about pacts between factions it has never met. Filter on contact before it enters the world view or it is an information cheat. docs/headless-harness.md section 4.2.
close_reason: Gated orchestrator-side in fog.py. redact() drops any delta naming a faction outside the world view's new contacts list, before the brain call -- a redaction applied after the prompt would be theatre, and the test asserts the brain never saw it. Deltas naming no parties are public news and survive; the viewing faction is implicitly contacted. Removals are counted on the decision record (redacted_deltas) and aggregated in coverage, so a leaking adapter shows up as a number rather than as a suspiciously well-informed run. A world view without contacts sets fog_enforced=false rather than reporting clean -- we cannot distinguish a legitimate delta from a leaked one, so absence of evidence is recorded as such. Contract gained contacts; headless-harness.md section 4.2 documents the gate. 10 tests. Adapter-side filtering at mod_NetMsg_pop is still the right first line and belongs with A1.
